title.zh: 卷三十四 列傳第二十二: 游雅 高閭 趙逸 胡叟 胡方回 張湛 段承根 闞駰 劉延明 趙柔 索敞 宋繇 江式
title.en: Volume 34 Biographies 22: You Ya, Gao Lu, Zhao Yi, Hu Sou, Hu Fanggui, Zhang Zhan, Duan Chenggen, Kang Yin, Liu Yanming, Zhao Rou, Sou Chang, Song Yao, Jiang Shi
title.raw: 卷三十四 列傳第二十二: 游雅 高閭 趙逸 胡叟 胡方回 張湛 段承根 闞駰 劉延明 趙柔 索敞 宋繇 江式 Volume 34 Biographies 22: You Ya, Gao Lu, Zhao Yi, Hu Sou, Hu Fanggui, Zhang Zhan, Duan Chenggen, Kang Yin, Liu Yanming, Zhao Rou, Sou Chang, Song Yao, Jiang Shi

sentences.zh: 游雅 高閭 趙逸 胡叟 胡方回 張湛 段承根 闞駰 劉延明 趙柔 索敞 宋繇 江式

translations.literal: You Ya, Gao Lu, Zhao Yi, Hu Sou, Hu Fanghui, Zhang Zhan, Duan Chenggen, Kang Yin, Liu Yanming, Zhao Rou, Sou Chang, Song Yao, Jiang Shi
translations.idiomatic: You Ya, Gao Lu, Zhao Yi, Hu Sou, Hu Fanghui, Zhang Zhan, Duan Chenggen, Kang Yin, Liu Yanming, Zhao Rou, Sou Chang, Song Yao, and Jiang Shi

sentences.zh: 列傳第二十二

translations.literal: Biographies 22
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 22

sentences.zh: 游雅從祖弟明根高閭趙逸兄子琰胡叟胡方回張湛段承根宗欽闞駰劉延明趙柔索敞宋繇孫游道江式

translations.literal: You Ya's younger cousin by five degrees Minggen, Gao Lu, Zhao Yi's nephew Yan, Hu Sou, Hu Fanghui, Zhang Zhan, Duan Chenggen's clansman Zongqin, Kang Yin, Liu Yanming, Zhao Rou, Sou Chang, Song Yao's grandson Youdao, Jiang Shi
translations.idiomatic: Minggen, You Ya's fifth-generation cousin; Gao Lu; Yan, nephew of Zhao Yi; Hu Sou; Hu Fanghui; Zhang Zhan; Zongqin of Duan Chenggen's clan; Kang Yin; Liu Yanming; Zhao Rou; Sou Chang; Youdao, grandson of Song Yao; and Jiang Shi

sentences.zh: 游雅，字伯度，小名黃頭，廣平任人也。

translations.literal: You Ya, styled Bodu, with the childhood name Huangtou, was a native of Ren in Guangping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: You Ya, whose style name was Bodu and whose childhood name was Huangtou, came from Ren in Guangping commandery.

sentences.zh: 太武時，與勃海高允等俱知名，徵拜中書博士。

translations.literal: During Emperor Taiwu's time, he was renowned together with Gao Yun of Bohai and others, and was summoned and appointed Erudite of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Taiwu he won fame alongside Gao Yun of Bohai and others, and was summoned to serve as Erudite of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 後使宋，授散騎侍郎，賜爵廣平子。

translations.literal: Later he was sent as envoy to Song, appointed Gentleman of the Palace Cadet, and granted the title Viscount of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: He was later dispatched as envoy to the Liu Song court, appointed Gentleman of the Palace Cadet, and ennobled as Viscount of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 稍遷太子少傅，領禁兵，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, commanded the forbidden troops, and advanced in rank to Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, took charge of the palace guard, and was advanced to marquis.

sentences.zh: 受詔與中書侍郎胡方回等改定律制。

translations.literal: He received an imperial order to revise laws and regulations together with Secretariat Attendant Hu Fanghui and others.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial command he joined Secretariat Attendant Hu Fanghui and others in revising the legal code.

sentences.zh: 出為東雍州刺史，假梁郡公。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as Governor of Eastern Yong province, with the provisional title Duke of Liang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Governor of Eastern Yong province and given the provisional title Duke of Liang.

sentences.zh: 在任廉白，甚有惠政。

translations.literal: In office he was incorruptible and had excellent benevolent policies.
translations.idiomatic: In his post he was scrupulously honest and governed with notable kindness.

sentences.zh: 徵為秘書監，委以國史之任，竟無所成。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Director of the Secretariat, entrusted with the duty of national history, but in the end accomplished nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to serve as Director of the Secretariat and charged with compiling the national history, he ultimately produced nothing.

sentences.zh: 雅性剛戇，好自矜誕，淩獵人物。

translations.literal: Ya by nature was stubborn and blunt, fond of boasting about himself, and preyed upon others.
translations.idiomatic: Ya was by nature obstinate and overbearing, given to self-aggrandizement, and ruthless toward those around him.

sentences.zh: 高允重雅文學，而雅輕允才，允性柔寬，不以為恨。

translations.literal: Gao Yun valued Ya's literary learning, but Ya looked down on Yun's talent; Yun was gentle and broad-minded and did not resent it.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yun held Ya's scholarship in high regard, yet Ya belittled Yun's abilities; Yun, mild and magnanimous by nature, bore no grudge.

sentences.zh: 允將婚于邢氏，雅勸允娶其族，允不從。

translations.literal: When Yun was about to marry into the Xing clan, Ya urged Yun to marry into his own clan; Yun did not follow his advice.
translations.idiomatic: When Yun was preparing to marry into the Xing clan, Ya pressed him to take a wife from the You family instead, but Yun refused.

sentences.zh: 雅曰：「人貴河間邢，不勝廣平遊；

translations.literal: Ya said: "People esteem the Xing of Hejian and cannot match the You of Guangping;
translations.idiomatic: Ya said, "Men may honor the Xing of Hejian, but they cannot outrank the You of Guangping;

sentences.zh: 人自棄伯度，我自敬黃頭。

translations.literal: others may abandon Bodu, but I myself honor Huangtou."
translations.idiomatic: others may spurn Bodu, but I still revere Huangtou."

sentences.zh: 」其貴己賤人，皆此類也。

translations.literal: His esteeming himself and slighting others were all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His habit of exalting himself while demeaning others was entirely in this vein.

sentences.zh: 允著《征士頌》，殊重雅。

translations.literal: Yun wrote the "Ode to Reclusive Scholars," which greatly valued Ya.
translations.idiomatic: Yun composed the "Ode to Reclusive Scholars," in which he singled out Ya for special praise.

sentences.zh: 雅因議論長短，忿儒者陳奇，遂陷奇至族。

translations.literal: Because of a discussion comparing merits and faults, Ya bore resentment against the Confucian Chen Qi and brought Qi to execution extending to his clan.
translations.idiomatic: During a debate over comparative merits, Ya took offense at the scholar Chen Qi and had him condemned in a case that wiped out his entire clan.

sentences.zh: 議者深責之。

translations.literal: Critics deeply blamed him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators condemned him harshly for it.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈相州刺史，諡曰宣侯。

translations.literal: When he died, he was posthumously made Governor of Xiang province, with the posthumous title Marquis Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously appointed Governor of Xiang province and given the posthumous title Marquis Xuan.

sentences.zh: 明根字志遠，雅從祖弟也。

translations.literal: Minggen, styled Zhiyuan, was Ya's younger cousin by five degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Minggen, whose style name was Zhiyuan, was You Ya's fifth-generation cousin.

sentences.zh: 祖鱓，慕容熙樂浪太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shan served as Administrator of Lelang under Murong Xi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shan had been Administrator of Lelang under Murong Xi.

sentences.zh: 父幼，馮跋假廣平太守。

translations.literal: His father You was provisionally made Administrator of Guangping by Feng Ba.
translations.idiomatic: His father You held the provisional post of Administrator of Guangping under Feng Ba.

sentences.zh: 明根幼年遭亂，為櫟陽王氏奴。

translations.literal: In his youth Minggen suffered the disorders and became a slave of the Wang family of Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Minggen was caught up in the chaos of his youth and ended up a bondservant in the household of the Wangs of Liyang.

sentences.zh: 主使牧羊，明根以漿壺倩人書字路邊，書地學之。

translations.literal: His master had him herd sheep; Minggen used a broth pot to borrow someone's brush to write characters by the roadside, and learned by writing on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: His master set him to tend sheep; Minggen would trade his broth jar for someone to write characters along the road, then copy them on the ground to teach himself.

sentences.zh: 長安鎮將竇瑾見之，呼問，知其姓名，乃告遊雅。

translations.literal: The garrison commander Dou Jin of Chang'an saw him, called him over to ask, learned his name, and told You Ya.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jin, the garrison commander at Chang'an, noticed him, summoned him for questioning, learned who he was, and reported the matter to You Ya.

sentences.zh: 雅使人贖之，教書。

translations.literal: Ya sent someone to redeem him and had him taught to read.
translations.idiomatic: Ya sent men to ransom him and put him to his studies.

sentences.zh: 年十六，辭雅歸鄉里，于白渠坎為窟，讀書積歲。

translations.literal: At sixteen he left Ya and returned to his home district, making a cave dwelling at the Baiqu canal bank where he read books for years.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he took leave of Ya and went home, excavating a cave beside the Baiqu canal where he buried himself in books for years on end.

sentences.zh: 雅稱薦之，太武擢為中書學生。

translations.literal: Ya praised and recommended him; Emperor Taiwu promoted him to a student of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Ya spoke highly of him and recommended him; Emperor Taiwu selected him as a student of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 性寡欲，綜習經史。

translations.literal: By nature he had few desires and studied comprehensively the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: He was abstemious by temperament and had mastered the full range of classical and historical texts.

sentences.zh: 文成踐阼，為都曹主書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wencheng ascended the throne, he became Chief Clerk of the Capital Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wencheng took the throne, he was appointed Chief Clerk of the Capital Bureau.

sentences.zh: 帝以其敬慎，每嗟美之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because of his respectfulness and caution, often sighed in admiration of him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, struck by his dutiful care, often praised him with audible admiration.

sentences.zh: 假員外散騎常侍、安樂侯，使宋。

translations.literal: He was provisionally made Acting Regular Attendant of the Palace Cadet and Marquis of Anle, and sent as envoy to Song.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the provisional posts of Acting Regular Attendant of the Palace Cadet and Marquis of Anle and dispatched as envoy to the Song court.

sentences.zh: 宋孝武稱其長者，迎送禮加常使。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu of Song called him an elder of stature, and the ceremonies of reception and send-off exceeded those for ordinary envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu of Song hailed him as a man of mature dignity, and the courtesies of his reception and farewell surpassed those accorded ordinary envoys.

sentences.zh: 獻文時，累遷東兗州刺史，封新泰侯，為政清平。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xianwen's time he was repeatedly promoted to Governor of Eastern Yan province, enfeoffed as Marquis of Xintai, and his administration was clear and fair.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xianwen he rose through successive appointments to Governor of Eastern Yan, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xintai, and governed with clarity and fairness.

sentences.zh: 孝文時為儀曹長，清約恭謹，號為稱職。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xiaowen's time he was Director of the Ceremonies Bureau, frugal and respectfully cautious, and was known as fulfilling his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowen he headed the Ceremonies Bureau, living frugally and conducting himself with scrupulous deference, and was regarded as thoroughly competent.

sentences.zh: 曆儀曹尚書，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He served successively as Minister of Ceremonies and was made Regular Attendant of the Palace Cadet.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to serve as Minister of Ceremonies and was additionally appointed Regular Attendant of the Palace Cadet.

sentences.zh: 遷大鴻臚卿、河南王幹師，尚書如故，隨例降侯為伯。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Grand Minister of Splendor and tutor to Prince Gan of Henan, retaining his ministerial post; following precedent his marquisate was reduced to a barony.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Minister of Splendor and appointed tutor to Prince Gan of Henan while keeping his ministerial title; in accordance with precedent his marquisate was lowered to a barony.

sentences.zh: 又參定律令，屢進讜言。

translations.literal: He also participated in compiling laws and statutes, repeatedly offering loyal remonstrances.
translations.idiomatic: He also took part in drafting laws and statutes and submitted forthright counsel on many occasions.

sentences.zh: 明根以年逾七十，表求致仕，優詔許之。

translations.literal: Minggen, being over seventy, submitted a memorial requesting retirement; an excellent edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: When Minggen passed seventy, he memorialized the throne requesting retirement, and a gracious edict approved his request.

sentences.zh: 引入陳謝，悲不自勝。

translations.literal: He was brought in to offer farewell thanks and could not restrain his grief.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned for a farewell audience and was overcome with sorrow.

sentences.zh: 帝言別殷勤，仍為流涕，賜青紗單衣、委貌冠、被褥、錦袍等物。

translations.literal: The emperor spoke parting words with great warmth and wept again, bestowing a green gauze unlined coat, a cap of ceremony, bedding, a brocade robe, and other items.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor addressed him with affectionate parting words, wept again himself, and granted him a green gauze coat, a ceremonial cap, bedding, a brocade robe, and other gifts.

sentences.zh: 其年，以司徒尉元為三老，明根為五更，行禮辟雍，賜步挽一乘，給上卿祿，供食之味，太官就第月送。

translations.literal: That year, with Minister of Works Yuan Xuan of the Secretariat as the Elder, Minggen as the Quintus, they performed rites at the Imperial Academy; he was granted a hand-pulled carriage, senior minister salary, food of the finest flavors, and the Imperial Kitchen sent monthly to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Yuan Xuan, Minister of Works, was appointed Elder and Minggen Quintus for the rites at the Imperial Academy; he received a hand-drawn carriage, a senior minister's stipend, delicacies for his table, and monthly deliveries from the Imperial Kitchen to his home.

sentences.zh: 以定律令。

translations.literal: He was appointed to compile laws and statutes.
translations.idiomatic: He was charged with revising the laws and statutes.

sentences.zh: 賜布帛等。

translations.literal: He was granted cloth and silk and the like.
translations.idiomatic: He received gifts of cloth, silk, and other goods.

sentences.zh: 歸本郡，又賜安車、兩馬、幄帳、被褥。

translations.literal: When he returned to his home commandery, he was again granted a comfort carriage, two horses, a canopy tent, and bedding.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to his native commandery he was further given a comfort carriage, two horses, a curtained pavilion, and bedding.

sentences.zh: 車駕幸鄴，明根朝於行宮，優詔賜以穀帛，敕太官備送珍羞，為造甲第。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage visited Ye, Minggen attended audience at the traveling palace; an excellent edict granted him grain and cloth, ordered the Imperial Kitchen to prepare and send delicacies, and had a fine mansion built for him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor traveled to Ye, Minggen presented himself at the temporary palace; a gracious edict bestowed grain and cloth, the Imperial Kitchen was ordered to supply delicacies, and a grand residence was built for him.

sentences.zh: 國有大事，恆璽書訪之。

translations.literal: When the state had great affairs, the emperor invariably sent sealed letters to consult him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever weighty matters arose for the state, the throne unfailingly sought his counsel by sealed edict.

sentences.zh: 舊疾發動，手詔問疾，太醫送藥。

translations.literal: When his old illness flared up, the emperor personally wrote to inquire after his health, and the imperial physicians sent medicine.
translations.idiomatic: When his chronic ailment returned, the emperor wrote in his own hand to ask after him, and the court physicians sent medicines.

sentences.zh: 卒于家，宣武弔祭贈賵甚厚，贈光祿大夫，金章紫綬，諡靖侯。

translations.literal: He died at home; Emperor Xuanwu mourned and sacrificed with very generous funeral gifts, posthumously appointing him Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with golden seal and purple cord, posthumous title Marquis Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home; Emperor Xuanwu sent condolences and lavish funeral gifts, posthumously raising him to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with golden seal and purple cord and the posthumous title Marquis Jing.

sentences.zh: 明根曆官內外五十餘年，處身以仁和，接物以禮讓，時論貴之。

translations.literal: Minggen held office at court and in the provinces for more than fifty years, conducting himself with benevolence and harmony and treating others with ritual courtesy; contemporary opinion prized him.
translations.idiomatic: Minggen served at court and in the provinces for more than fifty years, living with benevolence and treating others with courteous restraint; men of his day held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 孝文初，明根與高閭以儒老學業，特被禮遇，公私出入，每相追隨；

translations.literal: Early in Emperor Xiaowen's reign, Minggen and Gao Lu, as elderly Confucian scholars, received special courtesy; in public and private they went in and out, always following one another;
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaowen's reign, Minggen and Gao Lu, revered as venerable Confucian scholars, enjoyed exceptional favor; whether at court or abroad they were seldom apart;

sentences.zh: 而閭以才筆，時侮明根。

translations.literal: yet Lu, relying on his literary talent, often insulted Minggen.
translations.idiomatic: yet Lu, confident in his literary gifts, would often slight Minggen.

sentences.zh: 世號高、遊焉。

translations.literal: The age called them Gao and You.
translations.idiomatic: Their generation paired them as "Gao and You."

sentences.zh: 子肇襲，字伯始，孝文賜名焉。

translations.literal: His son Zhao inherited the title, styled Boshi; Emperor Xiaowen bestowed this name upon him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhao succeeded him, with the style name Boshi, a name granted by Emperor Xiaowen.

sentences.zh: 博綜經史。

translations.literal: He mastered comprehensively the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: He had a comprehensive command of the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 孝文初，為內秘書侍御中散，稍遷典命中大夫。

translations.literal: Early in Emperor Xiaowen's reign he was Attendant and Regular Palace Cadet of the Inner Secretariat, and was gradually promoted to Grand Master of Palace Writings.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaowen's reign he served as Attendant and Regular Palace Cadet of the Inner Secretariat, and was later promoted to Grand Master of Palace Writings.

sentences.zh: 車駕南伐，肇表諫，不納。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned south, Zhao submitted a memorial of remonstrance, but it was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor marched south on campaign, Zhao memorialized in protest, but his advice went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 尋遷太子中庶子。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 肇謙素敦重，文雅見任。

translations.literal: Zhao was modest, plain, and earnest in character, and was trusted for his literary refinement.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was modest, sober, and grave in bearing, and won trust through his cultivated learning.

sentences.zh: 以父老，求解官扶侍。

translations.literal: Because his father was elderly, he requested to leave office to support and attend him.
translations.idiomatic: When his father grew old, he asked to resign his post so he could care for him at home.

sentences.zh: 孝文欲令祿養，出為本州南安王楨鎮北府長史，帶魏郡太守。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen wished him to be supported by salary; he went out as Chief Clerk of the Northern Garrison Headquarters of Prince Zhen of Nan'an in his home province, concurrently serving as Administrator of Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen arranged for him to draw a stipend while serving near home as Chief Clerk on the staff of Prince Zhen of Nan'an's northern headquarters, with concurrent appointment as Administrator of Wei commandery.

sentences.zh: 王薨，復為高陽王雍鎮北府長史，太守如故。

translations.literal: When the prince died, he again became Chief Clerk of the Northern Garrison Headquarters of Prince Yong of Gaoyang, retaining his post as Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: After that prince's death he took the same post on Prince Yong of Gaoyang's northern staff, still holding the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 為政清簡，加以匡贊，曆佐二王，甚有聲績。

translations.literal: His administration was clear and simple, and he moreover offered loyal counsel; serving two princes in succession, he achieved considerable renown.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with clarity and restraint while offering steadfast counsel; assisting two princes in turn, he built a strong reputation.

sentences.zh: 以父憂解任。

translations.literal: He left office on account of his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned when his father died.

sentences.zh: 復授黃門侍郎，兼侍中，為畿內大使，黜陟善惡，賞罰分明。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and concurrently Attendant-in-Ordinary, serving as envoy within the capital region, promoting and demoting according to merit and fault with clear rewards and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was reappointed Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and Attendant-in-Ordinary, and as metropolitan inspector he promoted the worthy and removed the unfit, distinguishing rewards from punishments with unmistakable clarity.

sentences.zh: 曆太府、廷尉卿，兼御史中尉，黃門如故。

translations.literal: He served successively as Minister of the Imperial Treasury and Minister of Justice, concurrently as Chief Commandant of Censors, retaining his Yellow Gate post.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to head the Imperial Treasury and the Ministry of Justice, while also serving as Chief Commandant of Censors and keeping his Yellow Gate title.

sentences.zh: 肇儒者，動存名教，直繩所舉，莫非傷風敗俗。

translations.literal: As a Confucian, Zhao always upheld the teachings of propriety; every case he prosecuted with the straight cord concerned offenses against custom and morality.
translations.idiomatic: A Confucian in spirit, he upheld the moral order in every action; every case he brought forward as censor involved conduct that offended public decency.

sentences.zh: 持法仁平，斷獄務於矜恕。

translations.literal: He upheld the law with benevolence and fairness, and in judging cases strove for compassionate forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: He applied the law with humane evenhandedness and judged cases with an eye to mercy.

sentences.zh: 尚書令高肇，宣武之舅，百僚懾憚，以肇名與己同，欲令改易。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Gao Zhao, maternal uncle of Emperor Xuanwu, was feared by all officials; because Zhao's name was the same as his own, he wished to have it changed.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Gao Zhao, the emperor's uncle on his mother's side, inspired fear throughout the bureaucracy; finding that Zhao bore the same personal name, he wanted him to change it.

sentences.zh: 肇以孝文所賜，執志不許，高肇甚銜之，宣武嘉其剛梗。

translations.literal: Zhao, because it had been bestowed by Emperor Xiaowen, held firmly to his resolve and would not agree; Gao Zhao deeply resented this, but Emperor Xuanwu praised his stubborn integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao refused, insisting that the name had been granted by Emperor Xiaowen; Gao Zhao bore a deep grudge, but Emperor Xuanwu admired his unyielding integrity.

sentences.zh: 肇外寬柔，內剛直，耽好經傳，手不釋書。

translations.literal: Outwardly Zhao was gentle and yielding, inwardly firm and upright; he was devoted to the classics and commentaries and never put his books down.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly mild, inwardly unbending, he was devoted to the classics and never let a book leave his hand.

sentences.zh: 善《周易》、《毛詩》，尤精《三禮》。

translations.literal: He was skilled in the "Book of Changes" and the "Mao Version of the Odes," and especially expert in the "Three Rites."
translations.idiomatic: He excelled in the Book of Changes and the Mao recension of the Odes, and was especially masterful in the Three Rites.

sentences.zh: 為《易集解》，撰《冠婚儀》、《白圭論》，詩賦表啟凡七十五篇。

translations.literal: He compiled "Collected Explanations of the Changes," wrote "Rites of Capping and Marriage" and "Discourse on the White Jade," and composed in all seventy-five pieces of poetry, rhapsodies, memorials, and reports.
translations.idiomatic: He produced Collected Explanations of the Changes, authored Rites of Capping and Marriage and Discourse on the White Jade, and wrote seventy-five works in all, including verse, fu, memorials, and reports.

sentences.zh: 謙廉不競，曾撰《儒棋》，以表其志。

translations.literal: He was modest, incorruptible, and uncontentious; he once composed "Confucian Chess" to express his aims.
translations.idiomatic: Humble, upright, and free of rivalry, he once wrote Confucian Chess to declare his principles.

sentences.zh: 清貧寡欲，資仰俸祿而已。

translations.literal: He was poor and pure with few desires, relying on his salary alone.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in clean poverty with few wants, subsisting on his official stipend alone.

sentences.zh: 為廷尉時，宣武嘗敕肇有所降恕，執而不從，曰：「陛下自能恕之，豈可令臣曲筆也。

translations.literal: When he was Minister of Justice, Emperor Xuanwu once ordered Zhao to show leniency in certain cases; he held firm and would not obey, saying: "Your Majesty can yourself show mercy—how could you have me bend the brush?"
translations.idiomatic: As Minister of Justice, he once received an order from Emperor Xuanwu to extend clemency in certain cases; he stood firm and refused, saying, "Your Majesty may pardon whom you will—how can you ask me to distort the record?"

sentences.zh: 」其執意如此。

translations.literal: His firmness of purpose was of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the steadfastness of his convictions.

sentences.zh: 及明帝初，近侍群官預在奉迎者，自侍中崔光以下並加封，封肇文安縣侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming first ascended, the group of close attendants who had taken part in welcoming him, from Attendant-in-Ordinary Cui Guang downward, all received enfeoffments; Zhao was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wen'an county.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign, every close attendant who had helped receive him at his accession, from Cui Guang the Attendant-in-Ordinary on down, was ennobled; Zhao was made Marquis of Wen'an.

sentences.zh: 肇獨曰：「子襲父位，今古之常，因此獲封，何以自處？

translations.literal: Zhao alone said: "A son inherits his father's position—this is the constant practice of past and present; to receive enfeoffment for that reason—how could one comport oneself?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhao alone protested, "A son succeeds his father's place—that is the way of every age. To be ennobled for that alone—how could one face the world?"

sentences.zh: 」固辭不應。

translations.literal: He firmly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He steadfastly refused the honor.

sentences.zh: 論者高之。

translations.literal: Commentators held him in high esteem for this.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary opinion ranked him the higher for it.

sentences.zh: 子祥，字宗良，頗有才學。

translations.literal: His son Xiang, styled Zongliang, had considerable literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiang, whose style name was Zongliang, was a man of real learning.

sentences.zh: 襲爵新泰伯，位國子博士，領尚書郎中。

translations.literal: He inherited the title Baron of Xintai, held the post of Erudite of the Imperial University, and concurrently served as Bureau Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited his father's barony of Xintai, served as Erudite of the Imperial University, and concurrently headed a bureau in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 明帝以肇昔辭文安之封，復欲封祥，祥守其父志，卒不受。

translations.literal: Because Zhao had once declined the enfeoffment of Wen'an, Emperor Ming wished again to enfeoff Xiang; Xiang upheld his father's resolve and in the end did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Remembering that Zhao had once refused Wen'an, Emperor Ming sought to ennoble Xiang instead; Xiang held to his father's principles and ultimately declined.

sentences.zh: 又追論肇前議清河，守正不屈，乃封祥高邑縣侯。

translations.literal: The court also reviewed Zhao's earlier remonstrance concerning Qinghe, in which he had upheld righteousness without yielding, and therefore enfeoffed Xiang as Marquis of Gaoyi county.
translations.idiomatic: The court then recalled Zhao's earlier stand on the Qinghe affair, when he had upheld principle without bending, and enfeoffed Xiang as Marquis of Gaoyi.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈給事黃門侍郎、幽州刺史，諡曰文。

translations.literal: When he died, he was posthumously made Supervisor of Attendants of the Yellow Gate and Governor of You province, with the posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously appointed Supervisor of Attendants of the Yellow Gate and Governor of You province, with the posthumous epithet Wen.

sentences.zh: 高閭，字閻士，漁陽雍奴人也。

translations.literal: Gao Lu, styled Yanshi, was a native of Yongnu in Yuyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lu, whose style name was Yanshi, came from Yongnu in Yuyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 五世祖原，晉安北將軍、上谷太守、關中侯，有碑在薊中。

translations.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor Yuan was Jin General Who Pacifies the North, Administrator of Shanggu, and Marquis Within the Passes; a stele to him stands in Ji.
translations.idiomatic: His fifth-generation ancestor Yuan had been a Jin general titled Pacifier of the North, Administrator of Shanggu, and Marquis Within the Passes; a memorial stele to him still stood in Ji.

sentences.zh: 祖雅，少有令名，位州別駕。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ya had a fine reputation in youth and held the post of Provincial Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ya won an excellent name while young and rose to Provincial Attendant.

sentences.zh: 父洪，字季願，位陳留王從事中郎。

translations.literal: His father Hong, styled Jiyuan, held the post of Attendant of the Prince of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hong, styled Jiyuan, served as Attendant on the staff of the Prince of Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 閭貴，乃贈幽州刺史、固安貞子。

translations.literal: When Lu rose to prominence, Hong was posthumously made Governor of You province and Viscount Zhen of Gu'an.
translations.idiomatic: After Lu achieved distinction, his father was posthumously honored as Governor of You and Viscount Zhen of Gu'an.

sentences.zh: 閭早孤，少好學，博綜經史，下筆成章。

translations.literal: Lu was orphaned early, loved learning in youth, mastered comprehensively the classics and histories, and composed finished essays as soon as he took up the brush.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, Lu took eagerly to study in his boyhood, mastered the classics and histories, and wrote polished prose at a stroke.

sentences.zh: 少為車子，送租至平城，修剌詣崔浩。

translations.literal: In youth he was a cart-hand, delivering rent grain to Pingcheng; he composed a visiting card and presented himself to Cui Hao.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he drove carts, hauling rent grain to Pingcheng; he drafted a visiting card and called on Cui Hao.

sentences.zh: 浩與語奇之，使為謝中書監表。

translations.literal: Hao conversed with him and found him remarkable, and had him compose a letter of thanks to the Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Hao spoke with him, was struck by his ability, and had him draft a letter of thanks to the Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 明日，浩曆租車過，駐馬呼閭，諸車子皆驚。

translations.literal: The next day Hao passed along the line of rent carts, reined in his horse and called to Lu; all the cart-hands were astonished.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, as Hao passed the rent carts, he reined in and called out to Lu; every cart-hand was astonished.

sentences.zh: 閭本名驢，浩乃改為閭，而字焉，由是知名。

translations.literal: Lu's original name had been Donkey; Hao changed it to Lu and gave him a style name, and from this he became known.
translations.idiomatic: Lu had originally been named Donkey; Hao changed his name to Lu and gave him a style name, and from that moment he became known.

sentences.zh: 和平末，為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: At the end of the Heping era he became Secretariat Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Near the close of the Heping era he was appointed Secretariat Attendant.

sentences.zh: 文成崩，乙渾擅權，內外危懼，文明太后臨朝誅渾，引閭與中書令高允入禁中參決大政，賜爵安樂子。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wencheng died, Yichun Hun seized power and inner and outer court were filled with fear; Empress Dowager Wenming held court and executed Hun, summoning Lu and Chief Minister of the Secretariat Gao Yun into the inner palace to deliberate on great affairs of state, and granting Lu the title Viscount of Anle.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wencheng's death, Yichun Hun seized power and the court was gripped by fear; Empress Dowager Wenming took the reins, executed Hun, and brought Lu and Chief Minister Gao Yun into the inner palace to decide major policy, ennobling Lu as Viscount of Anle.

sentences.zh: 與鎮南大將軍尉元南赴徐州，以功進爵為侯。

translations.literal: Together with General Who Guards the South Yuan Xuan he marched south to Xuzhou, and for his merit was advanced in rank to Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied General Who Guards the South Yuan Xuan on the southern campaign to Xuzhou and, for his service, was promoted to marquis.

sentences.zh: 獻文即位，徙崇光宮，閭表上《至德頌》。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianwen ascended the throne, the court moved to Chongguang Palace; Lu submitted a memorial presenting the "Ode to Supreme Virtue."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianwen took the throne and the court relocated to Chongguang Palace, Lu memorialized the throne with his "Ode to Supreme Virtue."

sentences.zh: 高允以閭文章富逸，舉以自代，遂為獻文所知，參論政事。

translations.literal: Gao Yun, because Lu's writings were rich and elegant, recommended him to succeed himself; Lu thus came to Xianwen's notice and took part in deliberating on state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yun, impressed by the richness and grace of Lu's prose, proposed him as his successor; Lu thereby won Emperor Xianwen's attention and joined in deliberations on state policy.

sentences.zh: 永明初，為中書令、給事中，委以機密。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yongming era he became Chief Minister of the Secretariat and Palace Attendant, entrusted with confidential matters.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongming era he was appointed Chief Minister of the Secretariat and Palace Attendant, with charge of confidential affairs.

sentences.zh: 文明太后甚重閭，詔令書檄碑銘讚頌皆其文也。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming greatly valued Lu; imperial edicts, letters, proclamations, stele inscriptions, eulogies, and hymns were all his compositions.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming held Lu in high esteem; edicts, dispatches, stele texts, eulogies, and hymns issued under her name were largely his work.

sentences.zh: 太和三年，出師討淮北，閭表諫，陳四疑，請時速返旆。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taihe, when the army marched out to campaign against north of the Huai, Lu submitted a memorial of remonstrance, setting forth four doubts and asking that the banners be swiftly turned back.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taihe, as troops marched to subdue the region north of the Huai, Lu memorialized in protest, laying out four grounds for doubt and urging an immediate withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 文明太后曰：「六軍電發，有若摧朽，何慮四難也。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming said: "The six armies strike like lightning, as if shattering rotten wood—why worry over four difficulties?"
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming replied, "The six armies move like lightning, crushing all before them like rotten timber—what need to fret over four difficulties?"

sentences.zh: 」遷尚書、中書監。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Minister of the Secretariat and Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of the Secretariat and Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 淮南王他奏求依舊斷祿，閭表以為若不班祿，則貪者肆其姦情，清者不能自保，詔從閭議。

translations.literal: Prince Ta of Huainan memorialized requesting that salaries be cut off as in old times; Lu submitted a memorial holding that if salaries were not distributed, the greedy would indulge their wicked desires and the upright could not protect themselves; an edict followed Lu's opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ta of Huainan asked that official stipends be suspended as in earlier times; Lu argued that without regular distribution of salaries the corrupt would run unchecked and honest men could not survive; the throne adopted Lu's view.

sentences.zh: 孝文又引見王公以下于皇信堂，令辯忠佞。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen again summoned the princes, dukes, and officials down to the lower ranks to the Hall of Imperial Trust and ordered them to debate loyalty and flattery.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen again assembled the princes, nobles, and officials in the Hall of Imperial Trust and set them to debate the difference between loyalty and sycophancy.

sentences.zh: 閭曰：「佞者飾知以行事，忠者發心以附道，譬如玉石，皦然可知。

translations.literal: Lu said: "The flatterer adorns knowledge to carry out affairs; the loyal man sets forth his heart to attach himself to the Way—as with jade and stone, the distinction is plainly visible."
translations.idiomatic: Lu said, "The sycophant dresses up knowledge to get his way; the loyal man gives his heart to the Way. The difference is as clear as that between jade and common stone."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「玉石同體而異名，忠佞異名而同理。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Jade and stone share the same substance but bear different names; loyalty and flattery bear different names but share the same principle.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Jade and stone are the same in substance yet differ in name; loyalty and sycophancy differ in name yet rest on the same underlying pattern.

sentences.zh: 求之於同，則得其所以異；

translations.literal: Seek in what is the same, and you obtain the reason for what differs;
translations.idiomatic: Seek what they share in common, and you grasp why they differ;

sentences.zh: 尋之於異，則失其所以同。

translations.literal: search in what differs, and you lose what is the same.
translations.idiomatic: pursue only what sets them apart, and you lose sight of what unites them.

sentences.zh: 出處同異之間，交換忠佞之境，豈是皦然易明哉？

translations.literal: Between emerging and withdrawing, sameness and difference, the borderland where loyalty and flattery exchange places—how could this be plainly easy to discern?"
translations.idiomatic: Between advance and retreat, likeness and difference, the shifting ground where loyalty and sycophancy trade places—how could any distinction be obvious at a glance?"

sentences.zh: 或有托佞以成忠，或有假忠以飾佞，如楚之子綦，後事雖忠，初非佞也？

translations.literal: Some rely on flattery to achieve loyalty, some borrow loyalty to adorn flattery—as with Ziqi of Chu, whose later conduct was loyal though at first he was not flattery?"
translations.idiomatic: Some use sycophancy to accomplish loyalty; some borrow loyalty to mask sycophancy. Take Ziqi of Chu: though loyal in the end, was he not sycophantic at the outset?"

sentences.zh: 」閭曰：「子綦諫楚，初雖隨述，終致忠言，此適欲幾諫，非為佞也。

translations.literal: Lu said: "Ziqi remonstrated with Chu; at first he followed along in narration, but in the end brought forth loyal words—this was simply intending indirect remonstrance, not flattery.
translations.idiomatic: Lu replied, "When Ziqi remonstrated with the king of Chu, he began by echoing the king's own words yet ended in frank counsel. That was indirect remonstrance, not sycophancy.

sentences.zh: 子綦若不設初權，後忠無由得顯。

translations.literal: If Ziqi had not set up his initial expedient, the later loyalty would have had no means to appear."
translations.idiomatic: Without that initial stratagem, his later loyalty could never have come to light."

sentences.zh: 」帝善閭對。

translations.literal: The emperor approved Lu's reply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased with Lu's answer.

sentences.zh: 後上表曰：

translations.literal: Later he submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He later submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 臣聞為國之道，其要有五：一曰文德，二曰武功，三曰法度，四曰防固，五曰刑賞。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that the Way of governing a state has five essentials: first, civil virtue; second, martial achievement; third, laws and standards; fourth, defense and fortification; fifth, punishments and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that governing a state rests on five essentials: civil virtue, martial prowess, law and regulation, frontier defense, and the balance of punishment and reward.

sentences.zh: 故遠人不服，則修文德以來之；

translations.literal: Thus when distant peoples do not submit, cultivate civil virtue to draw them in;
translations.idiomatic: When distant peoples refuse submission, cultivate civil virtue to win them over;

sentences.zh: 荒狡放命，則播武功以威之；

translations.literal: when wild and cunning men defy orders, deploy martial achievement to awe them;
translations.idiomatic: when savage and defiant enemies run riot, display martial might to overawe them;

sentences.zh: 人未知戰，則制法度以齊之；

translations.literal: when men do not yet know warfare, establish laws and standards to bring them into order;
translations.idiomatic: when the people are untrained for war, establish laws and standards to discipline them;

sentences.zh: 暴敵輕侵，則設防固以禦之；

translations.literal: when violent enemies lightly invade, set up defenses and fortifications to repel them;
translations.idiomatic: when violent foes raid with impunity, build defenses to hold them off;

sentences.zh: 臨事制勝，則明賞罰以勸之。

translations.literal: when facing affairs and securing victory, clarify rewards and punishments to encourage them.
translations.idiomatic: when victory must be seized in the field, make rewards and punishments clear to spur men on.

sentences.zh: 用能辟國甯方，征伐四克。

translations.literal: By these means one can open the state and bring the realm to peace, and campaigns and punitive expeditions succeed on all sides.
translations.idiomatic: By such means a state may expand its borders, secure the realm, and prevail in every campaign.

sentences.zh: 北狄悍愚，同於禽獸，所長者野戰，所短者攻城。

translations.literal: The northern Di are fierce and stupid, like birds and beasts; what they excel at is fighting in the wild, what they are poor at is besieging cities.
translations.idiomatic: The northern barbarians are brutal and simple, little better than animals; they excel at open battle but are weak at siege warfare.

sentences.zh: 若以狄之所短，奪其所長，則雖眾不能成患，雖來不能內逼。

translations.literal: If one uses what the Di are poor at to overcome what they excel at, then though numerous they cannot become a calamity, and though they come they cannot press inward.
translations.idiomatic: If we exploit their weaknesses to neutralize their strengths, then even in great numbers they cannot threaten us, and even when they come they cannot press deep into our territory.

sentences.zh: 又狄散居野澤，隨逐水草，戰則與室家並至，奔則與畜牧俱逃。

translations.literal: Moreover the Di live scattered in marshes and wilds, following after water and grass; when they fight they arrive together with their households, when they flee they escape together with their herds.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover they live scattered across marshes and wild country, moving with the pasturage; when they fight they bring their families with them, and when they flee they drive off their herds as well.

sentences.zh: 是以古人伐北方，攘其侵掠而已。

translations.literal: Therefore the ancients in campaigning against the north merely drove off their raids and invasions.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the ancients, when they campaigned northward, contented themselves with repelling raids and incursions.

sentences.zh: 歷代為邊患者，良以倏忽無常故也。

translations.literal: The reason successive dynasties suffered frontier troubles was truly because the barbarians were sudden and unpredictable.
translations.idiomatic: Dynasty after dynasty suffered on the frontier chiefly because these enemies struck suddenly and without warning.

sentences.zh: 六鎮勢分，倍眾不鬥，互相圍逼，難以制之。

translations.literal: The six garrisons are divided in strength; though twice the enemy in number they do not fight, and when they surround and press one another they are hard to control.
translations.idiomatic: The six frontier garrisons are scattered; even at double strength they hesitate to give battle, and when they hem one another in they become difficult to command.

sentences.zh: 昔周命南仲，城彼朔方，趙靈、秦始，長城是築；

translations.literal: Formerly Zhou appointed Nanzhong and walled that northern region; King Ling of Zhao and the First Emperor of Qin built the Long Wall;
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Zhou commissioned Nanzhong to fortify the northern frontier; King Ling of Zhao and the First Emperor of Qin raised the Long Wall;

sentences.zh: 漢之孝武，踵其前事。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu of Han followed their earlier deeds.
translations.idiomatic: and Emperor Wu of Han followed their example.

sentences.zh: 此四代之君，皆帝王之雄傑，所以同此役者，非智術之不長，兵眾之不足，乃防狄之要事，理宜然也。

translations.literal: These rulers of four dynasties were all heroic emperors and kings; the reason they all undertook this task was not that their wisdom and arts were insufficient or their troops inadequate, but that defending against the Di was an essential matter and reason demanded it.
translations.idiomatic: These four rulers were all formidable sovereigns. They undertook the same labor not from lack of strategy or troops, but because guarding against the northern barbarians was essential—and rightly so.

sentences.zh: 今故宜於六鎮之北築長城，以禦北虜，雖有暫勞之勤，乃有永逸之益。

translations.literal: Now it is fitting to build the Long Wall north of the six garrisons to repel the northern invaders; though there is temporary toil, there will be lasting ease.
translations.idiomatic: We should therefore build a long wall north of the six garrisons to hold off the northern foe. The labor would be brief; the benefit, lasting.

sentences.zh: 即於要害，往往開門，造小城於其側，因施卻敵，多置弓弩。

translations.literal: At strategic points open gates at intervals, build small cities beside them, deploy means to repel the enemy, and station many crossbows.
translations.idiomatic: At every critical point open gates at intervals, erect small forts beside them, deploy countermeasures against attack, and stock them heavily with crossbows.

sentences.zh: 狄來，有城可守，有兵可捍。

translations.literal: When the Di come, there will be cities to defend and troops to resist.
translations.idiomatic: When the barbarians come, there will be walls to hold and soldiers to fight.

sentences.zh: 既不攻城，野掠無獲，草盡則走，終始必懲。

translations.literal: Unable to besiege cities, with no gains from wild raiding, when the grass is exhausted they will flee, and from beginning to end they will surely be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to take walled places and finding no profit in open raiding, they will withdraw once the pasturage is spent—and in the end they will always be punished.

sentences.zh: 又宜發近州武勇四萬人，及京師二萬人，合六萬人，為武士；

translations.literal: It is also fitting to mobilize forty thousand valiant warriors from nearby provinces and twenty thousand from the capital, sixty thousand in all, as martial troops;
translations.idiomatic: We should also mobilize forty thousand seasoned fighters from nearby provinces and twenty thousand from the capital—sixty thousand warriors in all.

sentences.zh: 于苑內立征北大將軍府，選忠勇有志幹者以充其選。

translations.literal: establish within the park a headquarters of the General Who Campaigns North, and select men who are loyal, brave, and ambitious to fill its ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Establish a headquarters for the General Who Campaigns North within the imperial park, and fill its ranks with men of loyalty, courage, and resolve.

sentences.zh: 下置官屬，分為三軍：二萬人專習弓射，二萬人專習刀楯，二萬人專習騎槊。

translations.literal: Set subordinate officials beneath it and divide into three armies: twenty thousand to specialize in archery, twenty thousand in sword and shield, twenty thousand in mounted lance.
translations.idiomatic: Appoint a full staff beneath it and divide the force into three corps: twenty thousand trained in archery, twenty thousand in sword and shield, and twenty thousand in mounted lance combat.

sentences.zh: 修立戰場，十日一習。

translations.literal: Construct drill grounds and practice every ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Build training grounds and drill the men every ten days.

sentences.zh: 采諸葛亮八陣之法，為平地禦敵之方，使其解兵革之宜，識旌旗之節。

translations.literal: Adopt Zhuge Liang's Eight Arrays method to form tactics for meeting the enemy on level ground, so that they understand the fitness of arms and armor and know the regulations of banners and flags.
translations.idiomatic: Adopt Zhuge Liang's Eight Arrays formation for open-field defense, so that the men learn the proper use of arms and the signals of banner and drum.

sentences.zh: 兵器精堅，必堪禦寇。

translations.literal: Weapons should be refined and strong, surely fit to repel invaders.
translations.idiomatic: Their weapons must be of the finest make, fit to repel any foe.

sentences.zh: 使將有定兵，兵有常主，上下相信，晝夜如一。

translations.literal: Let generals have fixed troops and troops have regular commanders; above and below trust one another, alike day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Let each commander have a fixed force and each soldier a fixed leader, so that officers and men trust one another without fail, day or night.

sentences.zh: 七月，發六郡兵萬人，各備戎作之具，敕臺北諸屯倉庫，隨近往來，俱送北鎮。

translations.literal: In the seventh month mobilize ten thousand troops from six commanderies, each equipped with tools for military labor; order the depots and granaries north of the capital to dispatch supplies according to proximity, all sent to the northern garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month mobilize ten thousand men from six commanderies, each with tools for military construction; order the depots north of the capital to forward supplies as convenience allows, all destined for the northern garrisons.

sentences.zh: 至八月，征北部率所鎮，與六鎮之兵，直至磧南，揚威漠北。

translations.literal: By the eighth month the northern campaign headquarters will lead its command together with the troops of the six garrisons straight to south of the desert, displaying might north of the steppe.
translations.idiomatic: By the eighth month the northern headquarters should lead its forces and the six garrisons' troops to the southern desert and display our might across the northern steppe.

sentences.zh: 狄若來拒，與決戰；

translations.literal: If the Di come to resist, give them decisive battle;
translations.idiomatic: If the barbarians come out to fight, meet them in decisive battle;

sentences.zh: 若其不來，然後散分其地，以築長城。

translations.literal: if they do not come, then disperse and divide the territory to build the Long Wall.
translations.idiomatic: if they do not, then divide the labor across the territory and raise the long wall.

sentences.zh: 計六鎮，東西不過千里，若一夫一月之功當二步之地，三百人三里，三千人三十里，三萬人三百里，則千里之地，強弱相兼，計十萬人一月必就。

translations.literal: Calculating for the six garrisons, east to west is no more than a thousand li; if one man's labor in one month equals two paces of ground, three hundred men three li, three thousand men thirty li, thirty thousand men three hundred li, then for a thousand li of territory, strong and weak combined, calculating one hundred thousand men, in one month it will surely be completed.
translations.idiomatic: The six garrisons span no more than a thousand li east to west. If one man in one month can complete two paces of wall, then three hundred men will finish three li, three thousand thirty li, and thirty thousand three hundred li. With a mixed force of strong and weak totaling one hundred thousand men, the full thousand li could be finished in a single month.

sentences.zh: 軍糧一月，不足為多，人懷永逸，勞而無怨。

translations.literal: Army provisions for one month are not much; men will harbor lasting ease, toiling yet without complaint.
translations.idiomatic: A month's rations are a modest expense; the men will accept brief hardship for lasting security and labor without resentment.

sentences.zh: 計築長城，其利有五：罷遊防之苦，其利一也；

translations.literal: Calculating the building of the Long Wall, its benefits are five: ending the suffering of roaming defense—benefit one;
translations.idiomatic: Building the long wall offers five benefits: first, an end to the misery of roving frontier defense;

sentences.zh: 北部放牧，無抄掠之患，其利二也；

translations.literal: herding in the northern regions without the trouble of raids and plunder—benefit two;
translations.idiomatic: second, secure pasturage in the north without fear of raids;

sentences.zh: 登城觀敵，以逸待勞，其利三也；

translations.literal: ascending the wall to observe the enemy, meeting labor with ease—benefit three;
translations.idiomatic: third, the ability to watch the enemy from the walls and meet their exertion with rested troops;

sentences.zh: 省境防之虞，息無時之備，其利四也；

translations.literal: sparing frontier defense anxieties, resting from unceasing readiness—benefit four;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, relief from constant frontier anxiety and endless vigilance;

sentences.zh: 歲常遊運，永得不匱，其利五也。

translations.literal: the yearly constant transport by roving, forever without shortage—benefit five.
translations.idiomatic: fifth, an end to the annual emergency convoys and perpetual shortages of supply.

sentences.zh: 孝文詔曰：「比當與卿面論。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen issued an edict: "Recently I shall discuss this with you face to face."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen replied, "I shall discuss this with you in person before long."

sentences.zh: 」又詔閭為書問蠕蠕。

translations.literal: He also ordered Lu to compose a letter of inquiry to the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Lu to draft a diplomatic letter to the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 時蠕蠕國有喪而書不敘凶事。

translations.literal: At that time the Rouran state was in mourning, but the letter did not mention the bereavement.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran were in mourning at the time, yet the letter made no mention of the bereavement.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿職典文辭，不論彼之凶事，若知而不作，罪在灼然；

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Your office is in charge of literary compositions; not to address their misfortune—if you knew and did not write, the guilt is obvious;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Your office oversees state documents. To ignore their bereavement—if you knew and omitted it, the fault is plain;

sentences.zh: 若情思不至，應謝所任。

translations.literal: if your feelings and thoughts did not reach there, you should resign your post."
translations.idiomatic: if your heart was not in the task, you ought to resign your post."

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「昔蠕蠕主敦崇和親，其子屢犯邊境，如臣愚見，謂不宜吊。

translations.literal: He replied: "Formerly the Rouran ruler earnestly upheld harmony and kinship, but his son repeatedly violated the border; in your servant's foolish view, it is not fitting to offer condolences."
translations.idiomatic: Lu replied, "The late Rouran ruler honored peace with us, yet his son has raided our borders again and again. In my humble view, condolences would be inappropriate."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「敬其父則子悅，敬其君則臣悅，卿雲不合吊慰，是何言歟？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Honor the father and the son is pleased; honor the ruler and the ministers are pleased—yet you say it is not fitting to offer condolences and comfort; what sort of talk is this?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Honor the father and the son is gratified; honor the ruler and his ministers are gratified—yet you say we should not send condolences. What kind of counsel is that?"

sentences.zh: 」閭遂免冠謝罪。

translations.literal: Lu thereupon removed his cap and apologized for his offense.
translations.idiomatic: Lu removed his cap and begged the emperor's pardon.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「蠕蠕使牟提，小心恭慎，同行疾其敦厚，恐其還北，必被謗誣。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The Rouran envoy Mouti is careful and respectful; his companions resent his earnest honesty, and I fear that when he returns north he will surely be slandered.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The Rouran envoy Mouti is careful and respectful. His companions resent his integrity, and I fear that when he returns north he will be slandered.

sentences.zh: 昔劉准使殷靈誕，每禁下人不為非禮事，及還，果被譖訴，以致極刑。

translations.literal: Formerly when Liu Song sent Yin Lingdan, he always forbade his subordinates from improper conduct, and when he returned he was indeed denounced and brought to extreme punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Song once sent Yin Lingdan as envoy, he forbade his attendants every impropriety; on his return he was denounced nonetheless and put to death.

sentences.zh: 今書可明牟提忠於其國，使蠕蠕主知之。」

translations.literal: In today's letter make clear that Mouti is loyal to his state, so that the Rouran ruler may know it."
translations.idiomatic: Let today's letter make plain that Mouti is loyal to his country, so that the Rouran ruler may know it."

sentences.zh: 是年冬至，大饗群官，孝文親舞于太后前，群臣皆舞。

translations.literal: That year at the winter solstice a great feast was held for the officials; Xiaowen himself danced before the empress dowager, and all the ministers danced.
translations.idiomatic: At the winter solstice that year the court held a grand feast for the officials; Emperor Xiaowen danced before the empress dowager, and the whole assembly followed.

sentences.zh: 帝乃長歌，仍率群臣再拜上壽。

translations.literal: The emperor then sang a long song and led the ministers in bowing twice to offer wishes for long life.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then sang a long verse and led the ministers in bowing twice to offer wishes for long life.

sentences.zh: 閭進曰：「臣聞大夫行孝，行合一家；

translations.literal: Lu stepped forward and said: "Your servant has heard that when a grandee practices filial piety, his conduct harmonizes one household;
translations.idiomatic: Lu stepped forward and said, "I have heard that when a grandee practices filial piety, his household is brought into harmony;

sentences.zh: 諸侯行孝，聲著一國；

translations.literal: when a feudal lord practices filial piety, his reputation resounds through one state;
translations.idiomatic: when a feudal lord practices it, his renown fills a whole state;

sentences.zh: 天子行孝，德被四海。

translations.literal: when the Son of Heaven practices filial piety, his virtue covers the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: when the Son of Heaven practices it, his virtue reaches the four seas.

sentences.zh: 今陛下敦行孝道，臣等不勝慶踴，謹上千萬歲壽。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty earnestly practices filial piety; your servants cannot contain our rejoicing and leap for joy, and respectfully offer wishes for ten thousand years of life."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty now practices filial piety with such devotion that we cannot contain our joy, and we respectfully wish you ten thousand years of life."

sentences.zh: 」帝大悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 又議政於皇信堂，閭曰：「伏思太皇太后十八條之令，及仰尋聖朝所行，事周於百揆，願終成其事。

translations.literal: Again they deliberated on government in the Hall of Imperial Trust; Lu said: "Your servant reflects on the Grand Empress Dowager's eighteen ordinances, and looking up traces what the sacred court has carried out—the affairs are comprehensive among the hundred offices; I wish to see them brought to completion."
translations.idiomatic: Deliberating again in the Hall of Imperial Trust, Lu said, "I reflect on the Grand Empress Dowager's eighteen ordinances and review what the sacred court has undertaken. The program touches every branch of government, and I pray it may be brought to completion."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「刑法者，王道所用。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Punishments and laws are what the kingly Way employs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Punishments and laws are instruments of the kingly Way.

sentences.zh: 何者為法？

translations.literal: What is called law?
translations.idiomatic: What counts as law?

sentences.zh: 何者為刑？

translations.literal: What is called punishment?
translations.idiomatic: What counts as punishment?

sentences.zh: 施行之日，何先何後？

translations.literal: On the day of putting them into practice, what comes first and what after?"
translations.idiomatic: When they are put into practice, which comes first and which after?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「刑制之會，軌物齊眾，謂之法；

translations.literal: He replied: "The meeting of penal institutions, regulating things and bringing the multitude into order, is called law;
translations.idiomatic: Lu replied, "The standards that regulate conduct and harmonize the people are called law;

sentences.zh: 犯違制約，致之於憲，謂之刑。

translations.literal: violating and transgressing regulations and contracts, bringing one under the statutes, is called punishment.
translations.idiomatic: transgression of those standards and subjection to the penal code is called punishment.

sentences.zh: 然則法必先施，刑必後著。

translations.literal: Thus law must be applied first, and punishment must come afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Law must therefore be established first; punishment follows after.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「《論語》稱：冉子退朝，孔子曰：'何晏也？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The Analects says: When Ranzi withdrew from court, Confucius said, 'Why so late?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The Analects records that when Ran withdrew from court, Confucius asked, 'Why so late?'

sentences.zh: '曰：'有政。

translations.literal: He said, 'There was government.'
translations.idiomatic: Ran replied, 'There was government business.'

sentences.zh: '子曰：'其事也，如其有政，雖不吾以，吾其與聞之。

translations.literal: Confucius said, 'It was affairs; if there really was government, though he did not employ me, I should have heard of it.'
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, 'Mere routine affairs. If it had been true government, even though he does not employ me, I should have heard something of it.'

sentences.zh: '何者為政？

translations.literal: What is called government?
translations.idiomatic: What counts as government?

sentences.zh: 何者為事？

translations.literal: What is called affairs?"
translations.idiomatic: What counts as routine affairs?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「政者，上之所行；

translations.literal: He replied: "Government is what those above carry out;
translations.idiomatic: Lu replied, "Government is what those above enact;

sentences.zh: 事者，下之所綜。

translations.literal: affairs are what those below administer."
translations.idiomatic: affairs are what those below manage."

sentences.zh: 」後詔閭與太常采雅樂以營金石。

translations.literal: Later an edict ordered Lu together with the Minister of Ceremonies to gather elegant music to furnish bells and stones.
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor ordered Lu and the Minister of Ceremonies to collect refined music for the court's bells and stone chimes.

sentences.zh: 又領廣陵王師，出除鎮南將軍、相州刺史。

translations.literal: He also headed the tutorial staff of the Prince of Guangling, then went out and was made General Who Guards the South and Governor of Xiang province.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as tutor to the Prince of Guangling, then left the capital as General Who Guards the South and Governor of Xiang province.

sentences.zh: 以參定律令之勤，賜布帛粟牛馬等。

translations.literal: For his diligence in participating in compiling laws and statutes, he was granted cloth, silk, grain, cattle, horses, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: For his work on the legal code he received gifts of cloth, silk, grain, cattle, and horses.

sentences.zh: 遷都洛陽，閭表諫，言遷有十損，必不獲已，請遷於鄴。

translations.literal: When the capital was moved to Luoyang, Lu submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying the move had ten harms; if it could not be avoided, he asked that the move be to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: When the court moved the capital to Luoyang, Lu memorialized in protest, arguing that the transfer entailed ten losses; if a move could not be avoided, he urged relocating to Ye instead.

sentences.zh: 帝頗嫌之。

translations.literal: The emperor was rather displeased with him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took considerable offense.

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史曹武據襄陽請降，車駕親幸懸瓠。

translations.literal: Cao Wu, Governor of Yong province, held Xiangyang and requested surrender; the imperial carriage personally visited Xuanchi.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Wu, Governor of Yong province, held Xiangyang and offered to surrender; the emperor went in person to Xuanchi.

sentences.zh: 閭表諫：洛陽草創，武既不遣質任，必非誠心，帝不納。

translations.literal: Lu submitted a memorial of remonstrance: Luoyang was newly established; since Wu sent no hostage, he surely was not sincere—the emperor did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Lu memorialized in protest: Luoyang was still being built, and since Wu had sent no hostage his offer could not be sincere. The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 武果虛詐，諸將皆無功而還。

translations.literal: Wu indeed was false and deceitful, and the generals all returned without achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Wu proved treacherous after all, and the generals returned without success.

sentences.zh: 車駕還幸石濟，閭朝於行宮。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned and visited Shiji, Lu attended audience at the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the emperor's return to Shiji, Lu presented himself at the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 帝謂曰：「朕往年之意，不欲決征。

translations.literal: The Emperor said to him: 'In years past, my intent was not to launch a decisive campaign.'
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said to him, "In earlier years I had not meant to commit to a full-scale campaign."

sentences.zh: 但兵士已集，恐為幽王之失，不容中止，遂至淮南。

translations.literal: But the soldiers had already assembled; fearing it would become King You's mistake, it could not be halted midway, and thus it reached Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: But the troops were already mustered, and I feared repeating King You's error—once begun, the campaign could not be stopped, and so it reached Huainan."

sentences.zh: 而彼諸將並列州鎮，至無所獲，實由晚一月日故耳。

translations.literal: Yet those generals all held concurrent posts as provincial governors and garrison commanders, so in the end they gained nothing; it was truly because the campaign was a month or so late.
translations.idiomatic: Those commanders all held provincial and garrison posts at the same time, so in the end we took almost nothing—the real reason was simply that we were a month too late."

sentences.zh: 」閭曰：「古攻戰法，倍則攻之，十則圍之。

translations.literal: Gao Lu said: 'In the ancient rules of attack and warfare, if you outnumber the enemy twofold, attack; if tenfold, besiege.'
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lu replied, "The old military rule says: double the enemy's strength and you attack; ten times it and you besiege."

sentences.zh: 聖駕親征，誠應大捷，所以無大獲，良由兵少故也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's personal campaign truly ought to have brought a great victory; the reason there was no major gain was simply that the army was too few.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty leads the army in person, a great victory is only right—but we won little because our forces were too few."

sentences.zh: 今京邑甫爾，庶事造創，願陛下當從容伊、瀍，使德被四海。

translations.literal: Now the capital has only just been established and all affairs are newly being founded; I hope Your Majesty will take the ease of ruling from the Yi and Chan, so that your virtue spreads over the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: The capital has only just been settled and every institution is still being built. I hope Your Majesty will govern at ease from the Yi and Chan rivers, and let your virtue reach the four seas."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「願從容伊、瀍，實亦不少，但未獲耳。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: 'My wish to take ease at Yi and Chan is indeed not slight—but I have simply not achieved it yet.'
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "My wish to rule at ease from Yi and Chan is no small one—but I have not yet attained it."

sentences.zh: 」閭曰：「司馬相如臨終，恨不封禪。

translations.literal: Gao Lu said: 'When Sima Xiangru was dying, he regretted that he had not performed the feng and shan sacrifices.'
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lu said, "On his deathbed Sima Xiangru regretted that he had never performed the feng and shan rites."

sentences.zh: 今雖江介不賓，然中州地略以盡平，豈可聖明之辰，而闕盛禮？

translations.literal: Though the lands along the rivers still do not submit, yet the Central Plains are largely pacified—how can we, in this age of sagely brilliance, omit this grand rite?
translations.idiomatic: Though the riverlands still hold out, the heartland is largely at peace. How can an age as enlightened as this go without the supreme ceremony?"

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「荊揚未一，豈得如卿言也？

translations.literal: The Emperor said: 'Jing and Yang are not yet unified—how can things be as you say?'
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Jing and Yang are not yet united—how can I do as you suggest?"

sentences.zh: 」閭以江南非中國，且三代之境，亦不能遠。

translations.literal: Gao Lu held that the lands south of the Yangzi were not China, and even the borders of the Three Dynasties could not be said to extend far in that direction.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lu considered the lands south of the Yangzi not to be China, and held that even the Three Dynasties had never reached far beyond that.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「淮海惟揚州，荊及衡陽惟荊州，此非近中國乎？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: 'Between the Huai and the sea is Yang Province; Jing and Hengyang constitute Jing Province—is this not close to the Central Plains?'
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "From the Huai to the sea is Yang Province; Jing and Hengyang make up Jing Province—is that not near the heartland?"

sentences.zh: 及車駕至鄴，孝文頻幸其州館，下詔褒揚之。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage arrived at Ye, Emperor Xiaowen frequently visited his provincial residence and issued an edict praising him.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial procession reached Ye, Emperor Xiaowen often called at Gao Lu's provincial residence and issued an edict commending him.

sentences.zh: 閭每請本州以自效，詔曰：「閭以懸車之年，方求衣錦。

translations.literal: Gao Lu repeatedly requested to serve his home province to prove his worth; an edict stated: 'Gao Lu, at the age when one should suspend the chariot, now seeks to return home in embroidered robes.'
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lu repeatedly asked to serve in his home province and prove himself. An edict read: "Gao Lu, at the age when one should retire, now seeks to return home in glory."

sentences.zh: 知進忘退，有塵謙德，可降號平北將軍。

translations.literal: He knows advance but forgets retreat, staining the virtue of humility; he may be demoted in rank to General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: He knows how to press forward but not how to step back, tarnishing the virtue of humility. Let his title be reduced to General Who Pacifies the North."

sentences.zh: 朝之老成，宜遂情願，徙授幽州刺史，令存勸兼行，恩法並舉。

translations.literal: As an elder statesman of the court, his wishes ought to be granted; transfer and appoint him Governor of You Province, ordering him to implement both nurturing encouragement and enforcement, combining favor and law.
translations.idiomatic: As a senior man of the court, his wish should be granted. Transfer him and appoint him Governor of You Province, with orders to practice both nurture and admonition together, blending grace and law."

sentences.zh: 」閭以諸州罷從事，依府置參軍，於政體不便，表宜復舊。

translations.literal: Gao Lu argued that since the various provinces had abolished the Recorder posts and placed Military Aides according to the prefecture system, this was inconvenient for governance, and memorialized that the old system should be restored.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lu held that abolishing provincial Recorders and staffing offices with Military Aides on the prefectural model was bad for governance, and submitted a memorial asking that the old arrangement be restored.

sentences.zh: 帝不悅。

translations.literal: The Emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，表求致仕，優答不許。

translations.literal: After more than a year, he memorialized requesting retirement; a gracious reply refused permission.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later he submitted a memorial asking to retire; the Emperor graciously refused.

sentences.zh: 徵為太常卿，頻表陳遜，不聽。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Minister of Ceremonies; he repeatedly memorialized declining, but the Emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as Minister of Ceremonies and repeatedly memorialized to decline, but the Emperor would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 又車駕南討漢陽，閭上表諫求回師，帝不納。

translations.literal: Again, when the imperial carriage marched south to campaign against Hanyang, Gao Lu memorialized remonstrating and asking to withdraw the army; the Emperor did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor marched south against Hanyang, Gao Lu submitted a memorial urging withdrawal; the Emperor did not accept his advice.

sentences.zh: 漢陽平，賜閭璽書，閭上表陳謝。

translations.literal: When Hanyang was pacified, the Emperor granted Gao Lu an imperial letter under seal; Gao Lu memorialized expressing thanks.
translations.idiomatic: After Hanyang was pacified, the Emperor sent Gao Lu an imperial letter under seal, and Gao Lu submitted a memorial of thanks.

sentences.zh: 宣武踐阼，閭累表遜位，優詔授光祿大夫，金章紫綬；

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanwu ascended the throne, Gao Lu repeatedly memorialized declining office; a gracious edict appointed him Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, with golden seal and purple sash.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu took the throne, Gao Lu repeatedly asked to yield his post. A gracious edict appointed him Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, with golden seal and purple sash.

sentences.zh: 使吏部尚書邢巒就家拜授。

translations.literal: The Minister of the Civil Service, Xing Luan, was sent to his home to invest him with the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of the Civil Service, Xing Luan, was sent to his home to confer the appointment.

sentences.zh: 及辭，引見東堂，賜以肴羞，訪之大政。

translations.literal: When he came to take leave, the Emperor received him in audience at the Eastern Hall, bestowed food and delicacies upon him, and consulted him on great matters of state.
translations.idiomatic: When he came to bid farewell, the Emperor received him in the Eastern Hall, gave him a feast, and questioned him on weighty affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 以其先朝儒舊，告老求歸，帝為之流涕。

translations.literal: Because he was an elder scholar-official of the previous reign and sought to retire and return home on account of age, the Emperor wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: Because he was a scholar-official of the former reign who now asked to retire and go home, the Emperor wept for him.

sentences.zh: 優詔賜安車、几杖、輿馬、繪彩、衣服、布帛，事從豐厚。

translations.literal: A gracious edict granted him a comfort cart, armrest and staff, carriage and horses, painted silks, garments, and cloth—all with generous provision.
translations.idiomatic: A gracious edict granted him a comfort carriage, armrest and staff, horses and carriage, painted silks, robes, and cloth—all in generous measure.

sentences.zh: 百寮餞之，猶群公之祖二疏也。

translations.literal: The hundred officials saw him off, as the host of worthies had once escorted the Two Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The whole court saw him off, as the great ministers had once done for the Two Shu.

sentences.zh: 閭進陟北芒，上《望闕表》以示戀慕之誠。

translations.literal: Gao Lu went up onto Mount Beimang and submitted the 'Memorial Gazing Toward the Palace Gate' to show his devotion and yearning.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lu climbed Mount Beimang and submitted his "Memorial Gazing Toward the Palace Gate" to show his longing and loyalty.

sentences.zh: 卒于家，諡文貞。

translations.literal: He died at home; his posthumous title was Wen Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home and was given the posthumous name Wen Zhen.

sentences.zh: 閭好為文章，集四十卷。

translations.literal: Gao Lu loved composing literary works; his collected writings filled forty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lu loved writing, and his collected works ran to forty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 其文亦高允之流，後稱二高，為當時所服。

translations.literal: His writing was of the same caliber as Gao Yun's; later they were called 'the Two Gaos,' and were admired by their contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: His prose ranked with Gao Yun's; later the two were called "the Two Gaos," and men of the time held them in esteem.

sentences.zh: 閭強果敢直諫，其在私室，言裁聞耳；

translations.literal: Gao Lu was strong, resolute, and bold in direct remonstrance; in private quarters, his words barely reached one's ears.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lu was forceful, resolute, and fearless in direct remonstrance; in private his words scarcely rose above a whisper.

sentences.zh: 及於朝廷廣眾之中，則談論鋒起，人莫能敵。

translations.literal: But in the broad assembly of the court, his discourse flashed like blades, and no one could match him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the open court, his speech flashed like drawn steel, and no one could stand against him.

sentences.zh: 孝文以其文雅之美，每優禮之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen, on account of his literary refinement and elegance, always treated him with special honor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen, valuing his literary grace, always treated him with exceptional courtesy.

sentences.zh: 然貪褊矜慢。

translations.literal: Yet he was greedy, narrow-minded, arrogant, and condescending.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was greedy, petty, proud, and disdainful of others.

sentences.zh: 初在中書，好詈辱諸博士。

translations.literal: Early on, while at the Secretariat, he loved to revile and humiliate the various erudites.
translations.idiomatic: In his early days at the Secretariat he liked to curse and humiliate the court erudites.

sentences.zh: 學生百餘人，有所幹求者，無不受其賄。

translations.literal: Among his more than a hundred student clerks, anyone who came with a request none failed to give him a bribe.
translations.idiomatic: Of his more than a hundred student clerks, anyone who came with a request had to pay him a bribe—none escaped it.

sentences.zh: 及老為二州，乃更廉儉自謹，有良牧之譽。

translations.literal: When he grew old and served as governor of two provinces, he became more frugal and self-restrained, earning a reputation as a good administrator.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew old and governed two provinces, he turned frugal and self-disciplined and won a name as a good magistrate.

sentences.zh: 子元昌襲爵，位遼西、博陵二郡太守。

translations.literal: His son Yuan Chang inherited the marquisate and served as Administrator of both Liaoxi and Boling commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuan Chang inherited the marquisate and served as Administrator of Liaoxi and Boling commanderies.

sentences.zh: 閭弟悅，篤志好學，有美於閭，早卒。

translations.literal: Gao Lu's younger brother Yue was steadfast in aspiration and loved learning; he was finer than Gao Lu, but died young.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lu's younger brother Yue was devoted to learning and outshone Gao Lu in talent, but died young.

sentences.zh: 趙逸，字思群，天水人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Yi, courtesy name Sigun, was a native of Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yi, styled Sigun, was a native of Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 父昌，石勒黃門郎。

translations.literal: His father Chang was a Yellow Gate Attendant under Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chang had been a Yellow Gate Attendant under Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 逸好學夙成，仕姚興，曆中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Zhao Yi loved learning and matured early; he served Yao Xing and successively held the post of Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yi loved learning and showed early promise. He entered the service of Yao Xing and rose to Secretariat Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 後為赫連屈丐所虜，拜著作郎。

translations.literal: Later he was captured by Helian Qugai and was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was taken captive by Helian Qugai and appointed Compiler.

sentences.zh: 太武平統萬，見逸所著，曰：「此豎無道，安得為此言乎！

translations.literal: When Emperor Taiwu pacified Tongwan and saw what Zhao Yi had written, he said: 'This vile fellow has no way—how dare he speak such words!'
