translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taiwu took Tongwan and read Zhao Yi's writings, he said, "This worthless wretch has no principles—how dare he write such things!"

sentences.zh: 作者誰也？

translations.literal: 'Who is the author?'
translations.idiomatic: "Who wrote this?"

sentences.zh: 速推之。

translations.literal: 'Quickly bring him forward.'
translations.idiomatic: "Bring him here at once."

sentences.zh: 」司徒崔浩進曰：「彼之謬述，亦子雲《美新》，固宜容之。

translations.literal: Minister over the Masses Cui Hao stepped forward and said: 'His erroneous writings are like Yang Xiong's Praise of the New—they ought to be tolerated.'
translations.idiomatic: Minister over the Masses Cui Hao stepped forward and said, "These mistaken writings are like Yang Xiong's Praise of the New—they should be tolerated."

sentences.zh: 」帝乃止。

translations.literal: The Emperor then stopped pursuing it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 曆中書侍郎、赤城鎮將，頻表乞免，久乃見許。

translations.literal: He successively served as Secretariat Gentleman and General of Chicheng Garrison; he repeatedly memorialized requesting release from office, and only after a long time was his request granted.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Secretariat Gentleman and General of Chicheng Garrison, repeatedly asking to be relieved of office; only after a long while was he allowed to go.

sentences.zh: 性好墳典，白首彌勤，年逾七十，手不釋卷，凡所著述，詩賦銘頌五十餘篇。

translations.literal: His nature loved the classics; in old age he grew all the more diligent. Past seventy, he never laid book from hand; all his writings—poetry, rhapsodies, inscriptions, and eulogies—numbered more than fifty pieces.
translations.idiomatic: He loved the classics by nature and grew only more diligent with age. Past seventy he never put down his books; his writings—poems, rhapsodies, inscriptions, and eulogies—numbered more than fifty pieces.

sentences.zh: 逸兄溫，字思恭，博學有高名，為姚泓天水太守。

translations.literal: Zhao Yi's elder brother Wen, courtesy name Sigong, was broadly learned and highly renowned; he served as Administrator of Tianshui under Yao Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yi's elder brother Wen, styled Sigong, was widely learned and greatly admired; he served Yao Hong as Administrator of Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 劉裕滅泓，遂沒於氐。

translations.literal: When Liu Yu destroyed Yao Hong, he was captured by the Di.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu destroyed Yao Hong, Wen fell into Di hands.

sentences.zh: 氐王楊難當稱籓，太武以溫為難當府司馬，卒于仇池令。

translations.literal: When the Di king Yang Nandang declared vassalage, Emperor Taiwu appointed Wen as Chief Administrator of Nandang's princely establishment; he died while serving as Magistrate of Qiuchi.
translations.idiomatic: When the Di king Yang Nandang submitted as a vassal, Emperor Taiwu made Wen Chief Administrator in Nandang's princely household; he died while serving as Magistrate of Qiuchi.

sentences.zh: 溫子琰，字叔起。

translations.literal: Wen's son Yan, courtesy name Shuqi.
translations.idiomatic: Wen's son was Yan, styled Shuqi.

sentences.zh: 初，苻氏亂，琰為乳母攜奔壽春，年十四乃歸。

translations.literal: At first, when the Fu clan fell into chaos, Yan was carried off by his wet nurse to flee to Shouchun; only at fourteen did he return.
translations.idiomatic: When the Fu clan fell into chaos, Yan's wet nurse fled with him to Shouchun; he did not return until he was fourteen.

sentences.zh: 孝心色養，飪熟之節，必親調之。

translations.literal: He served his parents with filial devotion in expression and nurture; at the times when food was cooked and prepared, he always personally seasoned it.
translations.idiomatic: He cared for his parents with filial devotion in word and deed; whenever food was cooked, he personally saw to its preparation.

sentences.zh: 皇興中，京師儉，婢簡粟糶之，琰遇見，切責，敕留輕昻比。

translations.literal: In the Huangxing era, when the capital suffered famine, a maidservant sifted grain to sell it; Yan happened upon this, sharply rebuked her, and ordered that a light angbi measure be withheld.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huangxing reign, when the capital was in famine, a maidservant sifted grain to sell it. Yan caught her at it, rebuked her sharply, and ordered one light angbi measure withheld.

sentences.zh: 嘗送子應冀州娉室，從者于路遇得一羊，行三十里而琰知之，令送於本處。

translations.literal: Once, when sending his son Ying to Jizhou for a betrothal, a follower found a stray goat on the road; after thirty li Yan learned of it and ordered it sent back to where it had been found.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while sending his son Ying to Jizhou to arrange a marriage, a servant picked up a goat on the road. Thirty li later Yan found out and ordered it returned to the spot where it had been taken.

sentences.zh: 又過路旁，主人設羊羹，琰訪知盜殺，卒辭不食。

translations.literal: On another occasion he passed a roadside house where the host served goat stew; Yan inquired and learned it had been killed by theft, and in the end refused it and did not eat.
translations.idiomatic: On another journey he stopped at a roadside house where the host served goat stew. Yan asked around, learned the goat had been stolen and slaughtered, and in the end refused the meal.

sentences.zh: 遣人買耜刃，得剩六耜，即命送還刃主。

translations.literal: He sent someone to buy plow blades; six blades were left over, and he immediately ordered them returned to the blade-seller.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a man to buy plow blades; six blades were left over, and he at once ordered them returned to the seller.

sentences.zh: 刃主高之，義而不受，琰命委之而去。

translations.literal: The blade-seller admired his integrity and refused to take payment out of righteousness; Yan ordered the money left with him and departed.
translations.idiomatic: The seller, admiring his integrity, would not accept payment on principle; Yan had the money left with him and went on.

sentences.zh: 初為兗州司馬，轉團城鎮副將。

translations.literal: At first he served as Chief Administrator of Yanzhou; he was transferred to Deputy General of Tuancheng Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as Chief Administrator of Yanzhou, then was transferred to Deputy General of Tuancheng Garrison.

sentences.zh: 還京，為淮南王他府長史。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital, he became Senior Administrator in the establishment of the Prince of Huainan, Ta.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to the capital, he became Senior Administrator in the household of the Prince of Huainan, Ta.

sentences.zh: 時禁制甚嚴，不聽越關葬於舊兆，琰積四十餘年不得葬二親。

translations.literal: At that time restrictions were very strict, and crossing passes to bury the dead in ancestral tombs was forbidden; Yan accumulated more than forty years unable to bury his parents.
translations.idiomatic: Restrictions were then very strict: burial in ancestral tombs across the frontier was forbidden, and Yan went more than forty years unable to bury his parents.

sentences.zh: 及蒸嘗拜獻，未曾不嬰慕卒事。

translations.literal: At seasonal sacrifices and offerings, he never failed to be overcome with intense grief when the rites ended, weeping.
translations.idiomatic: At the seasonal sacrifices he never failed to be overcome with grief when the rites ended, weeping as he finished.

sentences.zh: 每於時節，不受子孫慶賀。

translations.literal: At each seasonal occasion, he would not accept congratulations from his children and grandchildren.
translations.idiomatic: At every seasonal festival he refused congratulations from his children and grandchildren.

sentences.zh: 年餘耳順，而孝思彌篤，慨歲月推移，遷窆無冀，乃絕鹽粟，斷諸肴味，食麥而已。

translations.literal: Past the age of sixty, his filial devotion grew ever more earnest; lamenting that years rolled on without hope of moving the coffins to the ancestral graves, he gave up salt and grain, cut off all savory foods, and ate only wheat.
translations.idiomatic: Past sixty his filial devotion only deepened. Grieving that the years passed with no hope of reburial, he gave up salt and grain, refused all savory food, and ate nothing but wheat.

sentences.zh: 年八十卒。

translations.literal: He died at eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 遷都洛陽，子應等乃還鄉葬焉。

translations.literal: When the capital was moved to Luoyang, his son Ying and the others were finally able to return home and bury the parents there.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital moved to Luoyang, his son Ying and the others were at last able to return home and bury their parents.

sentences.zh: 應弟煦，字賓育，好音律，以善歌聞於世，位秦州刺史。

translations.literal: Ying's younger brother Xu, courtesy name Binyu, loved music; famed throughout the world for his skill in song, he held the post of Governor of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ying's younger brother Xu, styled Binyu, loved music and was renowned for his singing; he served as Governor of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 胡叟，字倫許，安定臨涇人也，世為西夏著姓。

translations.literal: Hu Sou, courtesy name Lunxu, was a native of Linjing in Anding—a prominent clan of Western Xia for generations.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Sou, styled Lunxu, came from Linjing in Anding; his family had been a leading clan of Western Xia for generations.

sentences.zh: 叟少聰慧，年十三，辯疑釋理，鮮有屈焉。

translations.literal: Hu Sou was clever from youth; at thirteen, in debating doubts and expounding principles, few could best him.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Sou was bright from childhood; at thirteen, when debating knotty questions and explaining doctrine, few could get the better of him.

sentences.zh: 學不師受，拔讀群籍，再閱於目，皆誦焉。

translations.literal: He studied without taking a teacher, pulling books from the shelves and reading through the canon; after a second glance, he could recite them all.
translations.idiomatic: He studied without a teacher, pulling works from the shelves and reading through whole libraries; after a second reading he could recite them from memory.

sentences.zh: 好屬文，既善典雅之詞，又工鄙欲之句。

translations.literal: He loved composing texts, skilled both in refined elegant phrasing and in plain vulgar-style lines.
translations.idiomatic: He loved to write, excelling both in elegant diction and in plain, rough-hewn lines.

sentences.zh: 以姚氏將衰，遂入長安觀風化。

translations.literal: Seeing that the Yao clan was about to decline, he entered Chang'an to observe its customs and culture.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the Yao house nearing its fall, he went to Chang'an to observe its customs and culture.

sentences.zh: 隱匿名行，懼人見知。

translations.literal: He hid his name on his travels, fearing that people would recognize him.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled under a false name, afraid of being recognized.

sentences.zh: 時京兆韋祖思少閱典墳，多蔑時彥，待叟不足。

translations.literal: At that time Wei Zusi of Jingzhao had read few classics yet often looked down on the leading talents of the age, and treated Hu Sou with insufficient respect.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wei Zusi of Jingzhao had read little of the classics yet often scorned the day's leading men, and treated Hu Sou with scant courtesy.

sentences.zh: 叟拂衣而出，祖思固留之曰：「當與君論天人之際，何遽返乎？

translations.literal: Hu Sou shook out his robes and left; Zusi pressed him to stay, saying: 'I was about to discuss with you the border between Heaven and man—why leave so hastily?'
translations.idiomatic: Hu Sou shook out his robes and walked out. Zusi pressed him to stay, saying, "I meant to discuss Heaven and man with you—why leave in such haste?"

sentences.zh: 」叟曰：「論天人者其亡久矣，與君相知，何誇言若是。

translations.literal: Hu Sou said: 'Those who discuss Heaven and man have long since vanished; knowing you as I do, why such boastful talk?'
translations.idiomatic: Hu Sou said, "Men who truly discuss Heaven and man have been gone a long while. Knowing you as I do, why talk so grandly?"

sentences.zh: 」遂歸主人，賦韋、杜二族，一宿而成。

translations.literal: He then returned to his lodging and composed a piece on the Wei and Du clans, finishing it in one night.
translations.idiomatic: He went back to his host's house and wrote a piece on the Wei and Du clans, finishing it in a single night.

sentences.zh: 時年十八矣。

translations.literal: He was eighteen at the time.
translations.idiomatic: He was eighteen at the time.

sentences.zh: 其述前載，無違舊美；

translations.literal: In describing earlier ages, he violated none of the old praise.
translations.idiomatic: In treating earlier times he did not depart from the old encomia.

sentences.zh: 敘中世，有協時事；

translations.literal: In narrating the middle period, he accorded with current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In recounting the middle period he matched the affairs of the day.

sentences.zh: 而末及鄙黷。

translations.literal: At the end he added vulgar abuse.
translations.idiomatic: At the end he added coarse invective.

sentences.zh: 人皆奇其才，畏其筆。

translations.literal: Everyone marveled at his talent and feared his pen.
translations.idiomatic: All who read it marveled at his talent and feared his pen.

sentences.zh: 叟孤飄坎壈，未有仕路，遂入漢中。

translations.literal: Hu Sou, alone and adrift in hardship, had no path to office, and so entered Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Alone and adrift through hard times, with no road to office, Hu Sou went into Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 宋梁、秦二州刺史馮翊吉翰頗相禮接。

translations.literal: The Song Governor of Liang and Qin provinces, Jihan of Fenyang, treated him with considerable courtesy and hospitality.
translations.idiomatic: Jihan of Fenyang, Song Governor of Liang and Qin, treated him with real courtesy.

sentences.zh: 授叟末佐，不稱其懷。

translations.literal: He appointed Hu Sou to a low assistant post, which did not suit his aspirations.
translations.idiomatic: He gave Hu Sou a low assistant post, which did not satisfy Hu Sou's ambitions.

sentences.zh: 未幾，翰遷益州，叟隨入蜀。

translations.literal: Before long, Jihan was transferred to Yizhou, and Hu Sou followed him into Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Jihan was transferred to Yizhou, and Hu Sou followed him into Shu.

sentences.zh: 時蜀沙門法成率僧數千人鑄丈六金像，宋文帝惡其聚眾，將加大辟。

translations.literal: At that time the Shu monk Facheng led several thousand monks to cast a sixteen-foot golden image; Emperor Wen of Song detested their gathering crowd and was about to impose the death penalty.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Shu monk Facheng led several thousand monks in casting a sixteen-foot golden image. Emperor Wen of Song hated the mass gathering and was about to condemn him to death.

sentences.zh: 叟聞之，即赴丹楊，啟申其美，遂免。

translations.literal: Hu Sou heard of this, immediately went to Danyang, submitted a memorial stating its merits, and Facheng was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Sou heard of it, went at once to Danyang, and submitted a memorial setting out the project's merits; Facheng was spared.

sentences.zh: 復還蜀，法成遺其珍物，價直千餘匹，叟一無所受。

translations.literal: Returning again to Shu, Facheng offered him precious goods worth more than a thousand bolts of silk; Hu Sou accepted none of it.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to Shu, Facheng tried to give him valuables worth more than a thousand bolts of silk; Hu Sou would take none of it.

sentences.zh: 後入沮渠牧犍，牧犍遇之不重，叟乃為詩，示所知廣平程伯達。

translations.literal: Later he entered the domain of Juqu Mujian; Mujian did not treat him with respect, so Hu Sou wrote a poem and showed it to his acquaintance Cheng Boda of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: Later he entered the service of Juqu Mujian, who did not treat him well. Hu Sou then wrote a poem and showed it to his friend Cheng Boda of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 其略曰：「群犬吠新客，佞暗排疏賓；

translations.literal: Its gist ran: 'A pack of dogs bark at the new guest; flatterers in the dark drive off the plain guest.'
translations.idiomatic: It ran in part: "A pack of dogs bark at the new guest; sycophants in the dark drive off the honest guest."

sentences.zh: 直途既已塞，曲路非所遵。

translations.literal: The straight path is already blocked; crooked roads are not what I follow.
translations.idiomatic: The straight road is already shut; crooked paths are not for me."

sentences.zh: 望衛惋祝鮀，眄楚悼靈均。

translations.literal: Gazing toward Wei, I mourn Zhu Tuoruo; looking toward Chu, I grieve for Qu Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Looking toward Wei I mourn Zhu Tuoruo; looking toward Chu I grieve for Qu Yuan."

sentences.zh: 何用宣憂懷，托翰寄輔仁。

translations.literal: Why speak my sorrow aloud? I entrust it to writing, sending it to Furen.
translations.idiomatic: Why give voice to sorrow? I commit it to writing and send it to Furen."

sentences.zh: 」伯達見詩，謂曰：「涼州雖地居戎域，然自張氏以來，號有華風。

translations.literal: Cheng Boda saw the poem and said: 'Though Liangzhou lies in barbarian territory, since the Zhang clan it has been known for Chinese culture.'
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Boda read the poem and said, "Liangzhou may lie in barbarian country, but since the Zhang house it has been famed for Chinese culture."

sentences.zh: 今則憲章無虧，何祝鮀之有？

translations.literal: Now the laws and statutes are unblemished—why speak of Zhu Tuo?
translations.idiomatic: The laws stand intact and unbroken—what need is there to invoke the name of Zhu Tuo?

sentences.zh: 」叟曰：「貴主奉正朔而弗淳，慕仁義而未允。

translations.literal: Sou said: 'Your lordship follows the imperial calendar yet is not sincere; you admire benevolence and righteousness but have not attained them.'
translations.idiomatic: Sou said, "Your lordship observes the imperial calendar yet lacks sincerity; you affect benevolence and righteousness but have not fulfilled them."

sentences.zh: 吾之擇木，夙在大魏，與子暫違，非久闊也。

translations.literal: In choosing my perch, I have long fixed on Great Wei; parting from you for a while is no long estrangement.
translations.idiomatic: My chosen perch has always been Great Wei; a brief parting from you is no lasting estrangement.

sentences.zh: 」歲餘，牧犍破降。

translations.literal: More than a year later, Mujian was defeated and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Within a little more than a year Mujian was broken and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 叟既先歸魏，朝廷以其識機，賜爵始復男。

translations.literal: Sou had already returned to Wei first; the court, recognizing his foresight, ennobled him as Baron of Shifu.
translations.idiomatic: Sou had already gone back to Wei ahead of time; the court, noting his grasp of the moment, ennobled him as Baron Shifu.

sentences.zh: 家於密雲，蓬室草筵，唯以酒自適。

translations.literal: He made his home at Miyun in a thatched hut with a grass mat, finding his ease only in wine.
translations.idiomatic: He settled at Miyun in a thatched hut with a grass mat, taking his pleasure in wine alone.

sentences.zh: 謂友人金城宗舒曰：「我此生活，似勝焦先，志意所棲，謝其高矣。

translations.literal: He said to his friend Zong Shu of Jincheng: 'This life of mine seems even to surpass Jiao Xian's; as for the heights where the will may rest, I defer to him.'
translations.idiomatic: He told his friend Zong Shu of Jincheng, "This way of living of mine seems even better than Jiao Xian's; as for the lofty ambition one might embrace, I must yield to his height."

sentences.zh: 」文成時，召叟及舒，並使作檄，檄宋、蠕蠕。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Wencheng, Sou and Shu were both summoned and ordered to draft proclamations against Song and Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wencheng, Sou and Shu were both summoned and told to write proclamations denouncing Song and the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 舒文劣於叟。

translations.literal: Shu's prose was inferior to Sou's.
translations.idiomatic: Shu's writing fell short of Sou's.

sentences.zh: 尋歸家，不事產業，常苦饑貧，然不以為恥。

translations.literal: Before long he returned home, took no part in building an estate, often suffered hunger and poverty, yet did not consider it shameful.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he went home again, neglected property, often knew hunger and poverty, yet felt no shame in it.

sentences.zh: 養子字螟蛉，以自給養。

translations.literal: He adopted a son styled Mingling to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: He adopted a son styled Mingling to provide for his daily needs.

sentences.zh: 每至貴勝門，恆乘一牸牛，弊韋袴褶而已。

translations.literal: Whenever he came to Guisheng Gate he always rode a single cow, wearing only worn leather trousers and jacket.
translations.idiomatic: Each time he came to Guisheng Gate he rode a single cow, dressed in nothing but threadbare leather trousers and jacket.

sentences.zh: 作布囊。

translations.literal: He made a cloth sack.
translations.idiomatic: He made a cloth sack.

sentences.zh: 容三四斛，飲啖醉飽，盛余肉餅以付螟蛉。

translations.literal: It held three or four hu; after eating and drinking his fill he would put the leftover meat cakes into it for Mingling.
translations.idiomatic: It held three or four hu; when he had eaten and drunk his fill he packed the leftover meat cakes into it for Mingling.

sentences.zh: 見車馬榮華者，視之蔑如也。

translations.literal: When he saw the splendor of carriages and horses he treated it with utter disdain.
translations.idiomatic: Carriages and horses in all their splendor he regarded with utter contempt.

sentences.zh: 尚書李敷嘗遺以財，都無所取。

translations.literal: Minister of the Secretariat Li Fu once sent him money, but he took none of it.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of the Secretariat Li Fu once sent him gifts of money; he would accept none of it.

sentences.zh: 初，叟一見高允曰：「吳、鄭之交，以糸寧縞為美談；

translations.literal: At first, on meeting Gao Yun, Sou said: 'The friendship of Wu and Zheng was celebrated for its gifts of fine silk.'
translations.idiomatic: When he first met Gao Yun, Sou said, "The bond between Wu and Zheng was famed for its gifts of fine silk."

sentences.zh: 吾之於子，以弦韋為幽贄。

translations.literal: Between you and me, I offer bowstring and hide as my humble gift.
translations.idiomatic: As between us, I offer bowstring and leather as a modest token.

sentences.zh: 以此言之，彼可無愧也。

translations.literal: By this reckoning, they need feel no shame.
translations.idiomatic: Spoken thus, they need feel no shame.

sentences.zh: 」於允館見中書侍郎趙郡李璨，被服華靡；

translations.literal: At Yun's residence he saw Secretariat Attendant Li Can of Zhao commandery, splendidly dressed.
translations.idiomatic: At Yun's house he saw Secretariat Attendant Li Can of Zhao commandery, dressed in lavish finery.

sentences.zh: 叟貧老衣褐，璨頗忽之。

translations.literal: Sou, poor and old in hemp robes, Can rather looked down on him.
translations.idiomatic: Sou, poor and old in coarse hemp, Can looked down on him.

sentences.zh: 叟謂曰：「李子，今若相脫體上袴褶衣帽，君欲作何許也？

translations.literal: Sou said to him: 'Master Li, if one stripped you of the trousers, jacket, cap, and robes on your body, where would you claim to belong?'
translations.idiomatic: Sou said, "Master Li, if someone stripped off the trousers, jacket, cap, and robes on your body, where would you say you belonged?"

sentences.zh: 」譏其惟假盛服。

translations.literal: — mocking him for relying on fine clothes alone.
translations.idiomatic: — mocking him for depending on splendid dress alone.

sentences.zh: 璨惕然失色。

translations.literal: Can turned fearful and changed color.
translations.idiomatic: Can blanched in sudden alarm.

sentences.zh: 叟少孤，每言及父母，則淚下若孺子號。

translations.literal: Sou was orphaned young; whenever he spoke of his parents tears would fall as though a child wailing.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, whenever he spoke of his parents tears would fall like a child crying out.

sentences.zh: 春秋當祭之前，則先求旨酒美膳，將其所知廣甯常順陽、馮翊田文宗、上谷侯法俊，提壺執俎，至郭外空靜處，設坐奠拜，盡孝思之敬。

translations.literal: Before each spring and autumn sacrifice he would first seek fine wine and delicacies, then with those he knew—Chang Shunyang of Guangning, Tian Wenzong of Fenyang, and Hou Fajun of Shanggu—carry wine jars and sacrificial dishes to an empty quiet place outside the city wall, set out seats, bow, and fully observe filial reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Before each spring and autumn offering he first sought fine wine and delicacies, then with Chang Shunyang of Guangning, Tian Wenzong of Fenyang, and Hou Fajun of Shanggu—men he knew—carried wine jars and sacrificial trays to a quiet place outside the walls, set out seats, bowed, and paid the full rites of filial remembrance.

sentences.zh: 時燉煌汜潛家善釀酒，每節送一壺與叟。

translations.literal: At the time Si Qian of Dunhuang's household was skilled at brewing; each festival he sent Sou a flask of wine.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Si Qian's household in Dunhuang brewed well; every festival he sent Sou a flask of wine.

sentences.zh: 著作佐郎博陵許赤武、河東裴定宗等謂潛曰：「再三之惠，以為過厚，子惠於叟，何其恆也？

translations.literal: Chief Clerk for Compilation Xu Chiwu of Boling, Pei Dingzong of Hedong, and others said to Qian: 'Such repeated kindness seems excessive; how constant is your generosity toward Sou?'
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk for Compilation Xu Chiwu of Boling, Pei Dingzong of Hedong, and others said to Qian, "Such repeated kindness seems too much—why are you so constant in your generosity toward Sou?"

sentences.zh: 」潛曰：「我恆給祭者，以其恆於孝思也。

translations.literal: Qian said: 'I constantly supply one who sacrifices because he is constant in filial thought.'
translations.idiomatic: Qian said, "I constantly supply one who makes offerings because he is constant in filial thought."

sentences.zh: 」論者以潛為君子矣。

translations.literal: Commentators judged Qian a gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators took Qian for a gentleman.

sentences.zh: 順陽等數子，稟叟獎示，頗涉文流。

translations.literal: Shunyang and several of the others, benefiting from Sou's encouragement and guidance, entered largely into literary circles.
translations.idiomatic: Shunyang and several others, encouraged and instructed by Sou, entered largely into literary circles.

sentences.zh: 高閭曾造其家，遇叟短褐曳柴，從田歸舍，為閭設濁酒蔬食，皆手自辦。

translations.literal: Gao Lu once visited his home and found Sou in short hemp robe dragging firewood, returning from the fields to his dwelling; for Lu he set out coarse wine and plain food, all prepared with his own hands.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lu once called at his house and found Sou in a short hemp robe dragging firewood back from the fields; for Lu he laid out coarse wine and plain food, all prepared with his own hands.

sentences.zh: 然案其館宇卑陋，園疇褊局，而飯菜精潔，醢醬調美。

translations.literal: Yet though his lodging was low and cramped and his garden small, the rice and dishes were refined, the sauces and relish beautifully seasoned.
translations.idiomatic: Yet though his dwelling was low and cramped and his garden plot narrow, the rice and dishes were refined and the sauces and relish beautifully seasoned.

sentences.zh: 見其二妾，並年衰跛眇，衣布穿弊。

translations.literal: He saw Sou's two concubines, both aged, lame, and blind in one eye, in patched hemp clothes.
translations.idiomatic: He saw Sou's two concubines, both aged, lame, and blind in one eye, in patched hemp garments.

sentences.zh: 閭見其貧，以衣物直十餘匹贈之，亦無辭免。

translations.literal: Lu, seeing his poverty, gave him clothing worth more than ten bolts of cloth; Sou did not refuse.
translations.idiomatic: Lu, seeing his poverty, gave him clothing worth more than ten bolts of cloth, and Sou did not decline.

sentences.zh: 閭作《宣命賦》，叟為之序。

translations.literal: Lu composed the 'Ode on the Imperial Edict,' and Sou wrote its preface.
translations.idiomatic: Lu wrote the "Ode on the Imperial Edict," and Sou composed its preface.

sentences.zh: 密雲左右皆祗仰其德，歲時奉以布麻穀麥，叟隨分散之，家無餘財。

translations.literal: Those around Miyun all revered his virtue; each year they brought him cloth, hemp, grain, and wheat, and Sou distributed it as he went, leaving nothing at home.
translations.idiomatic: Those around Miyun all revered his virtue; each year they brought him cloth, hemp, grain, and wheat, and Sou gave it away as he went, leaving nothing at home.

sentences.zh: 卒，無子。

translations.literal: He died without sons.
translations.idiomatic: He died without sons.

sentences.zh: 無家人營主凶事，胡始昌迎殯之於家，葬於墓次。

translations.literal: No household members arranged the funeral; Hu Shichang received the coffin into his home and buried him beside the family tomb.
translations.idiomatic: With no family to manage the funeral, Hu Shichang received the coffin into his home and buried him beside the clan tomb.

sentences.zh: 即令弟繼之，襲其爵始復男、武威將軍。

translations.literal: He then had his younger brother Jizhi succeed to the barony of Shifu and the post of General Who Pacifies Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He then had his younger brother Jizhi inherit the barony of Shifu and the post of General Who Pacifies Wei.

sentences.zh: 叟與始昌雖宗室，性氣殊詭，不相附，其存，往來乃簡；

translations.literal: Though Sou and Shichang were of the same clan, their temperaments were utterly different and they did not attach to one another; while Sou lived, their contact was sparse.
translations.idiomatic: Though Sou and Shichang were clan kin, their temperaments were utterly unlike and they did not draw close; while Sou lived their contact was sparse.

sentences.zh: 及亡，而收恤至厚。

translations.literal: After his death, however, Shichang's care in receiving and mourning him was most generous.
translations.idiomatic: After his death, however, Shichang's care in receiving and mourning him was exceedingly generous.

sentences.zh: 議者以為非必敦哀疏宗，或緣求利品秩也。

translations.literal: Commentators thought this was not necessarily deep mourning toward a distant kinsman, but perhaps a bid for the benefit of rank and title.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators thought this was not necessarily deep mourning toward a distant kinsman, but perhaps a move to gain rank and title.

sentences.zh: 胡方回，安定臨涇人也。

translations.literal: Hu Fanghui was a native of Linjing in Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Fanghui came from Linjing in Anding commandery.

sentences.zh: 父義周，姚泓黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: His father Yizhou was Yellow Gate Attendant under Yao Hong.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yizhou served as Yellow Gate Attendant under Yao Hong.

sentences.zh: 方回仕赫連屈丐為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Fanghui served Helian Qifu as Secretariat Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Fanghui served Helian Qifu as Secretariat Attendant.

sentences.zh: 涉獵史籍，辭彩可觀，為屈丐《統萬城銘》、《蛇祠碑》諸文，頗行於世。

translations.literal: He ranged widely through historical records; his literary color was pleasing. He wrote for Qifu such pieces as the 'Inscription on Tongwan City' and the 'Stele of the Snake Shrine,' which circulated widely.
translations.idiomatic: He ranged widely through historical records and wrote with pleasing literary color; for Qifu he composed the "Inscription on Tongwan City," the "Stele of the Snake Shrine," and other pieces that circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 太武破赫連昌，方回入魏，未為時知。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taiwu defeated Helian Chang, Fanghui entered Wei but was not yet recognized by the age.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taiwu defeated Helian Chang, Fanghui entered Wei but was not yet known at court.

sentences.zh: 後為北鎮司馬，為鎮修表，有所稱薦，帝覽之嗟美。

translations.literal: Later as Northern Garrison Marshal he drafted a memorial commending the garrison; the emperor read it and sighed in praise.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as Northern Garrison Marshal, he drafted a memorial commending the garrison; the emperor read it and sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 閭知方回，召為中書博士，賜爵臨涇子。

translations.literal: Lu, recognizing Fanghui, summoned him as Erudite of the Secretariat and ennobled him as Viscount of Linjing.
translations.idiomatic: Lu, recognizing Fanghui's talent, summoned him as Erudite of the Secretariat and ennobled him as Viscount of Linjing.

sentences.zh: 遷侍郎，與太子少傅游雅等改定律制。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Attendant and, with Junior Tutor You Ya and others, revised the legal code.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attendant and, with Junior Tutor You Ya and others, revised the laws and statutes.

sentences.zh: 司徒崔浩及當時朝賢，並愛重之。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Cui Hao and the leading men of the court all esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Cui Hao and the leading men of the court all valued him highly.

sentences.zh: 清貧守道，以壽終。

translations.literal: He lived in poverty while holding to the Way, and died at an advanced age.
translations.idiomatic: Poor yet steadfast in the Way, he died at an advanced age.

sentences.zh: 張湛，字子然，一字仲玄，燉煌深泉人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhan, styled Ziran and also styled Zhongxuan, was a native of Shenquan in Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhan, styled Ziran and also Zhongxuan, came from Shenquan in Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 魏執金吾恭九葉孫，為河西著姓。

translations.literal: A ninth-generation descendant of Gong, Chamberlain for the Imperial Insignia of Wei; a leading clan of Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: He was a ninth-generation descendant of Gong, Chamberlain for the Imperial Insignia of Wei—a leading clan of Hexi.

sentences.zh: 祖質，仕涼，位金城太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhi served Liang and held the post of Administrator of Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhi served Liang as Administrator of Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 父顯，有遠量，武昭王據有西夏，引為功曹，甚器異之。

translations.literal: His father Xian had far-reaching judgment; when Prince Zhaowu of Liang seized Western Xia, he brought Xian in as Merit Officer and valued him highly.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xian had far-reaching judgment; when Prince Zhaowu of Liang held Western Xia, he brought Xian in as Merit Officer and valued him greatly.

sentences.zh: 嘗稱曰：「吾之臧子原也。

translations.literal: He once said: 'He is my Zang Ziyuan.'
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "He is my Zang Ziyuan."

sentences.zh: 」位酒泉太守。

translations.literal: He held the post of Administrator of Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Administrator of Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 湛弱冠知名涼土，好學能屬文，沖素有大志。

translations.literal: Zhan was famed in Liangzhou while still in his prime; he loved learning and could compose prose, pure and high-minded with great ambition.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan was famed in Liangzhou while still young; he loved learning and could compose prose, pure and high-minded with great ambition.

sentences.zh: 仕沮渠蒙遜，位兵部尚書。

translations.literal: He served Juqu Mengxun as Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He served Juqu Mengxun as Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 涼州平，拜甯遠將軍，賜爵南蒲男。

translations.literal: When Liangzhou was pacified he was appointed General Who Calms the Distance and ennobled as Baron of Nanpu.
translations.idiomatic: When Liangzhou was pacified he was appointed General Who Calms the Distance and ennobled as Baron of Nanpu.

sentences.zh: 司徒崔浩識而禮之。

translations.literal: Minister Cui Hao recognized and honored him.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Cui Hao recognized his worth and honored him.

sentences.zh: 浩注《易》，敘曰：「氇敦煌張湛、金城宗欽、武威段承根三人皆儒者，並有俊才，見稱西州。

translations.literal: In his commentary on the Changes, Hao wrote in the preface: 'Zhang Zhan of Dunhuang, Zong Qin of Jincheng, and Duan Chenggen of Wuwei—all three Confucian scholars with outstanding talent, famed in the western provinces.'
translations.idiomatic: In his commentary on the Changes, Hao wrote in the preface, "Zhang Zhan of Dunhuang, Zong Qin of Jincheng, and Duan Chenggen of Wuwei—all three Confucian scholars with outstanding talent, famed in the western provinces."

sentences.zh: 每與余論《易》，余以《左氏傳》卦解之，遂相勸為解注，故為之解。

translations.literal: Whenever they discussed the Changes with me, I explained the hexagrams by the Zuo Commentary; they urged one another to produce commentaries, and so I wrote my explanation.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever they discussed the Changes with me, I explained the hexagrams through the Zuo Commentary; they urged one another to write commentaries, and so I produced my explanation.

sentences.zh: 」其見稱如此。

translations.literal: He was praised in this way.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the praise he received.

sentences.zh: 湛至京師，家貧不立，操尚無虧。

translations.literal: When Zhan reached the capital his household was too poor to establish itself, yet his conduct was unblemished.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhan reached the capital his household was too poor to set itself up, yet his integrity was unblemished.

sentences.zh: 浩常給其衣食，薦為中書侍郎；

translations.literal: Hao regularly supplied his food and clothing and recommended him as Secretariat Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Hao regularly supplied his food and clothing and recommended him for Secretariat Attendant.

sentences.zh: 湛知浩必敗，固辭。

translations.literal: Zhan knew Hao was bound to fall and firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan knew Hao was bound to fall and firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 每贈浩詩頌，多箴規之言。

translations.literal: Whenever he sent Hao poems and eulogies they were full of admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he sent Hao poems and eulogies they were full of admonitory counsel.

sentences.zh: 浩亦欽敬其志，每常報答，極推崇之美。

translations.literal: Hao likewise respected his resolve and always replied, lavishing the highest praise.
translations.idiomatic: Hao likewise respected his resolve and always replied with the highest praise.

sentences.zh: 浩誅，湛懼，悉燒之，閉門卻掃，慶吊皆絕，以壽終。

translations.literal: When Hao was executed Zhan feared for himself, burned everything, shut his gate and swept the courtyard clean, cut off all condolence and congratulation, and died at an advanced age.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao was executed Zhan feared for himself, burned everything, shut his gate and swept the courtyard clean, cut off all visits of condolence and congratulation, and died at an advanced age.

sentences.zh: 兄銑，字懷義，閑粹有才幹，仕沮渠蒙遜，位建昌令。

translations.literal: His elder brother Xian, styled Huaiyi, was refined and capable; he served Juqu Mengxun as Magistrate of Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Xian, styled Huaiyi, was refined and capable; he served Juqu Mengxun as Magistrate of Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，母憂，哀毀過人，服制雖除，而蔬糲弗改。

translations.literal: Deeply filial by nature, when his mother died his grief and self-wasting surpassed others; though the mourning period ended he still ate plain vegetables and coarse grain.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply filial by nature, when his mother died his grief and self-wasting surpassed others; though the mourning period ended he still ate plain vegetables and coarse fare.

sentences.zh: 崔浩禮之與湛等。

translations.literal: Cui Hao honored him as he did Zhan and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hao honored him as he did Zhan and the others.

sentences.zh: 卒於征西參軍。

translations.literal: He died while serving as staff officer on the western campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as staff officer on the western campaign.

sentences.zh: 懷義孫通，字彥綽，博通經史，沈冥不預時事。

translations.literal: Huaiyi's grandson Tong, styled Yanchuo, mastered the classics and histories comprehensively and withdrew from worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiyi's grandson Tong, styled Yanchuo, mastered the classics and histories comprehensively and kept aloof from worldly affairs.

sentences.zh: 頓丘李彪欽其學行，與之遊款。

translations.literal: Li Biao of Dunqiu admired his scholarship and conduct and cultivated a close friendship with him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Biao of Dunqiu admired his scholarship and conduct and cultivated a close friendship with him.

sentences.zh: 及彪用事，言于中書令李沖，沖召見，甚器重之。

translations.literal: When Biao came to power he spoke of Tong to Director of the Secretariat Li Chong; Chong summoned him and valued him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: When Biao came to power he spoke of Tong to Director of the Secretariat Li Chong; Chong summoned him and valued him greatly.

sentences.zh: 太和中，征中書博士、中書侍郎，永平中，又征汾州刺史，皆不赴，終於家。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era he was summoned as Erudite and Attendant of the Secretariat; in Yongping he was again summoned as Governor of Fenzhou—all summons he declined, and he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taihe era he was summoned as Erudite and Attendant of the Secretariat; in Yongping he was again summoned as Governor of Fenzhou—all summons he declined, and he died at home.

sentences.zh: 通四子，徹、麟、儉、鳳，皆傳家業，知名於世。

translations.literal: Tong had four sons—Che, Lin, Jian, and Feng—all inherited the family tradition and won fame in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Tong had four sons—Che, Lin, Jian, and Feng—all inherited the family tradition and won fame in the world.

sentences.zh: 徹子方明，位侍中、衛尉卿，封西平縣公。

translations.literal: Che's son Fangming held the posts of Palace Attendant and Commandant of the Guard, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Xiping county.
translations.idiomatic: Che's son Fangming held the posts of Palace Attendant and Commandant of the Guard and was enfeoffed as Duke of Xiping county.

sentences.zh: 子敢之襲，位太中大夫、樂陵郡守。

translations.literal: His son Ganzhi succeeded, holding the post of Grand Master of Palace Counsel and Prefect of Leling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ganzhi succeeded, holding the post of Grand Master of Palace Counsel and Prefect of Leling commandery.

sentences.zh: 麟字嘉應，位廣平太守。

translations.literal: Lin, styled Jiaying, was Administrator of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: Lin, styled Jiaying, was Administrator of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 儉字元慎，位涼州刺史。

translations.literal: Jian, styled Yuanshen, was Governor of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jian, styled Yuanshen, was Governor of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 鳳字孔鸞，位國子博士、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Feng, styled Kongluan, was Erudite of the National University and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Feng, styled Kongluan, was Erudite of the National University and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 著《五經異同評》十卷，為儒者所稱。

translations.literal: He authored ten scrolls of 'Evaluations of Differences and Agreements among the Five Classics,' praised by Confucian scholars.
translations.idiomatic: He authored ten scrolls of "Evaluations of Differences and Agreements among the Five Classics," praised by Confucian scholars.

sentences.zh: 段承根，武威姑臧人，自雲漢太尉熲九世孫也。

translations.literal: Duan Chenggen, a native of Guzang in Wuwei, claimed to be a ninth-generation descendant of Han Grand Commandant Duan Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Chenggen came from Guzang in Wuwei and claimed to be a ninth-generation descendant of Han Grand Commandant Duan Ying.

sentences.zh: 父暉，字長祚，身八尺餘。

translations.literal: His father Hui, styled Changzuo, stood more than eight chi tall.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hui, styled Changzuo, stood more than eight chi in height.

sentences.zh: 師事歐陽湯，湯甚器愛之。

translations.literal: He studied under Ouyang Tang, who valued and loved him dearly.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Ouyang Tang, who valued and loved him dearly.

sentences.zh: 有一童子與暉同志，後二年，童子辭歸，從暉請馬。

translations.literal: There was a young lad who shared Hui's aspirations; two years later the lad took leave to return and asked Hui for a horse.
translations.idiomatic: There was a young lad who shared Hui's aspirations; two years later the lad took leave to return and asked Hui for a horse.

sentences.zh: 暉戲作木馬與童子。

translations.literal: Hui jokingly made a wooden horse for the lad.
translations.idiomatic: Hui jokingly made a wooden horse for the lad.

sentences.zh: 甚悅，謝暉曰：「吾太山府君子，奉敕遊學，今將歸，損子厚贈，無以報德。

translations.literal: Greatly pleased, he thanked Hui: 'I am a gentleman of the Mount Tai prefecture; by imperial command I have been studying abroad and now return. You have burdened yourself with so generous a gift, and I have no way to repay your kindness.'
translations.idiomatic: Greatly pleased, he thanked Hui, saying, "I am a gentleman of the Mount Tai prefecture; by imperial command I have been studying abroad and now return. You have burdened yourself with so generous a gift, and I have no way to repay your kindness."

sentences.zh: 子後至常伯封侯，非報也，且以為好。

translations.literal: 'Your son will later reach the rank of Chamberlain and be enfeoffed as marquis—not as repayment, but simply as a token of friendship.'
translations.idiomatic: "Your son will later reach the rank of Chamberlain and be enfeoffed as marquis—not as repayment, but simply as a token of friendship."

sentences.zh: 」言終，乘馬騰虛而去。

translations.literal: When he finished speaking he mounted the horse and soared away through the air.
translations.idiomatic: When he finished speaking he mounted the horse and soared away through the air.

sentences.zh: 暉乃自知必將貴。

translations.literal: Hui then knew he himself would surely rise to eminence.
translations.idiomatic: Hui then knew he himself would surely rise to eminence.

sentences.zh: 仕乞伏熾盤為輔國大將軍、涼州刺史、御史大夫、西海侯。

translations.literal: He served Qifu Chipan as Grand General Who Assists the State, Governor of Liangzhou, Grand Censor, and Marquis of Xihai.
translations.idiomatic: He served Qifu Chipan as Grand General Who Assists the State, Governor of Liangzhou, Grand Censor, and Marquis of Xihai.

sentences.zh: 熾盤子慕末襲位，政亂，暉父子奔吐谷渾。

translations.literal: When Chipan's son Mumo succeeded, amid chaotic government Hui and his son fled to Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: When Chipan's son Mumo succeeded, amid chaotic government Hui and his son fled to Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 慕容璝內附，暉與承根歸魏。

translations.literal: When Murong Gui submitted to Wei, Hui and Chenggen returned to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Gui submitted to Wei, Hui and Chenggen returned to Wei.

sentences.zh: 太武至長安，人告暉欲南奔，雲置金于馬韉中。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taiwu reached Chang'an someone reported that Hui meant to flee south, saying he had placed gold in his saddle bags.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taiwu reached Chang'an, someone reported that Hui meant to flee south, saying he had placed gold in his saddle bags.

sentences.zh: 帝密遣視之，果如告者言，斬之於市，暴屍數日。

translations.literal: The Emperor secretly sent someone to inspect; it was indeed as the informant had said. He was executed in the marketplace, and his corpse was displayed for several days.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor secretly sent men to investigate, and found matters exactly as the accuser had claimed. Hui was beheaded in the marketplace, and his body was left exposed for several days.

sentences.zh: 時有儒生京兆林白奴，欽暉德音，夜竊其屍，置之枯井。

translations.literal: At the time there was a Confucian scholar of Jingzhao named Lin Bairu who admired Hui's virtuous reputation; by night he stole the corpse and placed it in a dry well.
translations.idiomatic: A Confucian scholar from Jingzhao named Lin Bairu, who revered Hui's reputation for virtue, stole the body by night and hid it in a dry well.

sentences.zh: 女為燉煌張氏婦，聞之，乃向長安收葬。

translations.literal: His daughter was a wife of the Zhang clan of Dunhuang; when she heard of this, she went to Chang'an to recover the body for burial.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's daughter, married into the Zhang family of Dunhuang, heard what had happened and traveled to Chang'an to recover his body for burial.

sentences.zh: 承根好學機辯，有文思，而性行疏薄，有始無終。

translations.literal: Chenggen loved learning and was quick-witted and eloquent, with literary talent, but his character and conduct were loose and shallow—he had beginnings but no endings.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggen loved learning, was quick-witted and eloquent, and possessed real literary gifts, yet his character was fickle and shallow: he always started well and never finished.

sentences.zh: 司徒崔浩見而奇之，與同郡陰仲達俱被浩引，以為俱涼土文華，才堪注述。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Cui Hao saw him and found him extraordinary; he and Yin Zhongda of the same commandery were both brought in by Hao, who considered them both literary ornaments of Liang province, their talents fit for annotation and composition.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Cui Hao took notice of him and was struck by his gifts. He and Yin Zhongda of the same commandery were both brought forward by Hao, who regarded them as the finest literary minds of Liang province and judged their talents fit for scholarly compilation.

sentences.zh: 言之太武，並請為著作郎，引與同事。

translations.literal: He spoke of them to Emperor Taiwu, requesting that both be appointed Compilers, and brought them in to work together.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended them to Emperor Taiwu, asked that both be appointed Compilers, and brought them in to serve alongside him.

sentences.zh: 世咸重承根文而薄其行。

translations.literal: The world all valued Chenggen's writing but held his conduct in low esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone respected Chenggen's writing and looked down on his conduct.

sentences.zh: 甚為燉煌公李寶所敬待。

translations.literal: He was greatly respected and treated with honor by the Duke of Dunhuang, Li Bao.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Dunhuang, Li Bao, held him in high esteem and treated him with great respect.

sentences.zh: 浩誅，承根與宗欽等俱死。

translations.literal: When Hao was executed, Chenggen died together with Zongqin and others.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Hao was put to death, Chenggen was executed along with Zongqin and the others.

sentences.zh: 宗欽字景若，金城人。

translations.literal: Zongqin, styled Jingruo, was a native of Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zongqin, whose style name was Jingruo, came from Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 少好學，有儒者風。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning and had the bearing of a Confucian scholar.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he loved learning and carried himself like a true Confucian scholar.

sentences.zh: 仕沮渠蒙遜為中書郎、世子洗馬。

translations.literal: He served Juqu Mengxun as Secretariat Gentleman and Groom of the Heir Apparent's Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the service of Juqu Mengxun as Secretariat Gentleman and Groom of the Heir Apparent's Stud.

sentences.zh: 上《東宮侍臣箴》。

translations.literal: He submitted "An Admonition for Palace Attendants of the Eastern Palace."
translations.idiomatic: He submitted his "Admonition for Palace Attendants of the Eastern Palace."

sentences.zh: 太武平涼州，入魏，賜爵臥樹男，拜著作郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taiwu pacified Liang province, he entered Wei, was granted the title Baron of Woshu, and appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Taiwu conquered Liang province, he entered Wei, was ennobled as Baron of Woshu, and appointed Compiler.

sentences.zh: 與高允書，贈詩，允答書並詩，甚相褒美。

translations.literal: He exchanged letters with Gao Yun and presented poems; Yun replied with letters and poems, and they greatly praised each other.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote to Gao Yun and sent him poems; Yun answered with letters and poems of his own, and the two men lavished praise on each other.

sentences.zh: 在河西撰《蒙遜記》十卷，無足可稱。

translations.literal: While in Hexi he compiled ten scrolls of "Records of Mengxun," which had nothing worth noting.
translations.idiomatic: While in Hexi he wrote ten scrolls of Records of Mengxun, a work of no particular distinction.

sentences.zh: 闞駰，字玄陰，燉煌人也。

translations.literal: Kan Yan, styled Xuanyin, was a native of Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Kan Yan, whose style name was Xuanyin, came from Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 祖倞，父玖，並有名於西土，玖位會稽令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jing and father Jiu were both famous in the western lands; Jiu held the post of Magistrate of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jing and his father Jiu were both renowned in the western regions; Jiu served as magistrate of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 駰博通經傳，聰敏過人，三史群言，經目則誦，時人謂之宿讀。

translations.literal: Yan was thoroughly versed in the classics and commentaries and surpassed others in intelligence; the Three Histories and various writings—once he laid eyes on them he could recite them, and people of the time called him one who had read them in a former life.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had mastered the classics and their commentaries and was unusually quick of mind. The Three Histories and every sort of learned text—he needed only to glance at a page to recite it from memory, and men of the day called him a reader from a previous life.

sentences.zh: 注王朗《易傳》，撰《十三州志》。

translations.literal: He annotated Wang Lang's "Commentary on the Changes" and compiled "Geographical Records of the Thirteen Provinces."
translations.idiomatic: He annotated Wang Lang's Commentary on the Changes and compiled Geographical Records of the Thirteen Provinces.

sentences.zh: 沮渠蒙遜甚重之，常侍左右，訪以政事損益。

translations.literal: Juqu Mengxun greatly valued him, keeping him constantly at his side and consulting him on what to add or remove in governance.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Mengxun held him in the highest regard, kept him constantly at his side, and consulted him on what policies should be adopted or abandoned.

sentences.zh: 拜秘書、考課郎中，給文吏三十人，典校經籍，刊定諸子三千餘卷。

translations.literal: He was appointed Secretariat and Evaluation Gentleman, given thirty clerical assistants, put in charge of collating the classics, and revised more than three thousand scrolls of the various masters.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Secretariat and Evaluation Gentleman, given thirty clerical assistants, and charged with overseeing the classics. He collated and revised more than three thousand scrolls of the various masters.

sentences.zh: 牧犍待之彌重，拜大行台，遷尚書。

translations.literal: Mujian treated him with even greater esteem, appointing him to the Grand Commissariat Office and promoting him to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Mujian treated him with even greater honor, appointing him to the Grand Commissariat Office and then promoting him to Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 及姑臧平，樂安王丕鎮涼州，引為從事中郎。

translations.literal: When Guzang was pacified, Prince Le'an Pi was stationed over Liang province and brought him in as Attendant Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: After Guzang fell, Prince Le'an Pi took command of Liang province and brought Yan in as Attendant Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 王薨，遷京師。

translations.literal: When the prince died, he was transferred to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince died, Yan was transferred to the capital.

sentences.zh: 家甚貧，不免饑寒。

translations.literal: His family was very poor and could not escape hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: His household was desperately poor and knew hunger and cold.

sentences.zh: 性能多食，一飯至三升乃飽。

translations.literal: By nature he could eat a great deal; it took three sheng of rice at one meal for him to be full.
translations.idiomatic: He had an enormous appetite by nature and needed three sheng of grain at a single meal before he felt satisfied.

sentences.zh: 卒，無後。

translations.literal: He died without posterity.
translations.idiomatic: He died leaving no heirs.

sentences.zh: 劉延明，燉煌人也。

translations.literal: Liu Yanming was a native of Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yanming came from Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 父寶，字子玉，以儒學稱。

translations.literal: His father Bao, styled Ziyu, was known for Confucian scholarship.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bao, whose style name was Ziyu, was celebrated for Confucian learning.

sentences.zh: 延明年十四，就博士郭瑀。

translations.literal: At fourteen Yanming went to study under Erudite Guo Yu.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen, Yanming went to study under the erudite Guo Yu.

sentences.zh: 瑀弟子五百餘人，通經業者八十餘人。

translations.literal: Yu had more than five hundred disciples, of whom more than eighty had mastered the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yu had more than five hundred disciples, and more than eighty of them had truly mastered the classics.

sentences.zh: 瑀有女始笄，妙選良偶，有心於延明。

translations.literal: Yu had a daughter who had just come of age; he carefully sought a worthy match and had Yanming in mind.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yu had a daughter who had just come of age. He wanted to choose an excellent son-in-law and had Yanming in mind.

sentences.zh: 遂別設一席，謂弟子曰：「吾有一女，欲覓一快女婿，誰坐此席者，吾當婚焉。

translations.literal: So he set out a separate seat and said to his disciples: "I have a daughter and wish to find a fine son-in-law; whoever sits in this seat, I shall give her to him in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: So he set out a separate seat and told his disciples, "I have a daughter and want to find her an outstanding husband. Whoever sits in this seat shall marry her.

sentences.zh: 」延明遂奮衣坐，神志湛然曰：「延明其人也。

translations.literal: " Yanming immediately flung aside his robe and sat down, his spirit serene, saying: "Yanming is the man.
translations.idiomatic: " Yanming at once threw off his outer robe, sat down, and with perfect composure said, "Yanming is your man.

sentences.zh: 」瑀遂以女妻之。

translations.literal: " Yu then gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: " Guo Yu then gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 延明後隱居酒泉，不應州郡命，弟子受業者五百餘人。

translations.literal: Yanming later lived in seclusion at Jiuquan, did not respond to summons from the prefecture or commandery, and had more than five hundred disciples studying under him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanming later withdrew to Jiuquan, ignored summons from the prefecture and commandery, and gathered more than five hundred disciples under his instruction.

sentences.zh: 涼武昭王徵為儒林祭酒、從事中郎。

translations.literal: Prince Wuzhao of Liang summoned him as Libationer of the Confucian Grove and Attendant Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wuzhao of Liang summoned him to serve as Libationer of the Confucian Grove and Attendant Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 昭王好尚文典，書史穿落者，親自補葺。

translations.literal: Prince Zhaowang delighted in classics and histories; when books and records were worn and torn, he personally mended them.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhaowang loved the classics and histories. When books and records were frayed or torn, he repaired them with his own hands.

sentences.zh: 延明時侍側，請代其事。

translations.literal: Yanming was then attending at his side and asked to take over this task.
translations.idiomatic: Yanming was attending him at the time and asked to take over the work.

sentences.zh: 王曰：「躬自執者，欲人重此典籍。

translations.literal: The prince said: "I handle this myself because I wish people to honor these books.
translations.idiomatic: The prince said, "I do this myself because I want others to treat these texts with respect.

sentences.zh: 吾與卿相遇，何異孔明之會玄德。

translations.literal: My meeting with you, sir, is no different from Kongming's meeting with Xuande.
translations.idiomatic: My meeting with you is no different from Kongming's meeting with Xuande.

sentences.zh: 」遷撫夷護軍，雖有政務，手不釋卷。

translations.literal: " He was transferred to Colonel Who Pacifies the Yi; though he had official duties, he never put down his scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: " He was transferred to Colonel Who Pacifies the Yi. Even with official business pressing on him, he never let go of his books.

sentences.zh: 昭王曰：「卿注記篇籍，以燭繼晝，白日且然，夜可休息。

translations.literal: Prince Zhaowang said: "You annotate and record texts, continuing by candlelight after daybreak—since you do so even in daylight, you may rest at night.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhaowang said, "You annotate and compile texts by lamplight long after dawn. If you work like that even in daylight, at least rest at night.

sentences.zh: 」延明曰：「朝聞道，夕死可矣，不知老之將至，孔聖稱焉。

translations.literal: " Yanming said: "If one hears the Way in the morning, one may die in the evening without regret; not knowing that old age is approaching—Confucius praised this.
translations.idiomatic: " Yanming replied, "If one hears the Way in the morning, one may die content that same evening. Not knowing that old age is near—Confucius praised that spirit.

sentences.zh: 延明何人斯，敢不如此。

translations.literal: What kind of man am I, Yanming, that I would dare not do likewise?
translations.idiomatic: What sort of man am I, Yanming, to dare do any less?

sentences.zh: 」延明以三史文繁，著《略記》百三十篇、八十四卷，《燉煌實錄》二十卷，《方言》三卷，《靖恭堂銘》一卷，注《周易》、《韓子》、《人物志》、《黃石公三略》行於世。

translations.literal: " Because the Three Histories were excessively verbose, Yanming wrote one hundred thirty pieces in eighty-four scrolls of "Brief Records," twenty scrolls of "True Records of Dunhuang," three scrolls of "Dialect Words," one scroll of "Inscription for the Hall of Reverent Respect," and annotated the "Book of Changes," "Han Feizi," "Records of Human Character," and "Three Stratagems of Master Yellow Stone," all of which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: " Finding the Three Histories unwieldy, Yanming wrote Brief Records in one hundred thirty sections across eighty-four scrolls, True Records of Dunhuang in twenty scrolls, Dialect Words in three scrolls, and Inscription for the Hall of Reverent Respect in one scroll. He also annotated the Book of Changes, Han Feizi, Records of Human Character, and Three Stratagems of Master Yellow Stone, and all these works circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜平酒泉，拜秘書郎，專管注記。

translations.literal: When Mengxun pacified Jiuquan, Yanming was appointed Secretariat Gentleman, exclusively in charge of annotation and recording.
translations.idiomatic: After Mengxun conquered Jiuquan, Yanming was appointed Secretariat Gentleman and put solely in charge of scholarly annotation and record keeping.

sentences.zh: 築陸沈觀於西苑，躬往禮焉，號玄處先生。

translations.literal: He built the Lushen Pavilion in the western park; Mengxun went in person to pay his respects and styled him Master Xuan Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun built the Lushen Pavilion in the western park, went in person to pay his respects, and honored Yanming as Master Xuan Chu.

sentences.zh: 學徒數百，月致羊酒。

translations.literal: His disciples numbered in the hundreds; each month they sent mutton and wine.
translations.idiomatic: He had several hundred disciples, and every month they brought him mutton and wine.

sentences.zh: 牧犍尊為國師，親自致拜；

translations.literal: Mujian honored him as National Preceptor and bowed to him in person;
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Mujian honored him as National Preceptor and bowed to him in person;

sentences.zh: 命官屬以下，皆北面受業。

translations.literal: he ordered officials and subordinates alike to face north and receive instruction from him.
translations.idiomatic: he ordered all officials and subordinates to face north and receive instruction from him.

sentences.zh: 時同郡索敞、陰興為助教，並以文學見稱，每巾衣而入。

translations.literal: At the time Suo Chang and Yin Xing of the same commandery served as assistant instructors; both were renowned for literary learning and each entered wearing plain scholars' robes.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Suo Chang and Yin Xing of the same commandery served as assistant instructors. Both were known for literary accomplishment and always entered dressed in plain scholars' garb.

sentences.zh: 太武平涼州，士庶東遷，夙聞其名，拜樂平王從事中郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taiwu pacified Liang province and gentry and commoners moved east, having long heard his name he was appointed Attendant Gentleman to Prince Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taiwu conquered Liang province and the gentry and common people were moved east, Yanming—long famous—was appointed Attendant Gentleman to Prince Le'an.

sentences.zh: 太武詔諸年七十已上，聽留本鄉，一子扶養。

translations.literal: Emperor Taiwu decreed that those seventy years and above might remain in their native districts, with one son to support them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu issued an edict allowing men seventy years of age and older to remain in their home districts, with one son permitted to stay and support them.

sentences.zh: 延明時老矣，在姑臧歲餘，思鄉而返，至涼州西四百里{艸韭}穀窟，疾卒。

translations.literal: Yanming was then old; after more than a year at Guzang, homesick, he set out to return; at the {艸韭} Valley Ravine cave four hundred li west of Liang province he fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yanming was by then an old man. After more than a year at Guzang he grew homesick and set out for home, but fell ill and died at the Jiugu Ravine cave, four hundred li west of Liang province.

sentences.zh: 太和十四年，尚書李沖奏：延明河右碩儒，今子孫沈屈，未有祿潤；

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Taihe, Director of the Secretariat Li Chong memorialized: "Yanming was a leading scholar of the lands west of the Yellow River; now his descendants are sunk in obscurity and receive no stipend;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Taihe, Director of the Secretariat Li Chong submitted a memorial: "Liu Yanming was a leading scholar of the lands west of the Yellow River, yet his descendants now languish in obscurity without any stipend.

sentences.zh: 賢者子孫，宜蒙顯異。

translations.literal: the descendants of the worthy ought to receive special distinction."
translations.idiomatic: The descendants of the worthy ought to receive special favor."

sentences.zh: 於是除其一子為郢州雲陽令。

translations.literal: Accordingly one of his sons was appointed Magistrate of Yunyang in Ying province.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly one of his sons was appointed magistrate of Yunyang in Ying province.

sentences.zh: 正光三年，太保崔光奏曰：「故樂平王從事中郎燉煌劉延明，著業涼城，遺文在茲。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengguang, Grand Tutor Cui Guang memorialized: "The late Attendant Gentleman to Prince Le'an, Liu Yanming of Dunhuang, established his reputation in Liang city; his written legacy remains here.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhengguang, Grand Tutor Cui Guang submitted a memorial: "The late Attendant Gentleman to Prince Le'an, Liu Yanming of Dunhuang, built his reputation in Liang city, and his writings survive here.

sentences.zh: 如或愆釁，當蒙數世之宥。

translations.literal: If there was any fault, he ought to have received pardon for several generations.
translations.idiomatic: If he or his house had committed any offense, they should have received pardon for several generations.

sentences.zh: 況乃維祖逮孫，相去未遠，而令久淪皁隸，不獲收異，儒學之士，所為竊歎。

translations.literal: How much more when from forebears to grandchildren the distance is not great, yet they have long been reduced to menial servitude without receiving special exemption—Confucian scholars privately sigh over this.
translations.idiomatic: How much more so when only a few generations separate forebears from grandchildren, yet his descendants have long been reduced to menial service without receiving any special exemption. Confucian scholars cannot help sighing over this in private.

sentences.zh: 乞敕尚書，推檢所屬，甄免碎役，敦化厲俗，於是乎在。

translations.literal: I beg that the Secretariat be commanded to investigate those under its jurisdiction, select and exempt them from petty corvée—the promotion of teaching and the reform of custom depend on this."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that Your Majesty command the Secretariat to investigate the relevant offices, select his descendants, and exempt them from petty corvée. Encouraging learning and reforming custom depend on acts such as this."

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「太保啟陳，深合勸善，其孫等三家，特可聽免。

translations.literal: The edict said: "The Grand Tutor's memorial deeply conforms to encouraging goodness; these three households of his grandchildren may specially be permitted exemption."
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied, "The Grand Tutor's memorial accords perfectly with the encouragement of virtue. The three households of his grandchildren may specially be granted exemption."

sentences.zh: 」河西人以為榮。

translations.literal: People of Hexi regarded this as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: People throughout Hexi took this as an honor.

sentences.zh: 趙柔，字元順，金城人也，少以德行才學，知名河右。

translations.literal: Zhao Rou, styled Yuanshun, was a native of Jincheng; from youth he was known west of the Yellow River for virtue, conduct, talent, and learning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Rou, whose style name was Yuanshun, came from Jincheng. From youth he was renowned west of the Yellow River for virtue, talent, and learning.

sentences.zh: 沮渠牧犍時，為金部郎。

translations.literal: During the time of Juqu Mujian he was Gentleman of the Gold Office.
translations.idiomatic: Under Juqu Mujian he served as Gentleman of the Gold Office.

sentences.zh: 太武平涼州，內徙京師。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taiwu pacified Liang province, he was moved inward to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taiwu conquered Liang province, he was relocated to the capital.

sentences.zh: 曆著作郎、河內太守，甚著信惠。

translations.literal: He successively served as Compiler and Administrator of Henei, and was greatly noted for trustworthiness and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Compiler and administrator of Henei, and became widely known for integrity and kindness.

sentences.zh: 柔嘗在路，得人所遺金珠一貫，價直數百縑，柔呼主還之。

translations.literal: Once on the road Rou found a string of gold pearls someone had lost, worth several hundred bolts of silk; he called out for the owner and returned them.
translations.idiomatic: Once on the road Zhao Rou found a lost string of gold pearls worth several hundred bolts of silk. He called out for the owner and returned them.

sentences.zh: 後有人遺柔鏵數百枚者，柔與子善明鬻之市。

translations.literal: Later someone gave Rou several hundred iron plowshares; Rou and his son Shanming sold them at market.
translations.idiomatic: Later someone gave him several hundred iron plowshares, and Rou and his son Shanming took them to market to sell.

sentences.zh: 有人從柔買，柔索絹二十疋。

translations.literal: When someone came to buy from Rou, Rou asked twenty bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: When a buyer came to Rou, he asked twenty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 有商人知其賤，與柔三十匹。

translations.literal: A merchant knowing they were cheap offered Rou thirty bolts.
translations.idiomatic: A merchant who knew the plowshares were worth less offered him thirty bolts.

sentences.zh: 善明欲取之，柔曰：「與人交易，一言便定，豈可以利動心？

translations.literal: Shanming wished to accept; Rou said: "In trading with others, a single word settles the matter—how can one let profit move one's heart?
translations.idiomatic: Shanming wanted to accept, but Rou said, "In a bargain, one word fixes the price. How can profit sway the heart?

sentences.zh: 」遂與之。

translations.literal: " So he gave them for twenty bolts.
translations.idiomatic: " So he sold them for twenty bolts.

sentences.zh: 晉紳之流，聞而敬服。

translations.literal: Men of the Jin gentry class, hearing of this, revered and admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Men of the old Jin gentry, hearing of this, admired and respected him.

sentences.zh: 隴西王源賀采佛經幽旨作《祗洹精舍圖偈》六卷，柔為之注解，為當時俊僧所欽味。

translations.literal: Wang Yuanhe of Longxi distilled the subtle meaning of Buddhist sutras and wrote six scrolls of "Verses on the Diagram of the Jetavana Grove"; Rou annotated it, and eminent monks of the time savored it with admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuanhe of Longxi distilled the hidden meaning of Buddhist sutras and wrote six scrolls of Verses on the Diagram of the Jetavana Grove. Rou annotated the work, and leading monks of the day cherished it.

sentences.zh: 又憑立銘贊，頗行於世。

translations.literal: He also composed inscriptions and eulogies on commission, which circulated widely in his day.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote commissioned inscriptions and eulogies, which circulated widely in his time.

sentences.zh: 子默，字沖明，武威太守。

translations.literal: His son Mo, styled Chongming, was Administrator of Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mo, whose style name was Chongming, served as administrator of Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 索敞，字巨振，燉煌人也。

translations.literal: Suo Chang, styled Juzhen, was a native of Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Chang, whose style name was Juzhen, came from Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 為劉延明助教，專心經籍，盡能傳延明業。

translations.literal: He served as assistant instructor to Liu Yanming, devoted himself to the classics, and was fully able to transmit Yanming's teaching.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Liu Yanming's assistant instructor, devoted himself to the classics, and mastered Yanming's entire teaching.

sentences.zh: 涼州平，入魏，以儒學為中書博士。

translations.literal: When Liang province was pacified he entered Wei and, on account of his Confucian learning, became Erudite of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After Liang province was pacified he entered Wei and, on the strength of his Confucian learning, was appointed Erudite of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 京師貴遊之子，皆敬憚威嚴，多所成益，前後顯達位至尚書、牧、守者數十人，皆受業於敞。

translations.literal: Sons of the capital's high families all respected and feared his stern dignity; many benefited greatly—several dozen who later rose to prominence as Secretariat Directors, governors, and administrators had all studied under Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Sons of the capital's great families all respected and feared his stern authority, and many profited from his instruction. Several dozen men who later rose to posts as Secretariat directors, governors, and administrators had all studied under Chang.

sentences.zh: 敞以喪服散在眾篇，遂撰比為《喪服要記》。

translations.literal: Because mourning garb regulations were scattered across many texts, Chang compiled and collated them into "Essential Records on Mourning Garb."
translations.idiomatic: Because rules on mourning garb were scattered through many texts, Chang gathered and arranged them into Essential Records on Mourning Garb.

sentences.zh: 出補扶風太守，在位清貧，卒官。

translations.literal: Sent out to serve as Administrator of Fufeng, he was scrupulously poor in office and died in his post.
translations.idiomatic: Sent out to serve as administrator of Fufeng, he lived in scrupulous poverty in office and died there.

sentences.zh: 時舊同學生等為請諡，詔贈涼州刺史，諡曰獻。

translations.literal: Former fellow students and others petitioned for a posthumous title; an edict granted him posthumously the post of Governor of Liang province, with the posthumous name Xian (Dedicated).
translations.idiomatic: Former fellow students and others petitioned for a posthumous title. An edict posthumously appointed him Governor of Liang province and gave him the posthumous name Dedicated.

sentences.zh: 初，敞之在涼州，與鄉人陰世隆，文才相友。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Chang was in Liang province, he befriended Yin Shilong of his native place for their mutual literary gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Chang was in Liang province, he and Yin Shilong of his home district became friends through their shared literary gifts.

sentences.zh: 世隆至京師，被罪，徙和龍，屈上穀，困不前達，土人徐能抑掠為奴。

translations.literal: Shilong reached the capital, was convicted, exiled to Helong, detained at Shanggu, unable to advance further; a local man named Xu Neng seized and enslaved him.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong reached the capital, was convicted of a crime, and was exiled toward Helong. Held up at Shanggu and unable to go farther, he was seized and enslaved by a local man named Xu Neng.

sentences.zh: 敞因行至上穀，遇見世隆，對泣而別。

translations.literal: Chang happened to be traveling through Shanggu, met Shilong, and they wept face to face before parting.
translations.idiomatic: Chang happened to pass through Shanggu, met Shilong, and the two men wept as they parted.

sentences.zh: 敞為訴理，得免。

translations.literal: Chang pleaded his case and secured his release.
translations.idiomatic: Chang pleaded his case for him and won his release.

sentences.zh: 世隆子孟貴，性至孝。

translations.literal: Shilong's son Menggui was supremely filial by nature.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong's son Menggui was profoundly filial by nature.

sentences.zh: 每向田芸耨，早朝拜父，來亦如之，鄉人欽焉。

translations.literal: Whenever he went to work hoeing in the fields, he paid his respects to his father in the early morning; when he returned he did the same, and his neighbors admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he went out to hoe the fields, he paid his respects to his father at dawn; when he returned he did the same. His neighbors admired him for it.

sentences.zh: 宋繇，字體業，燉煌人也，世仕張氏。

translations.literal: Song Yao, styled Tiye, was a native of Dunhuang; his family had served the Zhang clan for generations.
translations.idiomatic: Song Yao, whose style name was Tiye, came from Dunhuang. His family had served the Zhang clan for generations.

sentences.zh: 父僚，張玄靚武興太守。

translations.literal: His father Liao was Administrator of Wuxing under Zhang Xuanjing.
translations.idiomatic: His father Liao had been administrator of Wuxing under Zhang Xuanjing.

sentences.zh: 繇生而僚為張邕所誅。

translations.literal: Yao was born after Liao had been put to death by Zhang Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Song Yao was born after his father Liao had been executed by Zhang Yong.

sentences.zh: 五歲喪母，事伯母張氏以孝聞。

translations.literal: At five he lost his mother; he served his aunt by marriage, Lady Zhang, and was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his mother at five and served his aunt by marriage, Lady Zhang, with such devotion that he became known for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 八歲而張氏卒，居喪過禮。

translations.literal: At eight Lady Zhang died; he observed mourning beyond what ritual required.
translations.idiomatic: When he was eight Lady Zhang died, and he observed mourning with a rigor that exceeded ritual requirement.

sentences.zh: 喟然謂妹夫張彥曰：「門戶傾覆，歲荷在繇，不銜膽自厲，何以繼承先業。

translations.literal: He sighed and said to his brother-in-law Zhang Yan: "Our house has collapsed; the burden of our clan rests on Yao. If I do not nurture resolve with gall in my mouth, how can I inherit our ancestors' enterprise?
translations.idiomatic: He sighed and said to his brother-in-law Zhang Yan, "Our house has fallen. The burden of the clan rests on me. If I do not swallow gall and steel myself, how can I carry on our ancestors' work?

sentences.zh: 」遂隨彥至酒泉，追師就學，閉室讀書，晝夜不倦，博通經史。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he followed Yan to Jiuquan, sought out teachers to study, shut himself in a room to read, toiling day and night without weariness, until he mastered the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: " So he followed Zhang Yan to Jiuquan, sought out teachers, shut himself in a room to read, and worked day and night without rest until he had mastered the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 呂光時，舉秀才，除郎中。

translations.literal: During the time of Lü Guang he was recommended as a Filial and Incorrupt graduate and appointed Gentleman of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Under Lü Guang he was recommended as a Filial and Incorrupt graduate and appointed Gentleman of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 後奔段業，為中散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Later he fled to Duan Ye and was made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He later fled to Duan Ye and was appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 以業無遠略，西奔涼武昭王。

translations.literal: Because Ye lacked long-range strategy, he fled west to the Martial and Illustrious King of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Ye devoid of far-reaching vision, he fled west to serve the Martial and Illustrious King of Liang.

sentences.zh: 歷位通顯，家無餘財；

translations.literal: He passed through positions of eminence, yet his household had no surplus wealth;
translations.idiomatic: Though he rose through posts of rank and renown, his household held no surplus wealth;

sentences.zh: 雖兵革間，講誦不廢。

translations.literal: even amid warfare, he never abandoned lectures and recitation.
translations.idiomatic: and even in the midst of war he never ceased teaching and reciting the classics.

sentences.zh: 每聞儒士在門，常倒屣出迎，引談經籍。

translations.literal: Whenever he heard that a Confucian scholar was at his gate, he would often rush out with shoes reversed to greet him and lead him in to discuss the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a scholar appeared at his door, he would hurry out with shoes still unlaced to welcome him and draw him into conversation over the classics.

sentences.zh: 尤明斷決，時事亦無滯也。

translations.literal: He was especially clear in judgments and decisions, and current affairs likewise met with no delay.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially sharp in judgment, and affairs of the day never stalled in his hands.

sentences.zh: 沮渠蒙遜平酒泉，於繇室得書數千卷、鹽米數十斛而已。

translations.literal: When Juqu Mengsun pacified Jiuquan, in Yao's house he found only several thousand scrolls of books and several dozen hu of salt and grain, nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: When Juqu Mengsun took Jiuquan, he searched Yao's home and found only a few thousand scrolls of books and a few dozen hu of salt and grain—nothing else.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜歎曰：「孤不喜克李氏，欣得宋繇耳。

translations.literal: Mengsun sighed and said: "I do not rejoice in having conquered the Li clan; I rejoice in having obtained Song Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Mengsun sighed and said, "I take no joy in defeating the Li clan—I rejoice only in gaining Song Yao.

sentences.zh: 」拜尚書吏部郎中，委以銓衡。
