translations.literal: " He was appointed Director of the Personnel Section in the Secretariat and entrusted with the evaluation and selection of officials.
translations.idiomatic: " Yao was then made Director of the Personnel Section in the Secretariat and charged with weighing merit and appointing men to office.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜將死，以子牧犍托之。

translations.literal: When Mengsun was about to die, he entrusted his son Muqian to him.
translations.idiomatic: As Mengsun lay dying, he entrusted his son Muqian to Yao's care.

sentences.zh: 牧犍以為左丞，送其妹興平公主于京師。

translations.literal: Muqian made him Left Assistant and sent his younger sister, the Princess of Xingping, to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Muqian appointed him Left Assistant and sent his sister, the Princess of Xingping, to the capital.

sentences.zh: 太武拜繇河西王右丞相，錫爵清水公。

translations.literal: Emperor Taiwu appointed Yao Right Chancellor to the King of Hexi and bestowed on him the title Duke of Qingshui.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu made Yao Right Chancellor to the King of Hexi and ennobled him as Duke of Qingshui.

sentences.zh: 及平涼州，從牧犍至京師，卒，諡恭公。

translations.literal: When Liang province was pacified, he followed Muqian to the capital, died there, and was posthumously titled Duke Gong.
translations.idiomatic: After Liang province fell, he followed Muqian to the capital, died there, and was posthumously honored as Duke Gong.

sentences.zh: 長子岩襲爵，改為西平侯。

translations.literal: His eldest son Yan inherited the title, which was changed to Marquis of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Yan inherited the title, though it was reduced to Marquis of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 岩子廕，中書議郎、樂安王范從事中郎，卒，贈咸陽太守。

translations.literal: Yan's son Yin served as Consultant of the Secretariat and Aide to Prince of Lean Wang Fan; he died in office and was posthumously made Administrator of Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's son Yin held posts as Consultant of the Secretariat and Aide to Prince Fan of Lean; he died in office and was posthumously named Administrator of Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 廕子季預，性清嚴，居家如官，位勃海太守。

translations.literal: Yin's son Jiyu was by nature austere and strict; he conducted himself at home as though in office, and rose to Administrator of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Yin's son Jiyu was stern and upright by nature, kept his household with the discipline of a yamen, and eventually became Administrator of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 子遊道。

translations.literal: His son was Youdao.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Youdao.

sentences.zh: 游道弱冠隨父在郡，父亡，吏人贈遺無所受，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Youdao, at the age of twenty, accompanied his father in the commandery; after his father's death, he accepted none of the gifts offered by officials and the people, and became known for filial devotion to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Youdao came of age while serving with his father in the commandery. When his father died, he refused every gift from officials and commoners alike and won renown for his devotion to his mother.

sentences.zh: 與叔父別居。

translations.literal: He lived separately from his uncle.
translations.idiomatic: He lived apart from his uncle.

sentences.zh: 叔父為奴誣以構逆，遊道誘令返，雪而殺之。

translations.literal: His uncle had been falsely accused of treason by a slave; Youdao lured the slave back, cleared the accusation, and then killed him.
translations.idiomatic: A slave had falsely accused his uncle of plotting rebellion. Youdao coaxed the slave into returning, cleared his uncle's name, and then killed the slave.

sentences.zh: 魏廣陽王深北伐，請為鎧曹，及為定州刺史，又以為府佐。

translations.literal: When the Wei Prince of Guangyang, Shen, marched north, Youdao was requested as armor-bureau officer; when Shen became Governor of Ding province, Youdao again served on his staff.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei Prince of Guangyang, Shen, launched his northern campaign, Youdao was asked to serve in the armor bureau; later, when Shen became Governor of Ding province, Youdao again joined his staff.

sentences.zh: 廣陽為葛榮所殺，元徽誣其降賊，收錄妻子，游道為訴得釋，與廣陽子迎喪返葬。

translations.literal: Guangyang was killed by Ge Rong; Yuan Hui falsely accused him of surrendering to the rebels and seized his wife and children. Youdao appealed on their behalf and secured their release, then joined Guangyang's son in bringing the coffin back for burial.
translations.idiomatic: After Guangyang was killed by Ge Rong, Yuan Hui falsely charged him with surrendering to the rebels and seized his family. Youdao pleaded their case and won their release, then helped Guangyang's son bring the body home for burial.

sentences.zh: 中尉酈善長嘉其氣節，引為殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: The Censor-in-Chief Li Shanchang admired his integrity and appointed him Palace Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: The Censor-in-Chief Li Shanchang admired his moral courage and made him a Palace Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 台中語曰：「見惡能討，宋遊道。」

translations.literal: Within the censorate they said: "When you see what is evil, you can strike it down—Song Youdao."
translations.idiomatic: A saying in the censorate ran: "See evil and strike it down—that is Song Youdao."

sentences.zh: 孝莊即位，除左兵中軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhuang ascended the throne, Youdao was appointed Commander of the Left Military Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhuang took the throne, Youdao was made Commander of the Left Military Army.

sentences.zh: 為尚書令臨淮王彧譴責，遊道乃執版長揖曰：「下官謝王瞋，不謝王理。

translations.literal: Rebuked by the Secretariat Director and Prince of Linhuai Yuan Yu, Youdao took his tablet and gave a formal bow, saying: "Your humble servant thanks the prince for his anger, not for his reasoning.
translations.idiomatic: Rebuked by the Secretariat Director, Prince of Linhuai Yuan Yu, Youdao took up his tablet and bowed deeply. "Your humble servant," he said, "thanks the prince for his anger—not for his reasoning.

sentences.zh: 」即日詣闕上書曰：「徐州刺史元孚頻有表，雲偽梁廣發士卒，圖彭城，乞增羽林二千。

translations.literal: " That same day he went to the palace gate and submitted a memorial, saying: "The Governor of Xuzhou, Yuan Fu, has repeatedly submitted reports claiming that the false Liang are widely dispatching troops to take Pengcheng, and requesting two thousand additional imperial guards.
translations.idiomatic: " That same day he went to the palace and submitted a memorial: "Yuan Fu, Governor of Xuzhou, has repeatedly reported that the false Liang are massing troops to seize Pengcheng and has asked for two thousand additional imperial guards.

sentences.zh: 以孚宗室重臣，告請應實，所以量奏給武官千人。

translations.literal: Because Fu is a weighty member of the imperial clan, his requests should have been credible; therefore I measured the need and reported granting one thousand military officers.
translations.idiomatic: As a senior member of the imperial clan, Fu's requests seemed credible, and I accordingly reported approval for one thousand military officers.

sentences.zh: 孚今代下，以路阻自防，遂納在防羽林八百人；

translations.literal: Fu is now leaving his post; citing blocked roads as a pretext for self-defense, he has taken in eight hundred of the guards stationed on defense;
translations.idiomatic: Fu is now leaving office. Citing dangerous roads, he has kept eight hundred of the guards assigned to frontier defense;

sentences.zh: 辭雲疆境無事，乞將還家。

translations.literal: yet his plea says the frontier is peaceful and asks to send them home.
translations.idiomatic: yet in his petition he claims the border is quiet and asks permission to send them home.

sentences.zh: 臣忝局司，深知不可。

translations.literal: Your servant, holding this bureau office, knows full well that this cannot be allowed.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant, who holds this bureau post, knows this cannot be permitted.

sentences.zh: 尚書令臨淮王彧，即孚之兄子，遣省事謝遠，三日之中，八度逼迫，雲宜依判許。

translations.literal: The Secretariat Director and Prince of Linhuai Yuan Yu, who is Fu's nephew, sent his attendant Xie Yuan, who within three days pressed eight times, saying the ruling should be approved.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat Director, Prince of Linhuai Yuan Yu—Fu's nephew—sent his attendant Xie Yuan, who within three days pressed eight times for the ruling to be granted.

sentences.zh: 臣不敢附下罔上，孤負聖明。

translations.literal: Your servant dares not collude below to deceive above, betraying the sage clarity of the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant dares not side with inferiors to mislead superiors and fail his sovereign's trust.

sentences.zh: 但孚身在任，乞師相繼；

translations.literal: While Fu was still in office, he kept asking for troops in succession;
translations.idiomatic: While still in office, Fu kept asking for reinforcements one after another;

sentences.zh: 及其代下，便請放還。

translations.literal: once he was leaving office, he asked to release them.
translations.idiomatic: but the moment he was leaving office, he asked to send them home.

sentences.zh: 進退為身，無憂國之意。

translations.literal: His comings and goings served himself alone, with no concern for the state.
translations.idiomatic: He acted only for his own convenience, with no thought for the realm.

sentences.zh: 所請不合，其罪下科。

translations.literal: His request does not accord with protocol; the offense falls under the lesser statutes.
translations.idiomatic: His request violates proper procedure and merits punishment under the lesser statutes.

sentences.zh: 彧乃召臣于尚書都堂云：'卿一小郎，憂國之心，豈厚於我？

translations.literal: Yu then summoned me in the Secretariat hall and said: 'You, a mere junior clerk—can your concern for the state truly outweigh mine?
translations.idiomatic: Yu then summoned me to the Secretariat hall and said, "You—a mere junior clerk—do you care more for the state than I do?

sentences.zh: '醜罵溢口，不顧朝章。

translations.literal: ' Filthy abuse poured from his mouth, heedless of court decorum.
translations.idiomatic: " Vile curses poured from his mouth with no regard for court propriety.

sentences.zh: 右僕射臣世隆、吏部郎中臣薛琡已下百餘人，並皆聞見。

translations.literal: Right Vice Director Shi Long, Director of the Personnel Section Xue Bo, and more than a hundred others all heard and witnessed it.
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Director Shi Long, Personnel Director Xue Bo, and more than a hundred others all heard and saw it.

sentences.zh: 臣實獻直言云：'忠臣奉國，事在其心，亦復何簡貴賤？

translations.literal: I truly offered plain speech, saying: 'Loyal ministers serve the state—the matter lies in the heart; why should we sort by rank and station?
translations.idiomatic: I spoke plainly in reply: "Loyal ministers serve the realm from the heart—what does rank matter?

sentences.zh: 比自北海入洛，王不能致身死難，方清宮以迎篡賊；

translations.literal: Since coming from Beihai into Luoyang, the prince could not offer his body in death against difficulty, yet cleared the palace to welcome usurping rebels;
translations.idiomatic: When you came from Beihai to Luoyang, you would not die for the dynasty, yet you cleared the palace to welcome usurpers;

sentences.zh: 鄭先護立義廣州，王復建旗往討。

translations.literal: when Zheng Xianhu raised righteous banners in Guangzhou, the prince again raised standards to march against him.
translations.idiomatic: when Zheng Xianhu raised the banner of righteousness in Guangzhou, you again took the field against him.

sentences.zh: 趣惡如流，伐善何速？

translations.literal: You rush toward evil like a flowing stream—why do you strike down the good so quickly?
translations.idiomatic: You run toward evil like a current and cut down the good with equal speed—why?

sentences.zh: 」今得冠冕百寮，乃欲為私害政！

translations.literal: " Now crowned above the hundred offices, you would use private ends to harm government!
translations.idiomatic: " Now that you stand at the head of the hundred offices, you would ruin governance for private ends!

sentences.zh: '為臣此言，彧賜怒更甚。

translations.literal: ' For these words of mine, Yu's wrath grew even fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: " At these words Yu's anger only burned hotter.

sentences.zh: 臣既不佞，干犯貴臣，乞解郎中。

translations.literal: Your servant, being no flatterer, having offended a high minister, requests dismissal from my director post.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant is no sycophant. Having offended a great minister, I ask to be relieved of my directorship.

sentences.zh: 」帝召見遊道，嘉勞之。

translations.literal: " The emperor summoned Youdao, praised him, and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor summoned Youdao, praised his courage, and rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 彧亦奏言：「臣忝冠百寮，遂使一郎攘袂高聲，肆言頓挫，乞解尚書令。

translations.literal: Yu also submitted a memorial, saying: "Your servant, bearing the headship among the hundred offices, was made to suffer a junior clerk rolling up his sleeves and shouting aloud, freely speaking and humbling me—I request release from the Secretariat directorship.
translations.idiomatic: Yu submitted a memorial of his own: "Your servant, who leads the hundred offices, was forced to endure a junior clerk rolling up his sleeves and shouting me down in public. I ask to be relieved of the Secretariat directorship.

sentences.zh: 」帝乃下敕，聽解台郎。

translations.literal: " The emperor then issued an edict permitting dismissal of the censorate officer.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor issued an edict granting the censorate officer's resignation.

sentences.zh: 後除司州中從事。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Mid-Level Staff Officer of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Mid-Level Staff Officer of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 時將還鄴，會霖雨，行旅擁於河橋。

translations.literal: At that time they were about to return to Ye; heavy rain fell, and travelers crowded at the river bridge.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court was preparing to return to Ye. Torrential rain fell, and travelers jammed the river bridge.

sentences.zh: 游道於幕下朝夕宴歌。

translations.literal: Youdao feasted and sang morning and evening beneath his tent.
translations.idiomatic: Youdao feasted and sang beneath his tent from morning till night.

sentences.zh: 行者曰：「何時節作此聲也？

translations.literal: Travelers said: "What season is this to make such sounds?
translations.idiomatic: Passersby said, "What season is this for singing and feasting?

sentences.zh: 固大癡！

translations.literal: Truly a great fool!
translations.idiomatic: The man is a perfect fool!

sentences.zh: 」游道應曰：「何時節而不作此聲也？

translations.literal: " Youdao replied: "What season is there when one should not make such sounds?
translations.idiomatic: " Youdao answered, "What season is there when one should not sing?

sentences.zh: 亦大癡！

translations.literal: Also a great fool!
translations.idiomatic: You people are the fools!

sentences.zh: 」後齊神武自太原來朝，見之曰：「此人是遊道邪？

translations.literal: " Later the Divine Martial Emperor of Qi came from Taiyuan to court, saw him, and said: "Is this man Youdao?
translations.idiomatic: " Later Gao Huan, the Divine Martial Emperor, came from Taiyuan to court, saw him, and said, "So this is Youdao?

sentences.zh: 常聞其名，今日始識其面。

translations.literal: I have often heard his name; today I first recognize his face.
translations.idiomatic: I have long heard his name—today I finally see his face.

sentences.zh: 」遷遊道別駕，後日，神武之司州，饗朝士，舉觴屬遊道曰：「飲高歡手中酒者大丈夫，卿之為人，合飲此酒。

translations.literal: " He transferred Youdao to Vice Administrator; some days later, when the Divine Martial Emperor went to Sizhou and feasted the court officers, he raised his cup and entrusted it to Youdao, saying: "He who drinks wine from Gao Huan's hand is a true man—your character suits this cup.
translations.idiomatic: " He promoted Youdao to Vice Administrator. A few days later, when Gao Huan visited Sizhou and feasted the court, he raised his cup to Youdao and said, "A man who drinks from Gao Huan's hand is a true man—and you, sir, are such a man.

sentences.zh: 」及還晉陽，百官辭於紫陌，神武執遊道手曰：「甚知朝貴中有憎忌卿者。

translations.literal: " When returning to Jinyang, the hundred officers took leave at Zimo Lane; the Divine Martial Emperor took Youdao's hand and said: "I know well that among the court nobles there are those who resent and envy you.
translations.idiomatic: " On the return to Jinyang, as the hundred officers took leave at Zimo Lane, Gao Huan took Youdao's hand and said, "I know many at court resent and envy you.

sentences.zh: 但用心，莫懷畏慮，當使卿位與之相似。

translations.literal: Only apply yourself; do not harbor fear—I shall make your rank similar to theirs.
translations.idiomatic: Stand firm and do not be afraid. I will see that your rank matches theirs.

sentences.zh: 」於是啟以游道為中尉。

translations.literal: Thereupon he memorialized to appoint Youdao Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized to make Youdao Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 文襄執請，乃以吏部郎中崔暹為御史中尉，以游道為尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Wencheng strenuously requested otherwise, so Cui Xuan, Director of the Personnel Section, was made Chief Censor, and Youdao was made Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng pressed his own preference, so Cui Xuan of the Personnel Section became Chief Censor while Youdao was made Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 文襄謂暹、遊道曰：「卿一人處南台，一人處北省，當使天下肅然。」

translations.literal: Wencheng told Cui and Youdao: "With one of you at the Southern Platform and one in the Northern Bureau, the realm should be brought to awe.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng told Cui and Youdao, "One of you at the Southern Platform and one in the Northern Bureau should be enough to make the realm tremble.

sentences.zh: 遊道入省，劾太師咸陽王但、太保孫騰、司徒高隆之、司空侯景、錄尚書元弼、尚書令司馬子如官貸金銀，催征酬價。

translations.literal: Youdao entered the secretariat and impeached Grand Preceptor Prince Xianyang Dan, Grand Guardian Sun Teng, Minister of Works Gao Longzhi, Minister of Public Works Hou Jing, Recorder of the Secretariat Yuan Bi, and Secretariat Director Sima Ziru for lending official gold and silver and demanding repayment with interest.
translations.idiomatic: Youdao entered the Secretariat and impeached Grand Preceptor Prince Xianyang Dan, Grand Guardian Sun Teng, Minister of Works Gao Longzhi, Minister of Public Works Hou Jing, Secretariat Recorder Yuan Bi, and Secretariat Director Sima Ziru for lending out official gold and silver and pressing for repayment.

sentences.zh: 雖非指事贓賄，終是不避權豪。

translations.literal: Though not a direct accusation of bribery, it was nevertheless a refusal to shun the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: It was not a direct charge of graft, yet it showed he would not flinch before the mighty.

sentences.zh: 又奏駁尚書違失數百條；

translations.literal: He also memorialized refuting several hundred breaches by the secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted memorials correcting several hundred violations within the Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 省中豪吏王儒之徒，並鞭斥之；

translations.literal: powerful clerks in the bureau such as Wang Ru were all whipped and driven out;
translations.idiomatic: powerful clerks such as Wang Ru were whipped and expelled;

sentences.zh: 始依故事於尚書省立門名，以記出入早晚。

translations.literal: and for the first time, according to precedent, he established a gate register in the secretariat to record comings and goings morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: and for the first time he instituted a gate register at the Secretariat, recording who came and went and at what hour.

sentences.zh: 令僕已下皆側目。

translations.literal: Vice directors and below all looked askance.
translations.idiomatic: Vice directors and everyone below watched him with sidelong eyes.

sentences.zh: 魏安平王坐事亡，章武二王及諸王妃、太妃是其近親者，皆被征責。

translations.literal: When the Wei Prince of Anping was punished and fled, the two princes of Zhangwu and various princesses and grand princesses who were his close kin were all summoned and fined.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei Prince of Anping was condemned and fled, the two princes of Zhangwu and every princess and grand princess closely related to him were summoned and fined.

sentences.zh: 都官郎中畢義雲主其事，有奏而禁，有不奏輒禁者。

translations.literal: Director Bi Yiyun of the Punishments Section handled the matter: some cases were memorialized before detention, some were detained without memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Yiyun, Director of the Punishments Section, handled the cases—some were reported before arrest, others were arrested without report.

sentences.zh: 游道判下廷尉科罪。

translations.literal: Youdao judged and sent them down to the Court of Judicature for sentencing.
translations.idiomatic: Youdao ruled on the cases and referred them to the Court of Judicature for punishment.

sentences.zh: 高隆之不同，於是反誣游道厲色挫辱己，遂枉拷群令史證成之。

translations.literal: Gao Longzhi disagreed; he therefore in turn falsely accused Youdao of harshly rebuking and humiliating him, then tortured the clerks to force testimony.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Longzhi objected and in turn falsely accused Youdao of berating and humiliating him, then tortured the clerks until they gave the testimony he wanted.

sentences.zh: 與左僕射襄城王旭、尚書鄭述祖等上言曰：

translations.literal: Together with Left Vice Director Prince of Xiangcheng Xu, Secretariat Minister Zheng Shuzu, and others, they submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Together with Left Vice Director Prince Xu of Xiangcheng, Secretariat Minister Zheng Shuzu, and others, they submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 飾偽亂真，國法所必去；

translations.literal: Adorning falsehood to confuse truth is what national law must remove;
translations.idiomatic: To dress falsehood as truth is what the law must root out;

sentences.zh: 附下罔上，王政所不容。

translations.literal: colluding below to deceive above is what royal governance cannot tolerate.
translations.idiomatic: to collude with inferiors against superiors is what the throne cannot abide.

sentences.zh: 謹案：尚書左丞宋游道，名望本闕，功績何紀？

translations.literal: We respectfully report: Left Assistant Director Song Youdao—his renown was originally lacking; what achievements are recorded?
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully charge: Left Assistant Director Song Youdao had no reputation to speak of and no deeds worth recording.

sentences.zh: 屬永安之始，朝士亡散，乏人之際，叨竊台郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yong'an, when court officers fled and scattered, in that hour of want he presumptuously seized a censorate post.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yong'an era, when officials fled and the court was desperate for men, he clawed his way into a censorate post.

sentences.zh: 躁行謟言，肆其奸詐，空識名義，不顧典文。

translations.literal: Rash in conduct, flattering in speech, he indulged his treachery; he knew the names of righteousness but paid no heed to statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Restless and sycophantic, he gave free rein to deceit, mouthing righteousness while ignoring the code of law.

sentences.zh: 人鄙其心，眾畏其口。

translations.literal: People despised his heart; the multitude feared his mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Men despised his character; everyone feared his tongue.

sentences.zh: 出州入省，曆忝清資，而長惡不悛，曾無忌諱，毀譽由己，憎惡任情。

translations.literal: Going out to provinces and entering the secretariat, he repeatedly held pure appointments, yet persisted in evil without repentance, without restraint—praise and blame at his whim, likes and dislikes at his pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Whether in the provinces or the Secretariat, he held one prestigious post after another, yet never mended his ways. He praised and condemned as he pleased and indulged every grudge.

sentences.zh: 比因安平王事，遂肆其褊心，因公報隙，與郎中畢義雲遞相糾舉。

translations.literal: Recently, over the Prince of Anping affair, he indulged his narrow heart, using public business to settle private scores, mutually accusing with Director Bi Yiyun.
translations.idiomatic: Most recently, in the Prince of Anping case, he gave vent to petty malice and used official business to settle private scores, trading accusations with Bi Yiyun.

sentences.zh: 又在外兵郎中魏叔道牒云：「局內降人左澤等為京畿送省，令取保放出。

translations.literal: Also, in a memo from External Military Director Wei Shudao: "Surrendered men within the bureau such as Zuo Ze were sent to the secretariat by the capital region with orders to release them on bail.
translations.idiomatic: There is also a memo from External Military Director Wei Shudao stating that surrendered men in the bureau, including Zuo Ze, were sent to the Secretariat by the capital command with orders to release them on bail.

sentences.zh: 」大將軍在省日，判聽。

translations.literal: " On the day the Grand General was at the secretariat, judgment was given to hear it.
translations.idiomatic: " On the day the Grand General was present in the Secretariat, the case was approved.

sentences.zh: 遊道發怒曰：「往日官府成何物官府？

translations.literal: Youdao grew angry and said: "In former days, what sort of office was this office?
translations.idiomatic: Youdao flew into a rage and said, "In the old days, what kind of office was this?

sentences.zh: 將此為例！

translations.literal: You would take this as precedent!
translations.idiomatic: And you would make this your precedent!

sentences.zh: 」又云：「乘前旨格，成何物旨格？

translations.literal: " He also said: "Riding on former imperial directives—what sort of directives were those?
translations.idiomatic: " He also said, "Leaning on old imperial orders—what kind of orders were those?

sentences.zh: 」依事請問，遊道並皆承引。

translations.literal: " When questioned according to the facts, Youdao admitted everything cited.
translations.idiomatic: " When questioned on the facts, Youdao admitted every charge.

sentences.zh: 案律：「對捍詔使，無人臣之禮大不敬者，死。

translations.literal: According to the law: "Resisting an imperial emissary, lacking the rites of a subject—grand disrespect—merits death.
translations.idiomatic: The law states: "To resist an imperial emissary and show no subject's deference is grand disrespect—and death is the penalty.

sentences.zh: 」對捍使者尚得死坐，況遊道吐不臣之言，犯慢上之罪？

translations.literal: " Resisting an emissary already merits death—how much more Youdao's utterance of disloyal words, committing the crime of contempt toward superiors?
translations.idiomatic: " If resisting an emissary alone warrants death, how much more Youdao's disloyal words and contempt for his superiors?

sentences.zh: 口稱夷、齊，心懷盜蹠，欺公賣法，受納苞苴，產隨官厚，財與位積。

translations.literal: His mouth spoke of Bo Yi and Shu Qi, his heart harbored the thief Zhi; he deceived the public, sold the law, accepted bribes—property grew with rank, wealth accumulated with office.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke like Bo Yi and Shu Qi while his heart was that of the robber Zhi. He betrayed the public trust, traded in justice, and took bribes—his estate swelling with every promotion.

sentences.zh: 雖贓汙未露，而奸許如是，舉此一隅，餘詐可驗。

translations.literal: Though corruption was not yet exposed, treachery such as this—citing this one corner, the rest can be verified.
translations.idiomatic: Though his graft has not yet surfaced, deceit of this kind, once glimpsed in one corner, proves the rest.

sentences.zh: 今依禮據律，處遊道死罪。

translations.literal: Now, according to ritual and law, we sentence Youdao to death.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore ask, by ritual and statute, that Song Youdao be sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 是時朝士皆忿為遊道不濟。

translations.literal: At that time the court officers were all indignant that Youdao would not be saved.
translations.idiomatic: At the time every court officer seethed that Youdao might not be saved.

sentences.zh: 而文襄聞其與隆之相抗之言，謂楊遵彥曰：「此真是鯁直大剛惡人。

translations.literal: But Wencheng heard his words of resisting Longzhi and told Yang Zunyan: "This man is truly a stubborn, upright, fierce villain.
translations.idiomatic: But when Gao Cheng heard how Youdao had stood up to Longzhi, he told Yang Zunyan, "That man is a stubborn, incorruptible scourge.

sentences.zh: 」遵彥曰：「譬之畜狗，本取其吠，今以數吠殺之，恐將來無復吠狗。

translations.literal: " Zunyan said: "Compare it to keeping a dog—one keeps it for its bark; now if you kill it for barking too often, I fear in future there will be no more barking dogs.
translations.idiomatic: " Zunyan replied, "It is like keeping a dog for its bark. Kill it for barking too much, and soon you will have no dogs left to bark.

sentences.zh: 」詔付廷尉，遊道坐除名。

translations.literal: " An edict handed him to the Court of Judicature; Youdao was sentenced to removal from office.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict sent the case to the Court of Judicature, and Youdao was stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 文襄使元景康謂曰：「卿早逐我向并州他經略，不忍殺卿。

translations.literal: Wencheng sent Yuan Jingkang to tell him: "You should early follow me toward Bingzhou on other campaigns—I could not bear to kill you.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng sent Yuan Jingkang to tell him, "Come with me to Bingzhou while there is still time. I could not bring myself to kill you.

sentences.zh: 」游道從至晉陽，以為大行台吏部，又以為太原公開府諮議。

translations.literal: Youdao followed him to Jinyang and was appointed to the Personnel section of the Grand Commission, and also made Opening-the-Office Consultant to the Prince of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Youdao followed Wen Cheng to Jinyang and was placed in the Grand Commission's personnel office, then made opening-the-office consultant to the Prince of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 及平陽公為中尉，游道以諮議領書侍御史。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Pingyang became Central Censor, Youdao as Consultant concurrently headed Secretariat Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Pingyang took office as Central Censor, Youdao served as his consultant while concurrently heading the Secretariat Attendant Censorate.

sentences.zh: 尋以本官兼司徒左長史。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally appointed Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works while retaining his original post.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon additionally appointed Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works while keeping his existing rank.

sentences.zh: 及文襄疑黃門郎溫子升知元瑾之謀，系諸獄而餓之，食弊襦而死，棄屍路隅，遊道收而葬之。

translations.literal: When Wen Cheng suspected Yellow Gate Attendant Wen Zisheng of knowing Yuan Jin's plot, he imprisoned and starved him; he died eating ragged inner garments, his corpse was cast by the roadside, and Youdao gathered and buried him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen Cheng suspected Yellow Gate Attendant Wen Zisheng of complicity in Yuan Jin's plot, he had him jailed and starved; Zisheng died gnawing ragged inner garments, and his body was left by the road until Youdao recovered and buried it.

sentences.zh: 文襄謂曰：「吾近書與京師諸貴，論及朝士，雲卿僻於朋黨，將為一病。

translations.literal: Wen Cheng said: "I lately wrote the capital nobles about court gentlemen, saying you were aloof from faction—and that would be a fault.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Cheng told him, "I recently wrote the capital nobility about court gentlemen and said you stood apart from faction—that would be a failing.

sentences.zh: 今卿真是重舊節義人，此情不可奪。

translations.literal: Now I know you truly honor old ties and value integrity; this feeling cannot be taken from you.
translations.idiomatic: Now I see you truly honor old ties and hold to integrity; that loyalty cannot be stripped away.

sentences.zh: 子升吾本不殺之，卿葬之何所憚？

translations.literal: I never meant to kill Zisheng—why did you fear to bury him?
translations.idiomatic: I never intended to kill Zisheng—what was there to fear in burying him?

sentences.zh: 天下人代卿怖者，是不知吾心也。

translations.literal: Those in the world who were afraid for you do not know my heart.
translations.idiomatic: Those who feared for you on my account simply did not know my mind.

sentences.zh: 」尋除御史中尉。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 東萊王道習參御史選，限外投狀，道習與遊道有舊，使令史受之。

translations.literal: Prince of Donglai Dao Xi participated in censorial selection; he submitted a petition beyond the deadline; Dao Xi and Youdao were old acquaintances, and he had a clerk accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Donglai Dao Xi took part in censorial selection and submitted a petition after the deadline; because he and Youdao were old friends, he had a clerk accept it.

sentences.zh: 文襄怒，收遊道，辯而判之曰：「遊道稟性獷悍，是非肆己，吹毛洗垢，創疵人物。

translations.literal: Wen Cheng was angry, seized Youdao, argued the case and judged: "Youdao's nature is fierce and overbearing; he decides right and wrong by himself, picks at hairs to wash away stains, and finds fault with people.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Cheng was enraged, seized Youdao, and after hearing the case ruled: "Youdao is by nature fierce and overbearing; he decides right and wrong on his own, hunts for flaws in trifles, and invents faults in others.

sentences.zh: 往與郎中蘭景雲忿競，列事十條，及加推窮，便是虛妄。

translations.literal: Formerly he contended angrily with Bureau Director Lan Jingyun, listing ten charges; when these were pursued to the end, they proved false.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier he had quarreled with Bureau Director Lan Jingyun and laid ten charges against him; when the matter was fully investigated, every one proved false.

sentences.zh: 方共道習，陵侮朝典。

translations.literal: Just now with Dao Xi he flouted and insulted court statute.
translations.idiomatic: Only now, in the affair with Dao Xi, he has trampled on and insulted court law.

sentences.zh: 法官而犯，特是難原，宜付省科。

translations.literal: A law officer yet committing offense—especially hard to forgive; he should be handed over to the provincial sentencing bureau.
translations.idiomatic: For a judge himself to break the law is especially hard to pardon; he should be remanded to the provincial sentencing office.

sentences.zh: 」游道被禁，獄吏欲為脫枷，遊道不肯曰：「此令公命所著，不可輙脫。

translations.literal: " Youdao was imprisoned; the prison officer wished to remove his cangue; Youdao refused: "This was ordered by the Chancellor; it must not be removed lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Youdao was imprisoned; the jailer tried to take off his cangue, but Youdao refused: "This was imposed by the Chancellor's order and must not be removed at will.

sentences.zh: 」文襄聞而免之。

translations.literal: " Wen Cheng heard and pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen Cheng heard of it, he released him.

sentences.zh: 遊道抗志不改。

translations.literal: Youdao's resolute will did not change.
translations.idiomatic: Youdao's unyielding spirit remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 天保元年，以遊道兼太府卿，乃於少府覆檢主司盜截，得钜萬計。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao, Youdao was additionally appointed Minister of the Grand Storehouse; he reinspected the chief office of the Lesser Storehouse for embezzlement and found amounts reckoned in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 1, Youdao was additionally made Minister of the Grand Storehouse; he reinspected the chief office of the Lesser Storehouse for theft and uncovered sums in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 奸吏反誣奏之，下獄。

translations.literal: Corrupt clerks in turn falsely memorialized against him and he was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: The corrupt clerks then falsely impeached him, and he was thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 尋得出，不歸家，徑之府理事。

translations.literal: Soon released, he did not return home but went straight to the office to handle affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Released not long after, he did not go home but went directly to the office to conduct business.

sentences.zh: 卒，遺令薄葬，不立碑表，不求贈諡。

translations.literal: At death he left instructions for a simple burial, no stele or tomb tablet, and no request for posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he left orders for a plain burial, no stele or tomb inscription, and no petition for a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 贈瓜州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Governor of Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Governor of Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 武平中，以子士素久典機密，重贈儀同三司，諡曰貞惠。

translations.literal: During Wuping, because his son Shisu had long handled state secrets, he was again posthumously granted Provisionally Equal to the Three Excellencies, posthumous name Zhenhui.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wuping era, because his son Shisu had long managed state secrets, he was again posthumously granted Provisionally Equal to the Three Excellencies with the posthumous name Zhenhui.

sentences.zh: 遊道剛直，疾惡如仇，見人犯罪，皆欲致之極法。

translations.literal: Youdao was upright and stern, hating evil as an enemy; seeing anyone commit crime, he wished to bring them to the extreme penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Youdao was rigidly upright and hated wrongdoing like a personal enemy; whenever he saw a crime, he wanted it punished to the full extent of the law.

sentences.zh: 彈糾見事，又好察陰私，問獄察情，捶撻嚴酷。

translations.literal: In impeachments he seized on whatever he saw, and also loved probing hidden matters; in examining cases he gauged sentiments and beat prisoners with harsh severity.
translations.idiomatic: In impeachments he seized on whatever came to hand, loved probing private affairs, and in interrogations read motives and flogged prisoners with brutal severity.

sentences.zh: 兗州刺史李子貞在州貪暴，遊道案之。

translations.literal: Yanzhou Inspector Li Zizhen was greedy and violent in his province; Youdao investigated him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou Inspector Li Zizhen was rapacious and brutal in his province, and Youdao opened a case against him.

sentences.zh: 文襄以子貞預建義勳，意將含忍。

translations.literal: Wen Cheng, because Zizhen had shared in the merit for founding the righteous cause, intended to be lenient.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Cheng, considering that Zizhen had earned merit in the founding of the righteous cause, meant to show forbearance.

sentences.zh: 游道疑陳元康為其內助，密啟云：「子貞、元康交遊，恐其別有請屬。

translations.literal: Youdao suspected Chen Yuankang was his inside helper and secretly memorialized: "Zizhen and Yuankang are intimate; I fear they have other private requests."
translations.idiomatic: Youdao suspected Chen Yuankang of backing him from within and secretly memorialized: "Zizhen and Yuankang are close; I fear they have other private solicitations."

sentences.zh: 」文襄怒，于尚書都堂集百寮，撲殺子貞。

translations.literal: Wen Cheng was angry, assembled the hundred offices in the main hall of the Masters of Writing, and beat Zizhen to death.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Cheng was furious; he assembled the hundred officials in the main hall of the Masters of Writing and had Zizhen beaten to death on the spot.

sentences.zh: 又兗州人為遊道生立祠堂，像題曰「忠清君」。

translations.literal: Also, men of Yanzhou built Youdao a living shrine; on the image was inscribed "Lord Loyal and Pure."
translations.idiomatic: Men of Yanzhou also built Youdao a living shrine while he was still alive, with an image inscribed "Lord Loyal and Pure."

sentences.zh: 游道別劾吉寧等五人同死，有欣悅色。

translations.literal: When Youdao separately impeached Ji Ning and four others to die together, he had a look of delight.
translations.idiomatic: When Youdao separately impeached Ji Ning and four others to death together, he wore a look of satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 朝士甚鄙之。

translations.literal: Court gentlemen greatly despised him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Court gentlemen held him in deep contempt for it.

sentences.zh: 然重交遊，存然諾之分。

translations.literal: Yet he valued friendship and kept faith in promises.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he set great store by friendship and honored his word.

sentences.zh: 曆官嚴整，而時大納賄，分及親故之艱匱者，其男女孤弱，為嫁娶之，臨喪必哀，躬親營視。

translations.literal: Though strict in successive offices, he at times accepted large bribes but distributed them to relatives and friends in hardship; for orphaned and weak men and women he arranged marriages; at funerals he always mourned and personally oversaw arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: Though stern in every post he held, he sometimes took large bribes and gave them to kin and friends in need; he arranged marriages for orphaned and helpless men and women, and at every funeral mourned deeply and saw to the rites himself.

sentences.zh: 為司州綱紀，與牧昌樂、西河二王乖忤，及二王薨，每事經恤之。

translations.literal: As chief regulator of Sizhou he fell out with the governors, the Princes of Changle and Xihe; when the two princes died, in every matter he personally attended to their households.
translations.idiomatic: As chief regulator of Sizhou he clashed with the provincial governors, the Princes of Changle and Xihe; when both princes died, he personally looked after their households in every need.

sentences.zh: 與頓丘李獎，一面便定死交。

translations.literal: With Li Jiang of Dunqiu, at one meeting he sealed a friendship unto death.
translations.idiomatic: With Li Jiang of Dunqiu he formed, at a single meeting, a sworn friendship unto death.

sentences.zh: 獎曰：「我年位已高，會用弟為佐史，令弟北面於我足矣。

translations.literal: Jiang said: "My years and rank are already high; I will employ you, younger brother, as assistant clerk—having you face north to me is enough.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang said, "My years and rank are already advanced; I mean to employ you, younger brother, as assistant clerk—having you face north to me would be enough.

sentences.zh: 」遊道曰：「不能。

translations.literal: " Youdao said: "I cannot."
translations.idiomatic: Youdao replied, "I cannot."

sentences.zh: 」既而獎為河南尹，辟遊道為中正，便者相屬，以衣帢待之，握手歡謔。

translations.literal: Soon Jiang became Intendant of Henan and recruited Youdao as Chief Rectifier; messengers came in succession; he received him in informal cap and robe, clasping hands in merry banter.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Jiang became Intendant of Henan, recruited Youdao as Chief Rectifier, and sent messengers in steady succession; he received him in informal dress, clasping hands in easy banter.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，獎受其命。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Jiang accepted his commission.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Jiang accepted his appointment.

sentences.zh: 出使徐州，都督元孚與城人趙紹兵殺之。

translations.literal: Sent as envoy to Xuzhou, Area Commander Yuan Fu and a city man, Zhao Shao, killed him with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Dispatched as envoy to Xuzhou, he was killed by Area Commander Yuan Fu and the townsman Zhao Shao at the head of troops.

sentences.zh: 遊道為獎訟冤，得雪。

translations.literal: Youdao sued on Jiang's behalf and cleared the injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Youdao pressed Jiang's case and cleared the wrong done him.

sentences.zh: 又表為請贈，回己考一泛階以益之。

translations.literal: He also memorialized to request posthumous honors, transferring one general rank-step from his own father to augment Jiang's.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized for posthumous honors on Jiang's behalf, transferring one general rank-step from his own father's record to augment Jiang's.

sentences.zh: 又與劉廞結交，托廞弟粹于徐州殺趙紹。

translations.literal: He also befriended Liu Yin and entrusted Liu Yin's younger brother Cui to kill Zhao Shao at Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He also befriended Liu Yin and entrusted Yin's younger brother Cui with killing Zhao Shao at Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 後劉廞伏法於洛陽，粹以徐州叛，官軍討平之，梟粹首於鄴市。

translations.literal: Later Liu Yin was executed at Luoyang; Cui rebelled at Xuzhou; government troops suppressed him and displayed Cui's head in the market at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Later Liu Yin was executed at Luoyang; Cui rebelled at Xuzhou; government troops put down the revolt and displayed Cui's head in the market at Ye.

sentences.zh: 孫騰使客告市司，得五百匹後，聽收。

translations.literal: Sun Teng had a retainer tell the market bureau that after receiving five hundred bolts of silk, they might collect the corpse.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Teng had a client tell the market bureau that once five hundred bolts of silk were paid, they might take the corpse.

sentences.zh: 游道時為司州中從事，令家人作劉粹所視，於州陳訴，依律判許，而奏之。

translations.literal: Youdao was then Central Army Attendant of Sizhou; he had his household act as those who had seen Liu Cui, petitioned at the province, obtained judgment according to law, and memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: Youdao was then Central Army Attendant of Sizhou; he had members of his household pose as witnesses to Liu Cui, petitioned at the provincial level, won a judgment under law, and memorialized the result.

sentences.zh: 敕至，市司猶不許，遊道杖市司，勒使速付。

translations.literal: When the edict arrived the market bureau still refused; Youdao caned the market officials and compelled them to deliver promptly.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict arrived the market bureau still refused; Youdao flogged the market officials and forced them to hand over the body at once.

sentences.zh: 騰聞大怒，遊道立理以抗之。

translations.literal: Sun Teng heard and was furious; Youdao stood on principle to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Teng heard and was enraged; Youdao held to principle and resisted him.

sentences.zh: 既收粹屍，厚加贈遺。

translations.literal: After collecting Cui's corpse, he gave lavish gifts in addition.
translations.idiomatic: Once Cui's body was recovered, he added generous gifts of his own.

sentences.zh: 李獎二子構、訓居貧，遊道後令其求三富人死事判免之，凡得錢百五十萬，盡以入構、訓。

translations.literal: Li Jiang's sons Gou and Xun lived in poverty; later Youdao had them pursue death sentences against three rich men and obtain acquittals, receiving altogether 1.5 million cash, all of which went to Gou and Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiang's sons Gou and Xun lived in poverty; later Youdao had them bring capital cases against three wealthy men and secure acquittals, collecting 1.5 million cash in all, which he gave entirely to Gou and Xun.

sentences.zh: 其使氣党俠如此。

translations.literal: His bravado and chivalric factionalism were like this.
translations.idiomatic: His swaggering chivalry and factional loyalty were of this sort.

sentences.zh: 時人語曰：「遊道獼猴面，陸操科斗形，意識不關見，何謂醜者必無情。」

translations.literal: A saying of the day ran: "Youdao has a monkey's face, Lu Cao a tadpole's shape—awareness has nothing to do with looks; why say the ugly must be unfeeling?"
translations.idiomatic: People said at the time: "Youdao has a monkey's face and Lu Cao a tadpole's form—mind has nothing to do with appearance; why assume the ugly must be heartless?"

sentences.zh: 構嘗因遊道會客，因戲之曰：「賢從在門外，大好人，宜自迎接。

translations.literal: Gou once while Youdao was entertaining guests jested: "Your worthy clansman is at the door—a fine fellow; you should go welcome him yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while Youdao was entertaining guests, Gou jested: "Your worthy clansman is at the door—a splendid fellow; you ought to go welcome him yourself.

sentences.zh: 」為通名，稱族弟游山。

translations.literal: " He announced the name: clansman You Shan.
translations.idiomatic: He announced the name as clansman You Shan.

sentences.zh: 遊道出見之，乃獼猴而衣帽也。

translations.literal: Youdao went out to see—a monkey in cap and robes.
translations.idiomatic: Youdao went out to meet him and found a monkey dressed in cap and robes.

sentences.zh: 將與構絕，構謝之，豁然如舊。

translations.literal: He was about to break with Gou; Gou apologized and all was clear as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was ready to break with Gou, but Gou apologized and they were reconciled as before.

sentences.zh: 遊道死後，構為定州長史，遊道第三子士遜為墨曹、博陵王管記，與典簽共誣奏構。

translations.literal: After Youdao's death, Gou was Chief Administrator of Dingzhou; Youdao's third son Shixun was in the Ink Office and recorder for the Prince of Boling; with the chief clerk he jointly falsely memorialized against Gou.
translations.idiomatic: After Youdao died, Gou served as Chief Administrator of Dingzhou; Youdao's third son Shixun held posts in the Ink Office and as recorder to the Prince of Boling; with the chief clerk he jointly submitted a false impeachment against Gou.

sentences.zh: 構于禁所祭遊道而訴焉。

translations.literal: Gou at the place of confinement sacrificed to Youdao and appealed to him.
translations.idiomatic: Imprisoned, Gou offered sacrifice to Youdao and pleaded his case to him.

sentences.zh: 士遜晝臥如夢者，見遊道怒己曰：「我與構恩義，汝豈不知？

translations.literal: Shixun napping by day as if dreaming saw Youdao angry at him: "I and Gou had bonds of grace and duty—do you not know?
translations.idiomatic: Shixun, napping by day as in a dream, saw Youdao angry with him: "Gou and I shared bonds of grace and duty—do you not know that?

sentences.zh: 何共小人謀陷清直之士！

translations.literal: Why join with petty men to plot against an upright man!
translations.idiomatic: Why join petty men in plotting against an upright man!

sentences.zh: 」士遜驚跪曰：「不敢！

translations.literal: " Shixun woke in fright and kneeling said: "I dare not!
translations.idiomatic: Shixun woke in terror, knelt, and cried, "I dare not!

sentences.zh: 不敢！

translations.literal: I dare not!
translations.idiomatic: I dare not!"

sentences.zh: 」旬日而卒。

translations.literal: " Within ten days he died.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days he was dead.

sentences.zh: 遊道每戒其子士素、士約、士慎等曰：「吾執法太剛，數遭屯蹇，性自如此，子孫不足以師之。

translations.literal: Youdao often admonished his sons Shisu, Shiyue, Shizhen and others: "My law enforcement is too rigid; I have repeatedly met obstruction; my nature is like this—descendants need not take me as a model.
translations.idiomatic: Youdao often warned his sons Shisu, Shiyue, Shizhen, and the rest: "I enforce the law too harshly and have repeatedly met misfortune; that is my nature—my descendants need not take me as their model.

sentences.zh: 諸子奉父言，柔和廉遜。

translations.literal: The sons followed their father's words and were gentle, modest, and yielding.
translations.idiomatic: The sons obeyed their father's counsel and were gentle, modest, and deferential.

sentences.zh: 士素沉密少言，有才識，稍遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: Shisu was deep, guarded, and sparing of speech, with talent and insight; he was gradually promoted to Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Shisu was reserved, guarded, and sparing of words, yet talented and discerning; he rose gradually to Secretariat Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 趙彥深引入內省，參典機密。

translations.literal: Zhao Yanshen brought him into the Inner Secretariat to participate in handling state secrets.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yanshen brought him into the Inner Secretariat to share in managing state secrets.

sentences.zh: 曆中書、黃門侍郎，遷儀同三司、散騎常侍，恆領黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He served successively as Secretariat Gentleman and Yellow Gate Attendant, was promoted to Provisionally Equal to the Three Excellencies and Regular Palace Attendant, and always headed Yellow Gate Attendant concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Secretariat Gentleman and Yellow Gate Attendant, was promoted to Provisionally Equal to the Three Excellencies and Regular Palace Attendant, and always retained the Yellow Gate Attendant post.

sentences.zh: 自處機要，近二十年，周慎溫恭，甚為彥深所重。

translations.literal: Handling crucial affairs for nearly twenty years, he was careful and warm in manner, and Yanshen valued him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: For nearly twenty years he handled crucial affairs with circumspect warmth, and Yanshen held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 初，祖珽知朝政，出彥深為刺史。

translations.literal: Initially Zu Ting controlled court governance and sent Yanshen out as inspector.
translations.idiomatic: At first Zu Ting dominated court governance and sent Yanshen out to serve as provincial inspector.

sentences.zh: 珽奏以士素為東郡守，中書侍郎李德林白珽留之，由是還除黃門侍郎，共典機密。

translations.literal: Ting memorialized to make Shisu Administrator of Eastern Commandery; Secretariat Attendant Li Delin told Ting to keep him; thereby Shisu was instead appointed Yellow Gate Attendant and jointly handled secrets.
translations.idiomatic: Ting memorialized to appoint Shisu Administrator of Eastern Commandery; Secretariat Attendant Li Delin urged Ting to retain him, and Shisu was instead made Yellow Gate Attendant and continued to manage secrets with Yanshen.

sentences.zh: 士約亦重善士，官尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Shiyue was also a weighty and good man, serving as Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyue was likewise a man of substance and virtue, holding the post of Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 江式，字法字，陳留濟陽人也。

translations.literal: Jiang Shi, styled Fazi, was a native of Jiyang in Chenliu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Shi, whose style name was Fazi, came from Jiyang in Chenliu commandery.

sentences.zh: 六世祖瓊，字孟琚，晉馮翊太守，善蟲篆詁訓。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Qiong, styled Mengju, was Jin Administrator of Fengyi, skilled in seal script and glossarial explanation.
translations.idiomatic: His sixth-generation ancestor Qiong, styled Mengju, had been Jin Administrator of Fengyi and was skilled in seal script and lexicographical glossing.

sentences.zh: 永嘉大亂，瓊棄官投張軌，子孫因居涼士，世傳家業。

translations.literal: In the great disorder of Yongjia, Qiong abandoned office and joined Zhang Gui; his descendants thus settled in Liang territory and transmitted the family art for generations.
translations.idiomatic: In the great upheaval of Yongjia, Qiong left office and entered Zhang Gui's service; his descendants settled in the Liang region and passed down the family craft for generations.

sentences.zh: 祖強，字文威，涼州平，內徙代京。

translations.literal: His grandfather Qiang, styled Wenwei, when Liangzhou was pacified moved inward to the Dai capital.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Qiang, styled Wenwei, moved inward to the Dai capital when Liangzhou was pacified.

sentences.zh: 上書三十餘法，各有體例，又獻經史諸子千餘卷，由是拜中書博士。

translations.literal: He presented more than thirty calligraphic methods, each with its own set pattern, and also offered more than a thousand scrolls of classics, histories, and masters; thereby he was appointed Erudite of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted more than thirty calligraphic models, each with its own formal pattern, and also presented over a thousand scrolls of classics, histories, and masters' works; for this he was appointed Erudite of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈敦煌太守。

translations.literal: At death he was posthumously made Administrator of Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made Administrator of Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 父紹興，高允奏為秘書郎，掌國史二十餘年，以謹厚稱。

translations.literal: His father Shaoxing was recommended by Gao Yun as Secretariat Gentleman and managed national history for more than twenty years, famed for carefulness and steadiness.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shaoxing was recommended by Gao Yun for the post of Secretariat Gentleman and oversaw the national history for more than twenty years, renowned for diligence and steadiness.

sentences.zh: 卒于趙郡太守。

translations.literal: He died while Administrator of Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as Administrator of Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 式少專家學，數年中，常夢兩人時相教授；

translations.literal: Shi from youth specialized in the family learning; for several years he often dreamed of two persons alternately instructing each other;
translations.idiomatic: From youth Shi devoted himself to the family learning; for several years he often dreamed of two men teaching each other in turn;

sentences.zh: 及寤，每有記識。

translations.literal: on waking he always retained what he had memorized.
translations.idiomatic: and on waking always retained what he had learned.

sentences.zh: 初拜司徒長史兼行參軍，檢校御史，尋除符節令。

translations.literal: He was first appointed Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works with concurrent Acting Adjutant and Investigating Censor; soon he was made Keeper of Talismanic Insignia.
translations.idiomatic: He was first appointed Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works with concurrent acting adjutant and investigating censor; soon afterward he was made Keeper of Talismanic Insignia.

sentences.zh: 以書文昭太后尊號諡冊，除奉朝請，仍符節令。

translations.literal: For drafting the honorific title and posthumous edict of Empress Dowager Wen Zhao, he was made Court Gentleman for Attendance while retaining Keeper of Talismanic Insignia.
translations.idiomatic: For drafting the honorific title and posthumous edict of Empress Dowager Wen Zhao, he was made Court Gentleman for Attendance while continuing as Keeper of Talismanic Insignia.

sentences.zh: 篆體尤工，洛京宮殿諸門板題，皆式書也。

translations.literal: He was especially skilled in seal script; the inscribed boards of all palace gates in the Luoyang capital were Shi's writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially accomplished in seal script; the gate plaques of Luoyang's palaces were all in his hand.

sentences.zh: 延昌三年三月，式表曰：

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year of Yanchang, Shi memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Yanchang 3, Shi submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣聞伏羲氏作而八卦形其畫，軒轅氏興而靈龜彰其彩。

translations.literal: "Your subject has heard that when Fuxi arose the Eight Trigrams took form in their lines, and when the Yellow Emperor rose the divine tortoise displayed its markings.
translations.idiomatic: "Your subject has heard that when Fuxi came forth the Eight Trigrams took shape in their lines, and when the Yellow Emperor arose the sacred tortoise revealed its markings.

sentences.zh: 古史倉頡覽二象之爻，觀鳥獸之跡，別創文字，以代結繩，用書契以維事。

translations.literal: The ancient scribe Cangjie surveyed the lines of the two images and observed the tracks of birds and beasts; he separately created writing to replace knotted cords and used written tallies to govern affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient scribe Cangjie contemplated the lines of the two cosmic emblems and observed the tracks of birds and beasts; he then devised writing to replace knotted cords and used written contracts to order affairs.

sentences.zh: 宣之王跡，則百工以敘；

translations.literal: When the kingly trace of King Xuan spread, the hundred crafts were ordered;
translations.idiomatic: When King Xuan's royal way prevailed, the hundred crafts were put in order;

sentences.zh: 載之方冊，則萬品以明。

translations.literal: recorded in bound registers, the myriad things were clarified.
translations.idiomatic: and once set down in bound registers, the myriad things were made clear.

sentences.zh: 迄於三代，厥體頗異，雖依類取制，未能殊倉氏矣。

translations.literal: Down to the Three Dynasties the forms differed considerably; though models were taken by category, they could not be wholly distinct from Cangjie's system.
translations.idiomatic: Down to the Three Dynasties the script forms diverged widely; though each type was modeled by category, none could be wholly separate from Cangjie's invention.

sentences.zh: 故《周禮》：八歲入小學，保氏教國子以六書：一曰指事，二曰象形，三曰形聲，四曰會意，五曰轉注，六曰假借。

translations.literal: Thus the Offices of Zhou: at eight one enters elementary school; the tutor-in-chief teaches the sons of the state the Six Scripts: first, indicatives; second, pictographs; third, phonetic compounds; fourth, associative compounds; fifth, derivative cognates; sixth, phonetic loans.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Offices of Zhou: at eight one enters elementary school, and the tutor-in-chief teaches the sons of the state the Six Scripts—indicatives, pictographs, phonetic compounds, associative compounds, derivative cognates, and phonetic loans.

sentences.zh: 蓋是史頡之遺法。

translations.literal: These are the methods handed down from Scribe Cangjie.
translations.idiomatic: These were the methods handed down from the scribe Cangjie.

sentences.zh: 及宣王太史史籀著《大篆》十五篇，與古文或同或異，時人即謂之籀書。

translations.literal: When King Xuan's Grand Historian Shi Zhou composed the fifteen chapters of Great Seal, they were at points the same as or different from ancient script; men of the time called it Zhou script.
translations.idiomatic: When King Xuan's Grand Historian Shi Zhou composed the fifteen chapters of Great Seal, they partly matched and partly differed from ancient script; contemporaries called this Zhou script.

sentences.zh: 孔子修《六經》，左丘明述《春秋》，皆以古文，厥意可得而言。

translations.literal: Confucius compiled the Six Classics and Zuo Qiuming expounded the Spring and Autumn Annals—all in ancient script; their meaning can thus be spoken.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius edited the Six Classics and Zuo Qiuming composed the Spring and Autumn Annals, all in ancient script; their meaning can therefore still be expressed.

sentences.zh: 其後七國殊軌，文字乖別。

translations.literal: Afterward the Seven States had separate tracks and writing diverged.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the Seven States went their separate ways and writing diverged.

sentences.zh: 暨秦兼天下，丞相李斯乃奏蠲罷不合秦文者。

translations.literal: When Qin united the realm, Chancellor Li Si memorialized to abolish all that did not accord with Qin script.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin united the realm, Chancellor Li Si memorialized to abolish every script that did not conform to Qin writing.

sentences.zh: 斯作《倉頡篇》，車府令趙高作《爰曆篇》，太史令胡母敬作《博學篇》，皆取史籀式，頗有省改，所謂小篆者也。

translations.literal: Li Si composed the Cangjie Primer, Chariot Office Director Zhao Gao the Yuanli Primer, and Grand Astrologer Humu Jing the Boxue Primer—all taking Zhou script as model with considerable abbreviation and revision, what is called small seal script.
translations.idiomatic: Li Si composed the Cangjie Primer, Chariot Office Director Zhao Gao the Yuanli Primer, and Grand Astrologer Humu Jing the Boxue Primer—all drawing on Zhou script with considerable abbreviation and revision; this is what is called small seal script.

sentences.zh: 於是秦燒經書，滌除舊典，官獄繁多，以趣約易，始用隸書，古文由此息矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon Qin burned the classics and swept away old statutes; official prisons multiplied; to pursue brevity and ease they began to use clerical script, and ancient script thus ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Qin burned the classics and purged the old canon; with official documents multiplying, they sought brevity and ease and began to use clerical script, and ancient script thus fell out of use.

sentences.zh: 隸書者，始皇使下杜人程邈附於小篆所作也。

translations.literal: Clerical script was what the First Emperor had Cheng Miao of Xiadu create by adapting small seal script.
translations.idiomatic: Clerical script was invented when the First Emperor ordered Cheng Miao of Xiadu to adapt the small seal script.

sentences.zh: 世人以邈徒隸，即謂之隸書。

translations.literal: Because Miao had been a convict laborer, the world called it clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: Because Miao had served as a convict clerk, people called the new script "clerical writing."

sentences.zh: 故秦有八體：一曰大篆，二曰小篆，三曰符書，四曰蟲書，五曰摹印，六曰署書，七曰殳書，八曰隸書。

translations.literal: Thus Qin had eight scripts: first, great seal; second, small seal; third, talisman script; fourth, tadpole script; fifth, seal-impression script; sixth, signature script; seventh, weapon script; eighth, clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: Qin therefore recognized eight scripts: great seal, small seal, talisman script, tadpole script, seal-impression script, signature script, weapon script, and clerical script.

sentences.zh: 漢興，有尉律學，復教以籀書，又習八體，試之課最，以為尚書史。

translations.literal: When Han arose, there was the prison-law school, which again taught Zhou script and also trained students in the eight scripts; after testing them and ranking their achievement, they were made clerks of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Han there was a prison-law school that again taught Zhou script and the eight scripts; candidates were examined, ranked by merit, and appointed clerks of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 書省字不正，輒舉劾焉。

translations.literal: If the Masters of Writing found characters incorrectly written, they would immediately impeach the offender.
translations.idiomatic: If the Masters of Writing found a character wrongly written, they would at once impeach the offender.

sentences.zh: 又有草書，莫知誰始，其形書雖無厥誼，亦是一時之變通也。

translations.literal: There was also cursive script; no one knows who first devised it. Though its written forms had no fixed meaning, it too was a timely adaptation.
translations.idiomatic: Cursive script also appeared, though no one knows who invented it. Its forms carried no fixed authority, yet it was another expedient of the age.

sentences.zh: 孝宣時，召通《倉頡》讀者，獨張敞從受之。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Xiaoxuan, those who could read the *Cangjie* were summoned; only Zhang Chang came forward to receive instruction.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Xiaoxuan's reign, readers of the *Cangjie* were summoned to court; only Zhang Chang answered the call.

sentences.zh: 涼州刺史杜業、沛人爰禮講學，大夫秦近亦能言之。

translations.literal: Du Ye, Governor of Liang province, and Yuan Li of Pei lectured on the subject, and Grandee Qin Jin could also expound it.
translations.idiomatic: Du Ye, governor of Liang province, and Yuan Li of Pei gave lectures on the text, and Grandee Qin Jin could expound it as well.

sentences.zh: 孝平時，征禮等百餘人說文字于未央宮中，以禮為小學元士。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Xiaoping, Yuan Li and more than a hundred others were summoned to explain characters in Weiyang Palace, and Yuan Li was made Chief Scholar of Elementary Learning.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaoping, Yuan Li and more than a hundred scholars were summoned to Weiyang Palace to expound the script, and Yuan Li was appointed Chief Scholar of Elementary Learning.

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎揚雄采以作《訓纂篇》。

translations.literal: Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Yang Xiong gathered their material to compose the *Xunzuan*.
translations.idiomatic: Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Yang Xiong collected their work and compiled the *Xunzuan*.

sentences.zh: 及亡新居攝，自以運應制作，大司馬甄豐校文字之部，頗改定古文。

translations.literal: When Wang Mang usurped the throne, believing that Heaven's mandate had shifted to him, Grand Marshal Zhen Feng collated the categories of writing and substantially revised and fixed the ancient script.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Mang seized power, convinced that Heaven had transferred the mandate to him, Grand Marshal Zhen Feng reviewed the script categories and extensively revised the ancient forms.

sentences.zh: 時有六書：一曰古文，孔子壁中書也；

translations.literal: At that time there were six scripts: first, ancient script, the texts from Confucius's wall;
translations.idiomatic: At that time six scripts were recognized: first, ancient script—the texts recovered from Confucius's wall;

sentences.zh: 二曰奇字，即古文而異者；

translations.literal: second, odd characters, that is, ancient script with divergent forms;
translations.idiomatic: second, odd characters, meaning ancient forms that differed from the norm;

sentences.zh: 三曰篆書，雲小篆也；

translations.literal: third, seal script, that is, small seal;
translations.idiomatic: third, seal script, namely small seal;

sentences.zh: 四曰佐書，秦隸書也；

translations.literal: fourth, assistant script, the Qin clerical script;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, assistant script, the Qin clerical script;

sentences.zh: 五曰繆篆，所以摹印也；

translations.literal: fifth, twisted seal, used for seal impressions;
translations.idiomatic: fifth, twisted seal, used for carving seals;

sentences.zh: 六曰鳥蟲，所以幡信也。

translations.literal: sixth, bird-and-insect script, used for banners and credentials.
translations.idiomatic: sixth, bird-and-insect script, used for banners and credentials.

sentences.zh: 壁中書者，魯恭王壞孔子宅而得《尚書》、《春秋》、《論語》、《孝經》也。

translations.literal: The wall texts were what Prince Gong of Lu obtained when he demolished Confucius's house: the *Documents*, the *Spring and Autumn*, the *Analects*, and the *Classic of Filial Piety*.
translations.idiomatic: The wall texts were discovered when Prince Gong of Lu tore down Confucius's house and found the *Documents*, the *Spring and Autumn*, the *Analects*, and the *Classic of Filial Piety*.

sentences.zh: 又北平侯張倉獻《春秋左氏傳》，書體與孔氏相類，即前代之古文矣。

translations.literal: Marquis Cang of Beiping also presented the *Zuo Tradition to the Spring and Autumn*; its script resembled that of the Kong family and was the ancient script of earlier ages.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Cang of Beiping also submitted the *Zuo Tradition to the Spring and Autumn*; its script resembled the Kong family's and was the ancient writing of earlier ages.

sentences.zh: 後漢郎中扶風曹喜號曰工篆，小異斯法，而甚精巧，自是後學，皆其法也。

translations.literal: In Later Han, Palace Attendant Cao Xi of Fufeng was styled a master of seal script; he differed slightly from Li Si's method, yet was extremely refined and ingenious, and thereafter all who studied followed his method.
translations.idiomatic: In Later Han, Palace Attendant Cao Xi of Fufeng was famed as a master of seal script. His hand differed slightly from Li Si's method, yet was exquisitely refined, and later students all followed his style.

sentences.zh: 又詔侍中賈逵修理舊文，殊藝異術，王教一端，苟有可以加于國者，靡不悉集。

translations.literal: An edict also ordered Palace Attendant Jia Kui to restore the old texts; rare arts and unusual techniques, every branch of royal teaching—if anything could benefit the state, none was not gathered together.
translations.idiomatic: The court also ordered Palace Attendant Jia Kui to restore the old texts, gathering every rare art and unusual skill, every branch of royal teaching that might serve the state.

sentences.zh: 逵即汝南許慎古學之師也。

translations.literal: Kui was the master of ancient learning to Xu Shen of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Kui was the teacher in ancient learning to Xu Shen of Runan.

sentences.zh: 後慎嗟時人之好奇，歎俗儒之穿鑿，故撰《說文解字》十五篇，首一終亥，各有部屬，可謂類聚群分，雜而不越，文質彬彬，最可得而論也。

translations.literal: Later Shen lamented that people of the time loved novelty and sighed that vulgar Confucians forced meanings; therefore he compiled the fifteen chapters of *Explaining Graphs and Analyzing Characters*, from the first radical to the last, each with its category—truly gathering like with like and sorting into groups, mixed yet not confused, balanced in substance and ornament, and most fit to be discussed.
translations.idiomatic: Later Shen deplored the age's appetite for novelty and the vulgar scholars' habit of forcing meanings onto words, and so compiled the fifteen chapters of the *Explaining Graphs and Analyzing Characters*. From the first radical to the last, each entry had its place; like was grouped with like, distinctions held without confusion, and substance and style stood in fine balance—the work at its best repays close reading.

sentences.zh: 左中郎將陳留蔡邕采李斯、曹喜之法，為古今雜形，詔於太學立石碑，刊載《五經》，題書楷法，多是邕書也。

translations.literal: Left Palace General Cai Yong of Chenliu adopted the methods of Li Si and Cao Xi, made mixed ancient and modern forms, and by edict set up a stone stele at the Imperial Academy on which the *Five Classics* were cut; the inscribed standard script was mostly Yong's writing.
translations.idiomatic: Left Palace General Cai Yong of Chenliu took the methods of Li Si and Cao Xi, blended ancient and modern forms, and by imperial order erected a stone stele at the Imperial Academy bearing the *Five Classics* in the standard script—most of it in Yong's own hand.

sentences.zh: 後開鴻都，書畫奇能，莫不雲集。

translations.literal: Later, when the Hongdu Gate Academy was opened, every extraordinary talent in calligraphy and painting gathered there like clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Hongdu Gate Academy opened, every rare talent in calligraphy and painting flocked there.

sentences.zh: 時諸方獻篆，無出邕者。

translations.literal: At the time the various regions submitted seal-script works, and none surpassed Yong's.
translations.idiomatic: When the regions submitted examples of seal script, none could match Yong's.

sentences.zh: 魏初，博士清河張揖著《埤倉》、《廣雅》、《古今字詁》。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wei, Erudite Zhang Yi of Qinghe wrote the *Etymological Storehouse*, the *Broad Lexicon*, and the *Glosses on Ancient and Modern Characters*.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wei, Erudite Zhang Yi of Qinghe composed the *Etymological Storehouse*, the *Broad Lexicon*, and the *Glosses on Ancient and Modern Characters*.

sentences.zh: 究諸《埤》、《廣》，綴拾遺漏，增長事類，抑亦于文為益者。

translations.literal: Examining the *Storehouse* and the *Lexicon*, patching omissions and adding categories of things, this too was of some benefit to letters.
translations.idiomatic: In compiling the *Storehouse* and the *Lexicon*, he patched omissions and expanded the categories of terms—work that did some service to written learning.

sentences.zh: 然其《字詁》，方之許篇，古今體用，或得或失。

translations.literal: Yet in his *Character Glosses*, compared with Xu's work, the ancient and modern forms and usages were sometimes right and sometimes wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in his *Character Glosses*, measured against Xu's treatise, the ancient and modern forms and usages were sometimes correct and sometimes mistaken.

sentences.zh: 陳留邯鄲淳亦與揖同，博開古藝，特善《倉》、《雅》。

translations.literal: Handan Chun of Chenliu was Zhang Yi's equal, broadly versed in ancient arts and especially skilled in the *Cangjie* and the *Lexicon*.
translations.idiomatic: Handan Chun of Chenliu was Zhang Yi's peer: broadly versed in ancient arts and especially masterful in the *Cangjie* and the *Lexicon*.

sentences.zh: 許氏字指、八體、六書，精究閑理，有名於揖。

translations.literal: In the Xu family's explanations of character purpose, the eight scripts, and the six principles, he thoroughly investigated subtle principles and was more renowned than Zhang Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xu family's explanations of character purpose, the eight scripts, and the six principles, he pursued the subtle logic to the full and outshone Zhang Yi in reputation.

sentences.zh: 以書教諸皇子。

translations.literal: He taught writing to the various princes.
translations.idiomatic: He instructed the princes in writing.

sentences.zh: 又建《三字石經》於漢碑西，其文蔚煥，三體復宣。

translations.literal: He also erected the *Three-Script Stone Classic* west of the Han stele; its text was splendidly luminous, and the three scripts were again displayed.
translations.idiomatic: He also set up the *Three-Script Stone Classic* west of the Han stele; its text shone with brilliance, and the three scripts were displayed once more.

sentences.zh: 校之《說文》，篆、隸大同，而古字少異。

translations.literal: Compared with the *Explaining Graphs*, the seal and clerical forms were largely the same, though the ancient characters differed slightly.
translations.idiomatic: Checked against the *Explaining Graphs*, the seal and clerical forms were largely identical, though a few ancient characters differed.

sentences.zh: 又有京兆韋誕、河東衛覬二家，並號能篆。

translations.literal: There were also two masters styled able in seal script: Wei Dan of Jingzhao and Wei Ji of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Two other masters were famed for seal script: Wei Dan of Jingzhao and Wei Ji of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 當時台觀榜題，寶器之銘，悉是誕書。

translations.literal: At the time the inscriptions on palace towers and the texts on precious vessels were all in Dan's hand.
translations.idiomatic: In those days the inscriptions on palace towers and precious vessels were all written by Dan.

sentences.zh: 咸傳之子孫，世稱其妙。

translations.literal: All were handed down to their descendants, and generation after generation their skill was praised as marvelous.
translations.idiomatic: Their art passed to their descendants, and for generations their skill was hailed as exquisite.

sentences.zh: 晉世義陽王典祠令任城呂忱表上《字林》六卷，尋其況趣，附托許慎《說文》，而按偶章句，隱別古籀奇惑之字，文得正隸，不差篆意也。

translations.literal: In Jin, Lü Chen of Rencheng, Director of Sacrifices under the Prince of Yiyang, memorialized and submitted the six scrolls of the *Forest of Characters*; tracing its intent, it leaned on Xu Shen's *Explaining Graphs*, arranged parallel phrases, and discreetly distinguished ancient Zhou, odd, and misleading characters, so that the text kept correct clerical forms without losing seal intent.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin, Lü Chen of Rencheng, director of sacrifices under the Prince of Yiyang, submitted the six scrolls of the *Forest of Characters*. In spirit it followed Xu Shen's *Explaining Graphs*, arranged entries in parallel phrases, and discreetly sorted out ancient Zhou forms, odd characters, and misleading variants, preserving correct clerical writing without abandoning seal-script meaning.

sentences.zh: 忱弟靜別放故左校令李登《聲類》之法，作《韻集》五卷，使宮、商、角、徵、羽各為一篇，而文字與兄便是魯、衛，音讀楚、夏，時有不同。

translations.literal: Chen's younger brother Jing, separately following the method of the former Colonel Director of Works Li Deng's *Categories of Sounds*, composed the five scrolls of the *Collection of Rhymes*, making gong, shang, jue, zhi, and yu each one chapter; yet in written characters he and his elder brother were like Lu and Wei, and in pronunciation Chu and Xia—at times they differed.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's younger brother Jing, adapting the method of Li Deng's *Categories of Sounds*, compiled the five scrolls of the *Collection of Rhymes*, with gong, shang, jue, zhi, and yu each forming one chapter. In script he and his brother were as close as Lu to Wei, yet in pronunciation they were as far apart as Chu from Xia—sometimes they did not agree.

sentences.zh: 皇魏承百王之季，紹五運之緒。

translations.literal: Great Wei succeeded the last of the hundred kings and continued the thread of the five cycles.
translations.idiomatic: Great Wei succeeded the last of the hundred kings and carried forward the line of the five cycles.

sentences.zh: 世易風移，文字改變，篆形謬錯，隸體失真。

translations.literal: As the age changed and customs shifted, writing altered; seal forms went awry and clerical bodies lost their truth.
translations.idiomatic: As times changed and customs shifted, the script altered too: seal forms grew corrupt and clerical writing lost its integrity.

sentences.zh: 俗學鄙習，復加虛造。

translations.literal: Vulgar learning and base habit further added fictitious invention.
translations.idiomatic: Shallow scholarship and vulgar habit piled invention upon invention.

sentences.zh: 巧談辯士，以意為疑，炫惑于時，難以厘改。

translations.literal: Clever talkers and debaters, taking their own whims as grounds for doubt, dazzled and misled the age, and correction was hard to achieve.
translations.idiomatic: Clever talkers and debaters, treating private fancy as grounds for doubt, dazzled their contemporaries and made correction nearly impossible.

sentences.zh: 乃曰：追來為歸，巧言為辯，小免為< 需免>，神嵒為蠶。

translations.literal: They would say: "follow" was written for "return," "clever speech" for "debate," "small hare" for "need hare," and "divine cliff" for "silkworm."
translations.idiomatic: They would say that *zhui* (follow) stood for *gui* (return), *qiaoyan* (clever speech) for *bian* (debate), *xiaomian* (small hare) for *xumian*, and *shenyan* (divine cliff) for *can* (silkworm).

sentences.zh: 如斯甚眾，皆不合孔氏古書、史籀《大篆》、許氏《說文》、《石經》三字也。

translations.literal: Cases like these were extremely numerous, and none accorded with the Kong family's ancient books, Scribe Zhou's *Great Seal*, Xu Shen's *Explaining Graphs*, or the three-script stone classic.
translations.idiomatic: Such cases were legion, and none accorded with the Kong family's ancient texts, Scribe Zhou's *Great Seal*, Xu Shen's *Explaining Graphs*, or the three-script stone classic.

sentences.zh: 凡所關古，莫不惆悵焉。

translations.literal: Everything touching antiquity filled one with sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Every matter touching the ancient script filled the heart with sorrow.

sentences.zh: 嗟夫！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 文字者六籍之宗，王教之始，前人所以垂今，今人所以識古。

translations.literal: Writing is the ancestor of the Six Classics and the beginning of royal teaching; by it the men of old handed down to the present, and the men of today recognize antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Writing is the root of the Six Classics and the beginning of royal instruction: through it the ancients handed down the past to the present, and the present learns to know antiquity.

sentences.zh: 臣六世祖瓊，家世陳留，往晉之初，與從父兄俱受學于衛覬，古篆之法，《倉》、《雅》、《方言》、《說文》之誼，當時並收善譽。

translations.literal: Your subject's sixth-generation ancestor Qiong, whose family for generations was in Chenliu, in the early Jin studied together with a cousin under Wei Ji in the methods of ancient seal script and in the meanings of the *Cangjie*, the *Lexicon*, the *Dialect Words*, and the *Explaining Graphs*, and at the time all won fine repute.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject's sixth-generation ancestor Qiong came from a Chenliu family. In early Jin he and a cousin studied under Wei Ji in ancient seal script and in the *Cangjie*, the *Lexicon*, the *Dialect Words*, and the *Explaining Graphs*—and at the time both won high praise.

sentences.zh: 而祖遇洛陽之亂，避地河西，數世傳習，斯業所以不墜也。
