translations.literal: But my ancestor met the disorders at Luoyang, fled west of the Yellow River, and for several generations the tradition was transmitted and practiced, so this art did not fall away.
translations.idiomatic: When my ancestor met the chaos at Luoyang, he fled west of the river; for generations the art was handed down and practiced, and so the family craft did not perish.

sentences.zh: 世祖太延中，牧犍內附，臣亡祖文威杖策歸國，奉獻五世傳掌之書，古篆八體之法。

translations.literal: In the Ta Yan era of Emperor Shizu, when Mujian submitted and came over, my deceased ancestor Wenwei, staff in hand, returned to the homeland and presented the books handed down through five generations and the methods of the eight ancient scripts.
translations.idiomatic: In the Ta Yan era of Emperor Shizu, when Mujian submitted to the court, my late ancestor Wenwei returned home with staff in hand and presented the books preserved through five generations along with the methods of the eight ancient scripts.

sentences.zh: 時蒙褒錄，敘列于儒林，官班文省，家號世業。

translations.literal: At the time he received commendation and enrollment, was listed among the forest of scholars, ranked among the clerical offices, and the family was styled a hereditary profession.
translations.idiomatic: He was then commended and enrolled among the forest of scholars, given rank among the script offices, and the family came to be known for a hereditary craft.

sentences.zh: 暨臣闇短，識學庸薄，漸漬家風，有忝無顯。

translations.literal: As for me, I am dim and short in talent; my knowledge and learning are shallow and thin. Soaked in the family wind, I have disgraced it without distinction.
translations.idiomatic: As for myself, I am dim of mind and slight in talent, my learning shallow and thin. Nurtured in the family tradition, I have brought it shame without adding luster.

sentences.zh: 是藉六世之資，奉遵祖考之訓，竊慕古人之軌，企踐儒門之轍。

translations.literal: Therefore, relying on the resources of six generations, following my forefathers' instruction, I secretly admire the tracks of the ancients and hope to tread the path of the Confucian gate.
translations.idiomatic: Yet drawing on the resources of six generations and obeying my forefathers' teaching, I secretly admire the ancients' example and aspire to walk the Confucian path.

sentences.zh: 求撰集古來文字，以許慎《說文》為主，及孔氏《尚書》、《五經音注》、《籀篇》、《爾雅》、《三倉》、《凡將》、《方言》、《通俗文》、祖文宗《埤倉》、《廣雅》、《古今字詁》、《三字石經》、《字林》、《韻集》、諸賦文字有六書之誼者，以類編聯，文無復重，統為一部。

translations.literal: I ask to compile writing from antiquity, taking Xu Shen's *Explaining Graphs* as the main source, together with the Kong family's *Documents*, the *Phonetic Commentaries on the Five Classics*, the *Zhou Pian*, the *Erya*, the *Three Storehouses*, the *Fanjiang*, the *Dialect Words*, the *Popular Explanations of Characters*, the *Zu Wenzong*, the *Etymological Storehouse*, the *Broad Lexicon*, the *Glosses on Ancient and Modern Characters*, the *Three-Script Stone Classic*, the *Forest of Characters*, the *Collection of Rhymes*, and the characters in various rhapsodies that preserve the principles of the six scripts, arranging them by category and linking them together so that no text is duplicated, all unified in one work.
translations.idiomatic: I beg leave to compile the writing of antiquity, taking Xu Shen's *Explaining Graphs* as the foundation and drawing also on the Kong family's *Documents*, the *Phonetic Commentaries on the Five Classics*, the *Zhou Pian*, the *Erya*, the *Three Storehouses*, the *Fanjiang*, the *Dialect Words*, the *Popular Explanations of Characters*, the *Zu Wenzong*, the *Etymological Storehouse*, the *Broad Lexicon*, the *Glosses on Ancient and Modern Characters*, the *Three-Script Stone Classic*, the *Forest of Characters*, the *Collection of Rhymes*, and the characters in rhapsodies that preserve the six principles of writing—arranging all by category, linking like with like, eliminating duplication, and unifying them in one work.

sentences.zh: 其古籀、奇惑、俗隸諸體，咸使班於篆下，各有區別。

translations.literal: Ancient Zhou forms, odd and misleading characters, and vulgar clerical bodies shall all be set out beneath the seal forms, each with its own distinction.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient Zhou forms, odd and misleading characters, and vulgar clerical variants shall all be displayed beneath the seal forms, each clearly distinguished.

sentences.zh: 詁訓假借之誼，僉隨文而解；

translations.literal: The meanings of glosses and borrowed usages shall all be explained according to the text;
translations.idiomatic: Glosses and borrowed usages shall be explained in each case according to the text;

sentences.zh: 音讀楚、夏之聲，並逐字而注。

translations.literal: the pronunciations of Chu and Xia shall both be annotated character by character.
translations.idiomatic: and Chu and Xia pronunciations shall be noted for each character.

sentences.zh: 其所不知者，則闕如也。

translations.literal: Where I do not know, I shall leave blank.
translations.idiomatic: Where I do not know, I shall leave the entry blank.

sentences.zh: 脫蒙遂許，冀省百氏之觀，而同文字之域。

translations.literal: If I am granted permission, I hope to reduce the labors of the hundred schools and unite the realm of writing.
translations.idiomatic: If granted permission, I hope to spare the hundred schools their toil and bring the world of writing into one shared order.

sentences.zh: 典書秘書所須之書，乞垂敕給；

translations.literal: The books needed by the Directorate of Documents and the Imperial Library—I beg that an edict be issued to supply them;
translations.idiomatic: For the books required by the Directorate of Documents and the Imperial Library, I beg that an edict supply them;

sentences.zh: 並學士五人嘗習文字者，助臣披覽；

translations.literal: and five scholars versed in writing to assist me in examining them;
translations.idiomatic: together with five scholars practiced in writing to assist me in reviewing them;

sentences.zh: 書生各五人，專令抄寫。

translations.literal: and five copyists each, assigned solely to transcription.
translations.idiomatic: and five copyists apiece, assigned solely to transcription.

sentences.zh: 侍中、黃門、國子祭酒一月一監，誣議疑隱，庶無紕繆。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant, Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, and Director of the Imperial Academy shall oversee once a month, consulting on doubtful and obscure points, so that there may be no error.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant, Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, and Director of the Imperial Academy shall supervise once a month, deliberating on doubtful and obscure points so that no error may remain.

sentences.zh: 所撰名目，伏聽明旨。

translations.literal: As for the title of the work I propose to compile, I bow and await Your Majesty's clear instruction.
translations.idiomatic: As for the title of the work I propose, I bow and await Your Majesty's decision.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「可如所請，並就太常，冀兼教八書史也。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Let it be as requested, and assign the matter to the Minister of Ceremonies, in the hope that he may also teach the clerks of the eight scripts."
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied: "Let it be as requested, and refer the matter to the Minister of Ceremonies, that he may also instruct the clerks in the eight scripts."

sentences.zh: 其有所須，依請給之。

translations.literal: Whatever is needed shall be supplied as requested.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever is required shall be supplied as requested.

sentences.zh: 名目待書成重聞。

translations.literal: The title shall be reported again when the book is finished.
translations.idiomatic: The title may be reported again once the book is complete.

sentences.zh: 」式於是撰集字書，號曰《古今文字》，凡四十卷，大體依許氏《說文》為本，上篆下隸。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shi compiled the character book, titled *Characters Ancient and Modern*, forty scrolls in all; in general it followed Xu Shen's *Explaining Graphs* as the basis, with seal script above and clerical script below.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Shi compiled the lexicon, titled *Characters Ancient and Modern*, forty scrolls in all. In the main it followed Xu Shen's *Explaining Graphs*, with seal script above and clerical script below.

sentences.zh: 正光中，兼著作郎。

translations.literal: In the Zhengguang era he also served as Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengguang era he also served as Compiler.

sentences.zh: 卒官，贈巴州刺史。

translations.literal: He died in office and was posthumously made Governor of Ba province.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office and was posthumously appointed governor of Ba province.

sentences.zh: 其書竟未能成。

translations.literal: The book in the end was never completed.
translations.idiomatic: The book, in the end, was never finished.

sentences.zh: 式兄子征虜將軍順和，亦工篆書。

translations.literal: Shi's elder brother's son Shunhe, General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, was also skilled in seal script.
translations.idiomatic: Shi's nephew Shunhe, General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, was also accomplished in seal script.

sentences.zh: 先是，太和中，兗州人沈法會能隸書。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Taihe era, Shen Fahui of Yan province was skilled in clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Taihe era, Shen Fahui of Yan province was accomplished in clerical script.

sentences.zh: 宣武之在東宮，敕法會侍書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanwu was in the Eastern Palace, he ordered Fahui to attend upon writing.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu was crown prince, he ordered Fahui to serve as his writing attendant.

sentences.zh: 後以隸跡見知於閭里者甚眾，未有如崔浩之妙。

translations.literal: Later, many in the villages came to know him through his clerical traces, yet none matched the excellence of Cui Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Later many in the countryside knew him by his clerical hand, yet none could rival the mastery of Cui Hao.

sentences.zh: 論曰：游雅才業，亦高允之亞，至於陷族陳奇，斯所以絕世而莫祀。

translations.literal: The commentator says: You Ya's talent and achievement were second only to Gao Yun's; yet in implicating Chen Qi and exterminating his clan, therein lay the reason his line ended and none sacrifices to him.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: In talent and achievement You Ya stood second only to Gao Yun; yet in implicating Chen Qi and destroying his clan, he ensured that his line would die out unmourned.

sentences.zh: 明根雅道儒風，終受非常之遇。

translations.literal: Minggen's elegant Way and Confucian bearing won him, in the end, extraordinary favor.
translations.idiomatic: Minggen's refined conduct and Confucian bearing won him, in the end, exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 乙太和之盛，有乞言之重，抑乃曠世一時。

translations.literal: At the height of the Taihe era, with the weight of petitioning for counsel, this too was a glory unmatched in an age.
translations.idiomatic: At the height of the Taihe era, when remonstrance carried real weight, that too was a distinction rare in any age.

sentences.zh: 肇既聿修，克隆堂構，正清梗概，顛沛不渝；

translations.literal: Zhao both continued what he had received and enlarged the hall his fathers built; upright, pure, and firm in principle, he did not waver even in hardship;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao not only carried forward what he had inherited but enlarged the house his fathers built; upright, pure, and steadfast in principle, he did not bend even in adversity;

sentences.zh: 辭爵主幼之年，抗節臣權之日，顧視群公，其風固已遠矣。

translations.literal: in the years when he declined enfeoffment because the ruler was young, and in the days when he held to integrity though ministers held power, looking back at the host of lords, his bearing was already far removed from theirs.
translations.idiomatic: when he declined a fief while the emperor was still a child, and when he held to his integrity though powerful ministers ruled the court, he stood apart from the great lords around him by a distance already vast.

sentences.zh: 高閭發言有章句，下筆富文詞，故能受遇累朝，見重明主，掛冠謝事，禮備懸輿。

translations.literal: Gao Lu spoke with ordered phrasing and wrote with rich literary expression; therefore he received favor through successive reigns, was valued by enlightened rulers, resigned his cap and withdrew from office, and in retirement received every courtesy due one who suspends the chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lu spoke in measured periods and wrote with rich literary grace; therefore he won favor across successive reigns, earned the esteem of enlightened rulers, resigned his office, and in retirement received every honor due a man of years.

sentences.zh: 美矣！

translations.literal: Beautiful indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Beautiful indeed!

sentences.zh: 趙逸文雅自業，琰加之孝義，可謂世有人焉。

translations.literal: Zhao Yi took refinement and letters as his own profession, and Yan added filial duty and righteousness—truly, their age produced such men.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yi made literary refinement his calling, and Yan added filial piety and righteousness to it—truly, their generation had men worth remembering.

sentences.zh: 胡叟顯晦之間，優遊無悶，亦一代之異人歟！

translations.literal: Hu Sou, between obscurity and prominence, moved at ease without vexation—was he not also a singular man of his age!
translations.idiomatic: Hu Sou, whether in obscurity or in the light, moved at ease and without vexation—is he not also a singular figure of his age?

sentences.zh: 胡方回、張湛、段承根、闞駰、劉延明、趙柔、索敞皆通涉經史，才志不群，價重西州，有聞東國，故流播之中，自拔泥滓。

translations.literal: Hu Fanghui, Zhang Zhan, Duan Chenggen, Kang Yin, Liu Yanming, Zhao Rou, and Sou Chang all ranged broadly through the classics and histories; their talent and resolve were uncommon, their worth was heavy in the western provinces, and their names were heard in the eastern states—therefore amid exile and dispersal they lifted themselves out of the mire.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Fanghui, Zhang Zhan, Duan Chenggen, Kang Yin, Liu Yanming, Zhao Rou, and Sou Chang all ranged widely through the classics and histories; their talent and resolve were uncommon, their worth was prized in the western provinces, and their names reached the eastern courts—so even amid exile and dispersal they pulled themselves free of the mud.

sentences.zh: 人之不可以無能，信也。

translations.literal: That a man cannot be without ability—this is true indeed.
translations.idiomatic: That a man cannot afford to be without ability—this is certainly true.

sentences.zh: 宋繇處屈能申，終致顯達。

translations.literal: Song Yao, though placed in hardship, was able to rise again and in the end attained eminence.
translations.idiomatic: Song Yao, though brought low, was able to rise again and in the end won distinction.

sentences.zh: 游道剛直自立，任使為累。

translations.literal: Youdao was upright and self-reliant, yet his readiness to act on others' behalf became his burden.
translations.idiomatic: Youdao was upright and self-reliant, yet his readiness to act for others became his undoing.

sentences.zh: 江式能世其業，亦足稱云。

translations.literal: Jiang Shi was able to inherit the family profession through the generations—this too is enough to be praised.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Shi was able to carry the family craft from generation to generation—and that alone is praise enough.
